description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As an ICT Design Engineer, you will be part of a global engineering team, comprised of highly effective Architects, Structural, Civil, Mechanical, Electrical, Security, and Control Engineers.

At AWS, we're revolutionizing the design of critical communications pathways, spaces, and cabling within our data centers. We're looking for innovative people who can continue raising the bar for our ICT design, accelerating our time to market, and who have a desire for professional growth and continuous learning.

In this role, you’ll work with engineers and managers company-wide to develop solutions for the physical layer. Your responsibilities will include developing pathway, space, and cabling designs, along with specifications for construction and permitting. Additionally, you’ll engage with industry suppliers and manufacturers to define product requirements and explore emerging technologies.

This role offers a chance to apply and expand your expertise in a innovative and collaborative environment, where your contributions directly impact AWS and its customers. Join us in shaping the future of ICT design at AWS.


Key job responsibilities
- Ensure timely delivery of scalable fiber optic & copper plant designs and specifications.
- Review and approve of ICT pathway, cabling and equipment submittals.
- Identify and respond to risks and high-priority issues rapidly and effectively.
- Support new technology and design activities that improve infrastructure quality, reduce cost and installation time.
- Travel 20+% to review projects and coordinate with onsite personnel and contractors at AWS' Data Centers.
- Have fun and offer creative, out of the box solutions.

About the team
Why AWS?
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.


Basic Qualifications

- 4+ years of industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities experience
- 4+ years of commissioning experience
- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field
- Knowledge of Microsoft Office including Outlook, Word, and Excel
- Experience in industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities
- Experience researching new designs, technologies, and construction methods of data center equipment and facilities
- Experience in commissioning

Preferred Qualifications

- Professional Engineer License
- Experience with building codes and regulations for your region
- Experience carrying design concepts through exploration, development, and into deployment or mass production
- Experience reading, interpreting, and creating construction drawings, specifications, and submittal documents

Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status.

Our inclusive culture empowers Amazonians to deliver the best results for our customers. If you have a disability and need a workplace accommodation or adjustment during the application and hiring process, including support for the interview or onboarding process, please visit https://amazon.jobs/content/en/how-we-hire/accommodations for more information. If the country/region you’re applying in isn’t listed, please contact your Recruiting Partner.



The base salary range for this position is listed below. Your Amazon package will include sign-on payments and restricted stock units (RSUs). Final compensation will be determined based on factors including experience, qualifications, and location. Amazon also offers comprehensive benefits including health insurance (medical, dental, vision, prescription, Basic Life & AD&D insurance and option for Supplemental life plans, EAP, Mental Health Support, Medical Advice Line, Flexible Spending Accounts, Adoption and Surrogacy Reimbursement coverage), 401(k) matching, paid time off, and parental leave. Learn more about our benefits at https://amazon.jobs/en/benefits.

title: Director, Contracts Management- Power Generation
location: Alexandria, Virginia, United States; Austin, Texas, United States; Denver, Colorado, United States; Remote US; Seattle, Washington, United States
salary: $190,000 - $210,000 + Discretionary Bonus
description:
Fleet Data Centers designs, builds and operates mega-scale data center campuses. Fleet provides its customers flexibility and predictability to meet their upside demand forecasts, addressing a key need in the market as traditional leased models are struggling to keep pace with the demand for new Cloud and AI infrastructure. Fleet is led by a team of industry veterans that have already made a lasting imprint on the evolution of global digital infrastructure and are committed and uniquely capable of upleveling data center development scale and operations in the face of rising demand. Fleet is well positioned to bring in-house design, engineering and operational capabilities to collaborate with customers on tailored solutions for campuses of 500MW+. This unique model enables Fleet to provide the world’s largest and most sophisticated customers a seamless extension of their own data center fleets with constant access to design innovation.
Fleet Data Centers is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Contracts Management Director focused on high-value agreements spanning EPC contractors that support islanded power/power generation solutions. Reporting directly to the Vice President of Strategic Partnerships and Development, you will lead the commercial strategy and the prepositioning of EPC contracts with key partners for Behind-the-Meter, Battery Energy Storage Systems, and related islanded power solutions. You will partner with executive leadership, Legal, Engineering, Islanded Power technical teams, development, construction, operations, and finance to negotiate complex agreements, manage commercial risk, and handover to the proper project-execution team.  
How will you make a difference?

Lead commercial negotiations across a diverse portfolio of complex agreements (e.g., EPC to include BTM, BESS, etc.) 
 Negotiate and manage major EPC, engineering, construction, and contractor furnished/contractor installed equipment along with prepositioning related service contracts (e.g., O&M). 
 Develop commercial strategies that balance project delivery, cost, schedule, and contractual risk. 
 Provide executive leadership with commercial recommendations, negotiation strategies, and risk assessments. 
 Work with Systems and Operations teams across Supply Chain to establish contract management systems, governance procedures, and commercial controls. 
 Work with Legal to develop templates, negotiation plans, and commercial standards that improve consistency and efficiency. 
 Partnering closely with legal while maintaining ownership of commercial outcomes. 
 Support multiple high-value complex agreements simultaneously within a dynamic, fast-paced environment. 

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in business administration, Economics, Finance, Construction Management, Legal Studies, Contract Law, Business Law, Construction Management, or Supply Chain.
10+ years in contracts, commercial management. Extensive experience negotiating complex agreements for large-scale capital projects within industries such as Hyperscale Data Centers, Data Center Developers, Power Generation, Energy, Utilities, Industrial Infrastructure, mission critical EPC Projects. 
7+ years of data center experience or mission critical, fast-paced/large-scale infrastructure or data center projects. 
10+ years of commercial/transactional contracts management experience including awarding, drafting, negotiation, execution, and administration. Includes an applied understanding of commercial/contract language, engineering/network practices, risk management, supply chain, or similar contracts-related experience. 
Expertise in sourcing through contracting, cost management and optimization, supplier management, and strategic sourcing in construction, data center, or critical infrastructure sectors
Strong financial analysis and analytical capabilities
Excellent negotiation, communication, and stakeholder management skills
Technologically adept with procurement systems and tools; Microsoft Office proficiency
Proven success negotiating complex EPC, construction, engineering, and supply agreements.
Strong “cradle to grave” understanding of complex agreements and terms that impact contracts administration, change management, claims, and associated downstream commercial risk post contract execution.
Ability to influence executives and other senior stakeholders. 

Preferred Qualifications

Experience negotiating complex agreements for islanded power solutions specifically for BTM and BESS.
 Advanced Degree in business administration, economics, construction management, legal studies, contract/business law, or engineering.
 Start-up environment/mentality with a bias for execution.
 Strong knowledge of supply chain management tools, data analytics, and advanced reporting.
 Knowledge of supply chain sustainability/social responsibility 
 Proficiency in contract lifecycle management (CLM) capabilities (development of business requirements through active use). 
 Detail-oriented with strong organizational, analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making skills. .

Required Traits and Skills

Integrity and Ethical Standards: Build trust, ensure fairness, and foster long-term, transparent relationships with suppliers.
Effective Communication: Clearly convey expectations and requirements to suppliers and negotiation parties, while understanding their needs and concerns. Comfortable delivering written and verbal presentations to internal leadership teams.
Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Understand the emotions, cultural nuances, and motivations of others, while effectively managing one's own emotions during high-pressure negotiations.
Strategic Thinking: Recognize how supplier relationships and negotiations align with broader organizational goals, while aiming for outcomes that benefit both parties.
Critical Thinking Skills: Find innovative solutions and remain flexible in addressing unexpected challenges.
Analytical Ability: Make data-driven decisions, assess cost structures, and identify potential risks, ensuring informed and strategic outcomes.
Influence and Persuasion: Effectively advocate for a position, build consensus, and secure favorable agreements without compromising relationships.
Operational Paranoia: Anticipate risks, identify vulnerabilities, and proactively implement mechanisms to prevent and minimize disruptions and safeguard safety, security, availability, and scale.
Relationship Management: Cultivate trust, collaboration, and long-term partnerships, while building a broad network that provides valuable benchmarking, industry insights, and alternative sourcing options.

Location and Travel

Work location is flexible to Seattle, WA, Denver, CO, Austin, TX, or Alexandria, VA.  100% Remote employees will be considered on an individual basis.
Regular travel, as needed, to Fleet offices as well as to meet with vendors.

Expected Salary Range

$190,000 - $210,000 + Discretionary Bonus.

Please note that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship for this position. Only candidates who are authorized to work in the United States without sponsorship will be considered.
Fleet Data Centers Employment
Fleet Data Centers employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO.
NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the organization's ongoing needs.
Fleet Data Centers is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants are considered for employment regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or veteran status. If you need assistance applying for any of our open positions, please contact us at info@fleetdatacenters.com.

description_html:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Facility Controls Team

The Facility Controls team builds the control systems behind Fluidstack's data centers: real-time load control, MEP and behind-the-meter integration, automated commissioning, and autonomous deployment.

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Deliver the controls behind gigawatt-scale data centers this decade.

  • Own real-time load control and MEP and behind-the-meter integration.

  • Automate Level 4 and Level 5 commissioning.

  • Drive autonomous, robotic deployment.

Role Scope

  • Own the control and data contract between our facility energy controller and third-party power plant controllers. Define the objects, fields, units, update rates and staleness behavior that cross the boundary in each direction.

  • Define the sequences of operation our controller executes. Normal operation, generation shortfall, source transitions, blackstart and emergency shed, along with the degradation behavior for each.

  • Specify the point maps, interlocks and constraint classes that vendors build against. Then hold them to it through factory and site acceptance.

  • Translate between electrical and software. Turn electrical and generation constraints into requirements our software team can build, and turn software and data constraints back into terms a plant vendor and an engineer of record will accept.

  • Prove the interface in simulation before energization. Every constraint class and every mode transition, then carry that work into automated commissioning

What We're Looking For

The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You have worked in the protocols that move data between machines and between systems (MQTT, OPC UA, REST APIs) and you can say why you would pick one over another for a given job rather than reaching for whichever one you used last.

  • You write and read code in at least one language well enough to prototype an integration, test a point map against a live device, and review what the software team ships. Python or Go preferred.

  • You read a one-line and a panel schedule and can say what the protection, the breakers and the sources will actually do under a fault.

  • You have designed a data contract between two systems: the objects, the fields, the units, the update rates, and what a consumer does when a value goes stale. You held both sides to it.

  • You have written the control narrative for a system where two controllers had to agree, and you owned what happened when they disagreed.

  • You sit between the controls world and the software world and you are fluent in both. You have taken a control requirement from an electrical engineer and turned it into something a software team could actually build, and you have pushed back on a software design because it would not survive the field.

  • You have pushed back on a vendor's scope, or on your own company's assumption, with a number rather than an opinion.

  • Bonus: Microgrid and behind-the-meter control (grid-forming BESS, PV plant controllers, turbine and genset dispatch). Utility and industrial protocols (DNP3, IEC 61850 GOOSE, IEC 60870-5-104, Modbus TCP). Schema-driven contracts (OpenAPI, JSON Schema). Automated Level 4 and Level 5 commissioning.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

title: PMO Project Manager (Growth, Development, Power)
description:
Who We Are:
Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.
The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.
What We Value:
We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.
Who You Are:
The Project Management Office (PMO) Project Manager (Growth, Development, Power) is the PMO's embedded project management partner to the Growth, Development, and Power functions, providing the cross-functional coordination and execution structure required to move sites and related initiatives through the broader organization. Growth, Development, and Power sits at the intersection of numerous internal and external stakeholders.
Progress may depend on Pre-Construction, Construction, Operations, Technology, Finance, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Community Relations, Government Relations, consultants, and external agencies. While Growth, Development, and Power leadership and subject matter experts retain ownership of technical and development decisions, the PM ensures that the work surrounding those decisions is coordinated across the business.
The role creates visibility into what needs to happen, by whom, and when; identifies downstream impacts and dependencies early; and ensures other departments are engaged before gaps become schedule, resource, or business risks. This allows Growth, Development, and Power leaders to focus on development strategy and technical execution while the PM ensures that cross-functional commitments, dependencies, decisions, and business processes remain aligned and moving forward.
What You’ll Do:

Partner with Growth, Development, and Power leadership to understand the development pipeline, departmental priorities, upcoming milestones, constraints, and cross-functional requirements.
Break complex initiatives into clear workstreams, milestones, tasks, dependencies, owners, and decision points.
Maintain portfolio-level visibility into Growth, Development, and Power activities and ensure key initiatives are accurately represented in the PMO project management systems.
Identify and manage dependencies between Site Development and Pre-Construction, Construction, Operations, Technology, Finance, Procurement, Legal, Community Relations, Government Relations, and other stakeholders.
Engage impacted departments early when Growth, Development, and Power activities have downstream implications for scope, timing, resources, cost, or execution.
Establish and facilitate cross-functional meetings needed to resolve dependencies, align plans, make decisions, and maintain progress.
Track commitments and action items across departments and ensure accountability for agreed deliverables.
Identify emerging risks, constraints, stalled activities, resource conflicts, or unclear ownership and facilitate resolution.
Escalate issues to Growth, Development, and Power leadership, the Head of PMO, or broader business leadership when appropriate.

description:

The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.
What We Value:
We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.
Who You Are
You're a seasoned project controls professional with 7+ years managing schedule, cost, change, and documentation on large-scale, mission-critical construction programs — ideally in data centers, schedule-driven sector where downtime isn't an option. You read a P6 schedule critically — spotting broken logic, float that's been quietly manipulated, and a critical path that's about to move before it shows up in next week's update. You can pick apart a change order line by line and know a GMP well enough to catch a buyout gap before it becomes a claim.
You're equally comfortable pushing back on a general contractor in a weekly OAC meeting and briefing an executive on cost and schedule risk in five minutes flat. You don't wait to be asked for bad news — you surface it early, with the data to back it up. You build trust with GCs, design consultants, finance, and leadership not by being agreeable, but by being fair, prepared, and unwilling to accept a story that doesn't add up.
You think in systems — cost, schedule, risk, and change aren't separate disciplines to you, they're one integrated view of program health — and you're comfortable operating in an environment where the schedule compresses, the scope shifts, and the stakes don't.
What You'll Do

Manage the third-party scheduling consultants who review, analyze, and maintain the master schedule, setting expectations for quality, cadence, and reporting
Work directly with general contractors to review and validate their schedules — testing logic, durations, critical path, float, and sequencing against owner milestones
Own schedule health reporting to leadership, giving a clear, honest picture of progress, risk, and forecast, and escalating issues before they become delays
Own the change order process end-to-end: intake, review, verification, negotiation, and resolution
Critically evaluate change orders for scope, pricing, and schedule impact — verifying quantities, labor, markups, and backup rather than taking submissions at face value
Negotiate change orders directly with the general contractor to protect Galaxy's cost and schedule position
Represent Galaxy in weekly change and progress meetings with the GC, driving accountability and timely closure of open items
Maintain a complete, auditable change order log reconciled against the project budget and GMP
Serve as the bridge between field/GC reality and Finance's cost picture, ensuring both tell the same story
Own documentation control for active projects — RFIs, submittals, change documentation, meeting records, and contractual correspondence
Establish and improve project controls standards, templates, reporting, and governance across the portfolio

What We're Looking For

Bachelor's degree in Construction Management, Engineering, Architecture, Finance, or a related field, or equivalent experience
7+ years of project controls or construction management experience on large-scale, complex programs; mission-critical or data center experience required
Proven experience managing schedule on the owner's side, including oversight of scheduling consultants and review of GC-maintained schedules
Deep, hands-on command of CPM scheduling and Primavera P6 — enough to interrogate a schedule, not just read one
Demonstrated experience owning the change order process, including verification and direct negotiation with general contractors
Strong working knowledge of construction contracts and GMP structures (AIA A133/A201 or similar)
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and contract documents
Excellent negotiation and communication skills, with the ability to hold GCs accountable and brief executives with equal credibility
Ability to manage controls across multiple concurrent projects in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment

What You Bring

An owner's mindset — you protect the schedule, the GMP, and the record as if the capital were your own, and you hold contractors and consultants to that same standard.
The credibility to sit across from a general contractor and negotiate change with confidence, and the judgment to know which battles matter.
A sharp, detail-driven eye that catches the number that doesn't hold up, the logic that doesn't sequence, and the risk before it becomes a delay.
The versatility to move fluidly between the field, the GC, Finance, and the executive table, tailoring the message to each without losing the thread.
A bias for order and structure — you bring discipline to controls, documentation, and reporting in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
Willingness to travel up to 20% to Data Center sites as the work requires.

What We Offer:

Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
Flexible Time Off (i.e. unlimited paid vacation days)
Company paid Holidays (14)
Company paid sick leave
Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
3% 401(k) company contribution
Generous paid Parental Leave
Free virtual coaching and counseling sessions through Ginger
Free daily snacks in-office
Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.

title: Systems Engineer
description:
About us
Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.
As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.
Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore enjoys a culture of continuous learning and constant innovation.
 
Job Summary
We are seeking a Staff Hardware Engineer to provide advanced operational, diagnostic, and engineering support for Graphcore’s Arm-based hardware platforms across lab and data center environments.
This role focuses on supporting hardware bring-up, validation, and troubleshooting of complex AI compute platforms, including server blades, racks, and rack-scale infrastructure. The successful candidate will collaborate closely with engineering, platform, and data center teams to ensure the reliability and performance of next-generation AI systems.
 
The Team
The Systems Engineering and Hardware Engineering teams are responsible for enabling the bring-up, validation, and operational reliability of Graphcore’s AI infrastructure platforms.
The team works closely with server engineering, firmware teams, platform architects, and data center operations to support the development, testing, and deployment of next-generation AI compute systems.
This collaborative environment enables rapid problem-solving and continuous improvement of Graphcore’s hardware platforms from early development through production deployment.
 
Responsibilities and Duties

Lead advanced break-fix troubleshooting for server blades, motherboards, power systems, and rack-scale infrastructure.
Support engineering bring-up activities, including component validation and firmware interaction testing.
Diagnose system-level failures involving thermal behavior, power anomalies, network configuration, and BIOS/BMC issues.
Collaborate with server engineering teams to perform root cause analysis and propose corrective actions or design improvements.
Support deployment and rollout of next-generation hardware platforms through structured validation and qualification cycles.
Interface with facilities and infrastructure teams to understand environmental factors impacting system reliability.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), troubleshooting guides, and validation documentation.
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior technicians and engineers on troubleshooting methodologies and hardware diagnostics.
Participate in on-call rotations or off-hours support during critical engineering milestones or hardware bring-up phases.

Candidate Profile
Essential

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related discipline.
1-3+ years experience with server hardware architectures and board-level debugging.
Experience analyzing system logs, hardware telemetry, and power/thermal metrics to isolate hardware failures.
Hands-on experience with HPC systems, AI compute platforms, or rack-scale infrastructure.
Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively in fast-paced engineering environments.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable

Experience supporting prototype or pre-production hardware bring-up.
Familiarity with data center facilities, including liquid cooling and power distribution systems.
Experience using Python, Bash, or automation tools for hardware validation or troubleshooting.
Exposure to structured failure analysis and reliability engineering methodologies.

 
USA BenefitsIn addition to a competitive salary, Graphcore offers flexible working and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, wellbeing and financial future. Our benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), Health Savings Accounts (HSAs), disability and life insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan, commuter benefits, wellness services and an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP). We welcome people of different backgrounds and experiences; we're committed to building an inclusive work environment that makes Graphcore a great home for everyone. We offer an equal opportunity process and understand that there are visible and invisible differences in all of us. We can provide a flexible approach to interview and encourage you to chat to us if you require any reasonable adjustments.

description:
COMPANY OVERVIEW 
Hanwha Energy USA, headquartered in Houston, Texas, is part of the Hanwha Group—a FORTUNE Global 300 company and one of South Korea’s most respected business enterprises. With over a decade of experience delivering high-quality, utility-scale energy projects across North America, Hanwha Energy USA has evolved into a comprehensive energy solutions provider. Our portfolio now spans utility-scale renewables, natural gas generation, retail electricity, and strategic partnerships that power America’s growing data center industry.
Our expertise covers the entire energy value chain—from project development and engineering to construction, operations, and maintenance. By integrating advanced technologies, proven processes, and strong partnerships, we deliver reliable, customized solutions that meet the dynamic needs of local energy markets.
Hanwha Energy USA is actively advancing strategic initiatives in natural gas generation and data center development, including hyperscaler solutions on both sides of the meter. We are proud to serve as the parent company of:

Hanwha Renewables – specializing in utility-scale solar and battery energy storage systems (BESS)
Chariot Energy – providing retail electricity services for residential, commercial, and industrial customers in deregulated markets

 
POSITION OVERVIEW
We are seeking a Director, Gas Infrastructure to add pipeline-specific technical depth to Hanwha Energy USA's growing natural gas infrastructure and generation initiatives. The Director will serve as the company's lead technical resource for the evaluation and advancement of pipeline transportation, storage, compression, interconnection, and other gas infrastructure opportunities. The role will also support technical due diligence for gas-fired generation and related infrastructure investments.
The Director will lead technical workstreams from early screening through due diligence, investment approval, contracting support, and project handoff. Responsibilities include assessing physical feasibility, system operations, integrity and reliability, capital requirements, schedule considerations, and execution risks, and translating those findings into actionable recommendations for development, investment, and operational decision-making. For gas-fired acquisitions and investments, the Director will focus on fuel supply infrastructure, pipeline connectivity, and related technical considerations while coordinating broader plant evaluations with engineering and external subject matter experts.
This role serves as the company's primary technical authority for natural gas transportation and infrastructure matters. The position is responsible for evaluating infrastructure opportunities, identifying technical risks and constraints, supporting strategic planning efforts, and providing technical expertise throughout the project lifecycle. The role works closely with commercial, engineering, environmental, regulatory, and operational teams to ensure infrastructure decisions are grounded in sound technical analysis and aligned with business objectives. The employee may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management. All duties will be assigned in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.
The employee may be required to perform other job-related duties as requested by management.  All duties will be assigned in accordance with applicable laws and company policies.
 
RESPONSIBILITIES
 Pipeline Infrastructure and System Operations

Evaluate interstate and intrastate transmission pipelines, gathering systems, storage facilities, compression, metering, regulation, dehydration, and receipt and delivery interconnections.
Assess pipeline hydraulics, pressure profiles, compression requirements, system bottlenecks, fuel use, redundancy, outage exposure, expansion capability, and practical gas deliverability under normal and peak conditions.
Review pipeline operating data, maintenance practices, control-room management, SCADA and telecommunications, cybersecurity interfaces, emergency response, operator qualification, and reliability risks.
Evaluate integrity-management programs, inline inspection and direct-assessment results, corrosion control, anomaly remediation, class location and high-consequence areas, maximum allowable operating pressure records, leak history, and remaining-life considerations.
Identify pipeline compliance, land, environmental, and permitting issues that may affect feasibility, cost, schedule, operation, expansion, or transfer, and coordinate detailed review with the Environmental Permitting Manager and legal counsel.

 
Commercial Support

Partner directly with the Director, Gas Origination to screen and evaluate pipeline, lateral, storage, compression, and interconnection opportunities, including greenfield projects, brownfield expansions, joint ventures, and anchor-shipper positions.
Develop technical scopes, data-room requests, site-visit plans, management questions, and advisor workplans aligned with commercial priorities and transaction schedules.
Test proposed capacity and deliverability against hydraulic studies, compressor availability, outage assumptions, receipt and delivery pressures, gas quality requirements, downstream constraints, tariff provisions, and operating requirements.
Review route, design basis, constructability, cost estimates, schedule, procurement strategy, commissioning plans, and cost-to-complete exposure for pipeline additions and expansions; provide inputs to the Environmental Permitting Manager for permit strategy and schedule.
Provide technical assumptions for commercial negotiations and investment models, including capacity, availability, fuel loss, operating cost, maintenance capital, expansion capital, schedule, and contingency.

Gas Asset Due Diligence

Support technical due diligence for acquisitions and investments involving simple-cycle and combined-cycle generation assets, with particular emphasis on fuel supply infrastructure, pipeline interfaces, pressure and gas-quality requirements, storage, firm transportation, and no-notice capability.
Evaluate operating performance and asset condition, including heat rate, capacity, starts, equivalent operating hours, forced outages, degradation, major maintenance intervals, long-term service agreements, spare-parts strategy, and near-term capital requirements.
Coordinate specialist review of gas turbines, steam turbines, heat recovery steam generators, generators, balance-of-plant systems, electrical systems, water systems, and emissions controls when broader plant expertise is required.
Identify environmental permit conditions, operating limits, compliance history, and monitoring obligations that affect asset capability or value, and coordinate detailed environmental review with the Environmental Permitting Manager.
Complete a structured handoff of design and execution matters to the Sr. Director, Engineering and the applicable development, construction, or operations team.

Due Diligence and Investment Support

Lead or coordinate independent technical due diligence for pipeline and gas infrastructure acquisitions, equity investments, transportation commitments, and strategic partnerships.
Integrate engineering, operational, environmental, regulatory, and contractual findings into a clear view of asset condition, demonstrated capability, required capital, schedule, and execution risk.
Translate findings into recommendations for valuation assumptions, transaction structure, closing conditions, representations and warranties, indemnities, capital plans, and post-closing priorities.
Direct and challenge independent engineers, integrity specialists, hydraulic consultants, environmental consultants, and other technical advisors so their work addresses the relevant commercial and investment questions.
Prepare and present concise reports and investment materials for senior management, distinguishing confirmed facts, assumptions, sensitivities, unresolved issues, and recommended mitigations.

 
Cross Functional Collaboration

Partner with gas origination, engineering, environmental permitting, corporate strategy, business development, finance, legal, construction, operations, and asset-management teams.
Support commercial and legal teams in reviewing technical provisions of transportation, storage, interconnection, joint venture, acquisition, and transition-services agreements.
Maintain diligence procedures, operating benchmarks, lessons learned, and a qualified network of pipeline, integrity, hydraulic, and generation specialists.
Support asset onboarding and handoff through prioritized risk registers, capital plans, document-gap assessments, and clear ownership of open technical items.

 
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Bachelor's degree in mechanical, chemical, civil, petroleum, electrical, or a closely related engineering discipline from an accredited institution.
Twelve to twenty years of progressively responsible experience with a major interstate or intrastate pipeline company, midstream operator, oil and gas exploration and production company, independent power producer, utility, original equipment manufacturer, or engineering advisory firm.
Deep technical experience in natural gas pipelines and system operations, including hydraulics, compression, integrity management, operating reliability, and applicable PHMSA requirements.
Experience evaluating pipeline projects or operating assets for acquisition, investment, expansion, commercial commitment, major capital approval, or independent engineering review.
Working knowledge of gas-fired power generation and the relationship among plant operating requirements, pipeline deliverability, transportation, storage, pressure, gas quality, and contingency supply.
Ability to interpret hydraulic studies, engineering reports, operating data, inspection records, drawings, permits, tariffs, contracts, cost estimates, schedules, maintenance records, and investment-model assumptions.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including experience presenting material risks and recommendations to senior executives and investment committees.
Ability to manage multiple time-sensitive workstreams and travel approximately 25% to 40%, including asset and project site visits.

 
Preferred Qualifications

Professional Engineer license, advanced engineering degree, or MBA.
Direct experience in pipeline operations, control-room management, compression engineering, integrity management, system planning, storage operations, or major-project development.
Experience with interstate pipeline tariffs and operating requirements, gas transportation and storage contracts, and joint venture or project-development agreements.
Experience evaluating simple-cycle or combined-cycle power plants, including assets supporting large industrial or data center loads.
Experience supporting mergers and acquisitions, representations and warranties diligence, lender or independent engineer reviews, and post-acquisition integration.

 
COMPENSATION: $220,000 - $240,000 salary

title: Foreman
description:
Job Title: Foreman 
Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro South  Location: Afton, TX / On-site Reports to: Site Superintendent Employment Type: Full-Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt 
About Loenbro 
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation. 
Position Summary
The Foreman is responsible for overseeing and coordinating daily pipeline construction, installation, maintenance, and repair activities. This role provides direct supervision to field crews, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and in compliance with company standards, client requirements, and regulatory guidelines. The Pipeline Foreman serves as the primary field leader and acts as the key liaison between craft personnel, subcontractors, and project management.
Essential Responsibilities

Supervise and direct pipeline construction crews in the installation, maintenance, and repair of pipeline systems.
Plan and coordinate daily work activities, manpower, equipment, and material requirements.
Review project drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and construction schedules.
Conduct daily safety meetings and enforce all company, client, and regulatory safety requirements.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, DOT, environmental, and company policies.
Coordinate excavation, trenching, pipe installation, welding, coating, hydrostatic testing, tie-ins, and restoration activities.
Verify elevations, grades, alignments, and installation requirements are met according to project specifications.
Monitor crew productivity, project progress, and quality standards.
Identify and resolve field issues that could impact project schedules or budgets.
Coordinate with inspectors, utility companies, landowners, subcontractors, and project stakeholders.
Maintain accurate daily reports, production records, timesheets, equipment utilization reports, and safety documentation.
Ensure proper use, maintenance, and accountability of company equipment and tools.
Train and mentor crew members, fostering a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
Assist project management with project planning, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Participate in incident investigations and implement corrective actions when necessary.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED.
5+ years of pipeline construction experience.
2+ years of supervisory or foreman experience leading pipeline crews.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction methods, excavation, trench safety, and utility coordination.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and survey information.
Knowledge of OSHA regulations and industry safety standards.
Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to pass pre-employment and client-required screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with oil & gas, natural gas, water, wastewater, or industrial pipeline projects.
OSHA 30 Certification.
NCCER Foreman Certification.
First Aid/CPR Certification.
Competent Person Trenching and Excavation Certification.
Experience managing subcontractors and multiple work crews.
Knowledge of hydrostatic testing, welding inspection processes, and pipeline integrity requirements.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong leadership and team management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction equipment and methods.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Ability to work effectively with project managers, superintendents, inspectors, clients, and field personnel.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Frequent standing, walking, bending, kneeling, climbing, and lifting up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and travel as project demands require.
Ability to safely access active construction sites and uneven terrain.

Work Environment

Heavy civil and pipeline construction projects.
Exposure to construction equipment, noise, dust, vibration, and changing weather conditions.
Travel between project locations may be required.

Benefits 
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team: 

Medical, dental, and vision insurance 

401(k) retirement plan with company match 

Paid time off (PTO) 

Life and disability insurance 

Professional development and training opportunities 

Employee assistance program (EAP) 

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked. 
 
Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities.  If you’re ready to be part of a company that LEADS by: 

Living with Integrity 

Exceeding Expectations 

Acting with Urgency 

Delivering Excellence 

 
…we want to hear from you. 
 
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

description:

 Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro - South Location: Afton, TX Reports To: Superintendent Employment Type: Full Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. We have a national presence but a local approach, and every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs, we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps build and maintain the critical infrastructure that supports communities across the nation.
 
Position Overview: Loenbro Industrial Services Group is seeking to hire experienced Millwrights for our North Dakota jobsite.
As a Millwright, you will install, assemble, dismantle, maintain, troubleshoot, and repair machinery to specifications. Millwrights use precision tools and processes to ensure that the machinery is installed and working correctly and ensuring compliance with all safety regulations and guidelines. We offer a competitive salary, a full range of benefits, a challenging work environment, and growth potential.
Job Duties:

Work with industry-specific and complex precision machines, including but not limited to exhaust fans, generators, hydraulic systems, pumps, gears, bearings, compressors, etc.
Plan, inspect, verify, and document the scope of work.
Use precision leveling and alignment tools to measure angles, material thickness, and small distances with calipers, squares, micrometers, optical instruments, and other tools.
Fit bearings, align gears and wheels, attach motors, and connect belts according to manufacturer’s blueprints and drawings.
Dismantle machines using hammers, wrenches, crowbars, and other hand tools.
Assemble and install equipment such as shafting, exhaust fan blades, and pump systems.
Assemble machines and bolt, weld, rivet, and fasten machinery to foundations or other structures using hand tools and power tools.
Operate engine lathes, grinders, and files.
May construct foundations for machinery.
Fabricate and install parts, equipment, and machinery by measuring, cutting, drilling, and/or welding.
Unload, inspect, move, and set equipment into position using cranes, hoists, dollies, rollers, and trucks.
Use rigging and hoisting devices such as chokers, chain falls, and come-alongs to move equipment/materials into place.
Conduct preventative maintenance such as lubrication and fixing or repairing worn parts.
Follow directions from the supervisor.
Must be willing to perform other duties as assigned.
Other duties as assigned.
Able to recognize changing ground conditions.
Adheres to all safety rules.
Maintaining the work areas in a clean, safe, and orderly manner on a continuous basis
Perform all other job duties as assigned.

Skill/Qualifications:

Must have experience with industrial machinery installation, repair, and maintenance.
Must know how to read blueprints, schematic drawings, and engineering specifications, and understand how to read and interpret technical manuals to determine work procedures.
Must have experience using industrial hand tools and power tools.
Must have all Journeyman Precision Millwright hand tools.
Minimum 4-5 years of industrial construction/maintenance experience.
Minimum of 3 years of Millwright experience.
Must have reliable transportation.

Essential Requirements:

Demonstrated industrial construction/maintenance history experience.
Knowledge of hand tools, power tools, and layout tools such as lasers, ultrasonic measuring and alignment tools, plumb bobs, cutting torches, welding machines, hydraulic torch wrenches, hydraulic stud tensioners, soldering guns, and metalworking equipment, including lathes and grinding machines.
Organization and time management.
Good problem-solving abilities.
Good aptitude and manual dexterity
Knowledge of math concepts, geometry, and layout.
Demonstrated ability to lead others and provide detailed instructions.
Ability to work with others – team player.
Ability to work independently – minimal supervision.
Effective communication skills with co-workers and supervisors.
Employees are required to adhere to large amounts of standing, walking, bending, squatting, and lifting.
Employees may be required to lift, carry, and move up to 50 lbs.
Will occasionally work at heights, climb ladders and stairways, and work off platforms.
Must be capable of working outside in the elements, including, but not limited to heat, cold, rain, snow, and wind; and must be able to work for prolonged periods, up to 12 hours a day.
Employees will be required to wear personal protective equipment (PPE) i.e. hard hat, safety glasses/goggles, ear plugs/muffs, masks/respirators, safety vests, gloves, and steel-toe boots.
Walking on uneven terrain, with an average of two miles per day.
Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors
If driving is required, a valid driver’s license and proof of insurability will be required. All drivers are subject to a DMV background records search. 

 
This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro Environmental Health & Safety (EH&S) policies.
Benefits
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance
401(k) retirement plan with company match
Paid time off (PTO)
Life and disability insurance
Professional development and training opportunities
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.
Our Core Values (LEAD)
At Loenbro, we are guided by our core values:

Living with Integrity
Exceeding Expectations
Acting with Urgency
Delivering Excellence

If you're ready to join a company committed to building exceptional projects, developing outstanding people, and delivering excellence every day, we want to hear from you.

Job Title: QA/QC Manager
Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro - South       Location: Andrews, TX / On-site Reports to: Job Superintendent Employment Type: Full-Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt 
About Loenbro 
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation. 
The Industrial QA/QC Inspector is responsible for ensuring that construction, fabrication, installation, and maintenance activities comply with project specifications, quality standards, industry codes, and client requirements. This role performs inspections, audits, testing, and documentation reviews to verify that work is completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved quality control procedures. The Industrial QA/QC Inspector works closely with project management, field personnel, subcontractors, and clients to maintain quality excellence throughout all phases of the project.
Essential Responsibilities

Perform quality assurance and quality control inspections on industrial construction and maintenance projects.
Verify compliance with project specifications, drawings, codes, standards, and client requirements.
Conduct inspections of materials, equipment, fabrication, installation, and completed work.
Review construction documents, inspection test plans (ITPs), quality procedures, and work packages.
Verify proper implementation of approved procedures, work instructions, and quality programs.
Document inspection findings and prepare detailed quality reports.
Coordinate and witness testing activities, including pressure testing, hydrostatic testing, and functional testing as required.
Inspect structural steel, piping systems, mechanical installations, coatings, and electrical installations based on project scope.
Identify non-conforming work and issue deficiency reports when required.
Track corrective actions and verify resolution of quality issues.
Coordinate inspections with clients, third-party inspectors, and regulatory agencies.
Maintain quality records, turnover packages, test reports, material certifications, and inspection documentation.
Support project audits and quality reviews.
Participate in project meetings and communicate quality concerns to project leadership.
Promote continuous improvement initiatives related to quality and compliance.
Ensure all activities are performed in accordance with company safety policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED required.
Associate degree or technical training in Construction Management, Engineering Technology, Welding Technology, or a related field preferred.
3+ years of experience in quality control, quality assurance, inspection, construction, fabrication, or industrial maintenance.
Working knowledge of construction codes, standards, and inspection processes.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings, specifications, P&IDs, isometric drawings, and quality documents.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office and construction documentation systems.
Strong organizational, communication, and report-writing skills.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to pass required pre-employment and client-specific screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

AWS Certified Welding Inspector (CWI) certification.
NACE/AMPP Coating Inspector certification.
API certifications applicable to project scope.
ASNT Level II certification in NDT methods.
OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.
Experience in power generation, oil & gas, utility, manufacturing, mining, or industrial construction environments.
Experience with mechanical, piping, structural, electrical, or coatings inspections.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

The Industrial QA/QC Inspector is responsible for ensuring that construction, fabrication, installation, and maintenance activities comply with project specifications, quality standards, industry codes, and client requirements. This role performs inspections, audits, testing, and documentation reviews to verify that work is completed safely, accurately, and in accordance with approved quality control procedures.   • NACE/AMPP Coating Inspector certification.
  • API certifications applicable to project scope.
  • ASNT Level II certification in NDT methods.
  • OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification.

 Coordinate with other trades on the job site.

Company Description

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.Job Description
As an FTTx Designer, you will be responsible for creating fiber-to-the-x (FTTx) designs. Responsibilities include but are not limited to the following: sizing of serving boundaries using GIS address data; analyze, interpret, and organize large datasets; determine feeder routes, distribution routes, and drops to premises by utilizing, parcel, ROW, and easement documentation; determine fiber allocations; reviewing field staking sheets, as-Builts and field collected data to determine the optimal running line and construction method. Analyze aerial Imagery and general maps to identify existing utilities or potential obstructions; and produce and review high-quality constructible plan sets using GIS based software.

Qualifications

You are passionate about:

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

You bring to the team:

Ability to read, interpret, create maps and plan sets.
Ability to edit and create PDF documents (Bluebeam or Adobe skills)
Associate’s/bachelor’s degree or equivalent work experience.
General knowledge in OSP construction methods and best practices.
3-6 years of FTTx design and/or OSP experience.
General knowledge of FTTx and/or OSP networks is required.
Knowledge of Google Earth KMZ files.
Knowledge of AutoCAD based software is preferred.
Knowledge of ESRI ArcGIS Software products is preferred.
Knowledge of asset management platforms is preferred ((IQGEO, NetDesigner, CrescentLink, etc.)

title: Construction Foreman
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.CONSTRUCTION FOREMAN
Starbase is expanding its site infrastructure to support ongoing operations and growth. As a Construction Foreman on the Starbase Infrastructure team, you will lead a crew of technicians, laborers, and contractors in the field to build, maintain, and improve industrial facilities, utilities, and civil infrastructure across the site. Work may include earthwork, concrete, carpentry, structural steel, mechanical, electrical, piping, plumbing, HVAC, and related site utilities.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Lead day-to-day field work for assigned infrastructure projects, including work assignments, crew productivity, quality, and schedule
Supervise and instruct technicians, laborers, and subcontractors; set daily priorities and resolve field conflicts
Read and interpret drawings, specifications, and survey control to lay out work and verify grades, elevations, and dimensions
Plan and sequence construction activities across a range of trades as assigned (earthwork, concrete, framing, MEP, finishes, and related civil/industrial work)
Coordinate material deliveries, staging, equipment, and tools so the crew can work without delay
Estimate labor, materials, and equipment needs for assigned scopes; requisition materials and maintain simple, accurate field records
Enforce SpaceX safety policies and jobsite cleanliness; stop work for unsafe conditions and ensure incident reporting procedures are followed
Perform and oversee hands-on construction work as needed
Use hand tools, power tools, and construction equipment; ensure tools and equipment are maintained and secured at the end of each shift
Coordinate with engineering, project management, and adjacent trades to keep work aligned with broader site goals
Maintain a daily log of crew activities, progress, issues, and manpower; report status to supervision as required
Adjust crew size, sequence, and methods as needed to meet deadlines and quality standards; escalate issues that affect cost, schedule, or design

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate 
2+ years of experience as a foreman or crew lead

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Experience leading crews in a general construction or multi-trade environment
Familiarity with common construction trades such as earthwork, concrete, carpentry, mechanical, electrical, piping, and site utilities
Knowledge of standard methods, materials, tools, and equipment used in industrial and civil construction
Ability to interpret blueprints, shop drawings, and specifications, and to make field calculations for areas, volumes, and material quantities
Ability to instruct and direct skilled, semi-skilled, and unskilled workers
Knowledge of occupational hazards and safety practices applicable to construction work
Experience in a fast-paced construction environment with changing priorities
Written and verbal communication skills; use of MS Outlook and Teams
Experience with heavy equipment, forklifts, boom lifts, and/or scissor lifts
Ability to offer field feedback to the design team to improve cost, quality, and constructibility

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Work hours depend on site priorities and may require extended hours, weekends, and holidays; flexibility required
Periodic work in extreme outdoor environments: heat, cold, wind, rain
Must be able to lift up to 50 lbs. unassisted
Basic mechanical aptitude and ability to perform regular manual labor
Must be able to stand for long periods of time; work at heights, climbing up and down ladders, bending, grasping, sitting, pulling, pushing, stooping, and stretching may be required
Ability to work in confined spaces as required by the work
Must have a valid driver’s license
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.  

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

title: Manager, Chief Engineer, NA
description:
About Vantage Data Centers


Vantage Data Centers powers, cools, protects and connects the technology of the world’s well-known hyperscalers, cloud providers and large enterprises. Developing and operating across North America, EMEA and Asia Pacific, Vantage has evolved data center design in innovative ways to deliver dramatic gains in reliability, efficiency and sustainability in flexible environments that can scale as quickly as the market demands.

Position Overview  

The Facility Manager serves as the primary customer-facing operations leader for assigned data center facilities and is responsible for delivering exceptional customer experience while maintaining the operational readiness, appearance, and functionality of the campus. This role oversees facility maintenance programs, quality/warranty repair coordination, customer support activities, vendor performance, building services, and operational coordination within a mission critical environment. 

Acting as a trusted partner to the customer, the Facility Manager works closely with Site Operations, Construction, Engineering, Security, IT, Asset Management, Leasing, and Vendor Management teams to ensure customer needs are addressed efficiently and professionally. The Facility Manager coordinates facility related activities, maintenance programs, customer requests, inspections, warranty repairs, and service delivery while ensuring compliance with operational standards and service level expectations. 

The Facility Manager leads Facility Technicians and contracted service providers responsible for building operations, maintenance coordination, inspections, customer support activities, and campus readiness. Success in this position requires strong leadership, communication, customer relationship management, organizational skills, and a solid understanding of mission-critical environments. 

Reporting to the Senior Director of Operations, the Facility Manager plays a critical role in maintaining customer confidence, ensuring campus standards are upheld, and driving operational excellence across a rapidly growing hyperscale campus. 

 

Essential Job Functions and Duties 

Serve as a primary operational point of contact for assigned customers and develop trusted working relationships that support a positive customer experience. 

Lead customer-facing facility management activities while supporting overall campus operational objectives. 

Coordinate and manage customer requests, concerns, facility issues, and service-related activities to ensure timely resolution and communication. 

Oversee maintenance, repair, and lifecycle management activities for campus common areas, building exteriors, office spaces, amenities, and structural building components. 

Coordinate warranty and quality-related repair activities with internal stakeholders, contractors, developers, and equipment manufacturers. 

Track and drive resolution of warranty claims, construction-related deficiencies, punch list items, and customer-reported quality concerns. 

Lead a team of Facility Technicians responsible for building maintenance, customer support services, inspections, and campus operational readiness. 

Develop team capabilities through coaching, training, mentorship, and performance management. 

Manage vendor relationships, contracts, service agreements, and on-site service providers to ensure safe, high-quality, and cost-effective service delivery. 

Coordinate vendor activities to minimize customer impact and maintain compliance with campus operational requirements. 

Audit and oversee execution of maintenance programs for critical facility infrastructure to ensure compliance with company standards, contractual obligations, and operational expectations. 

Partner with Site Operations leadership to monitor infrastructure performance, reliability initiatives, and customer-impacting maintenance activities. 

Coordinate cross-functional support efforts involving Operations, Construction, Engineering, Security, IT, Asset Management, Leasing, and other campus stakeholders. 

Facilitate communication and planning for customer projects, move-ins, expansions, upgrades, and operational changes. 

Participate in customer meetings, operational reviews, site walks, and project coordination meetings. 

Monitor key performance metrics and service-level commitments to ensure customer expectations are consistently met. 

Support budget development, forecasting, expense management, and vendor cost control initiatives. 

Ensure compliance with company policies, environmental requirements, safety programs, and regulatory standards. 

Support response efforts for customer-facing facility issues and coordinate resources through resolution. 

Drive continuous improvement initiatives focused on customer experience, operational efficiency, and campus service delivery. 

Develop and maintain operational documentation, procedures, service standards, and communication plans. 

Perform additional duties as assigned by Management. 

 

Job Requirements 

Minimum 5 years, 7+ preferred, experience in facilities management, mission-critical operations, commercial property operations, building engineering, or data center environments. 

Minimum 2 years, 3+ preferred, of leadership experience managing facilities personnel, vendors, contractors, or operational teams. 

Associate's or Bachelor's degree in Facilities Management, Engineering, Construction Management, Business Administration, or related field preferred. 

Data center or mission-critical facility management experience preferred. 

Certified Facility Manager (CFM), FMP, RPA, CPM, PMP, or similar professional certification preferred. 

Experience serving in a customer-facing role supporting large enterprise, hyperscale, or mission-critical environments. 

Strong understanding of building systems, facility maintenance practices, construction warranty processes, and vendor management. 

Experience coordinating cross-functional teams and driving issue resolution across multiple stakeholders. 

Experience overseeing operational service delivery and maintenance programs in large-scale facilities. 

Knowledge of critical facility infrastructure including electrical distribution, cooling systems, generators, UPS systems, fire protection, and building management systems. 

Demonstrated ability to build strong customer relationships and deliver exceptional service. 

Strong communication skills with the ability to engage customers, vendors, and internal stakeholders. 

Strong technical writing skills and experience developing operational documentation and training programs 

Experience managing budgets, service contracts, procurement activities, and vendor performance. 

Proficiency with CMMS, work order management systems, and operational reporting tools. 

Strong communication, presentation, organization, and problem-solving skills. 

Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize multiple projects and customer commitments simultaneously. 

Must successfully complete a background check. 

Travel may be required up to 10% but may increase as business needs evolve. 

 

Physical activities and requirements  

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions. 

 

Additional Details 

Typical Working Hours: Monday to Friday 7:00am-4:00pm 

This position is eligible for company benefits including but not limited to medical, dental, and vision coverage, life and AD&D, short and long-term disability coverage, paid time off, employee assistance, participation in a 401k program that includes company match, and many other additional voluntary benefits.

Amazon Web Services is seeking a Mechanical Engineer to become part of a global engineering team, responsible for the design and continuous innovation of our rapidly expanding data center foot print.

Engineers at Amazon work to design resilient, cost effective mechanical distribution systems. As engineers at Amazon we are responsible for achieving a world class uptime for our customers. As an engineer at Amazon you have the ability to drive change and define/design the systems our customers rely on.
