description_html:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

About This Role:

As Senior Manager, Utility Contracts, you will sit within the Energy Development Group (EDG) and own the full lifecycle of Crusoe's utility infrastructure agreements: negotiating new agreements and amendments with serving utilities, and managing the obligations under executed agreements across our data center portfolio. You will be the person who knows every deadline, every deliverable, and every counterparty commitment. You will work hand-in-hand with our real estate, power engineering, legal, and finance teams, and help shape the obligation-management platform we are building to scale this function across every future project.

This is a role for someone who has lived inside the utility world - who reads tariffs and connection requirements fluently, understands how utilities think about interconnection, cost recovery, and reliability obligations, and can lead negotiations with utility commercial and legal teams.

What You’ll Be Working On:

  • Utility Agreement Negotiation: Lead the negotiation of utility infrastructure agreements for new and existing data center campuses - construction agreements, operating agreements, transfer agreements, and amendments - in coordination with EDG commercial leads, outside counsel, and utility counterparties.

  • Obligation Management: Own the responsibility matrix for each project's agreement stack: every obligation tracked with its contractual cite, deadline, owner, and status. Run the monthly deadline review, drive early escalation of at-risk items, and make sure recurring obligations (reports, forecasts, certifications, payments) never slip.

  • Utility Requirements & Compliance: Serve as EDG's authority on utility requirements - tariff provisions, end-user connection requirements, metering and interconnection specifications, Good Utility Practice, and NERC / RTO reliability obligations for large loads (load ride-through, UFLS, emergency operations, ramp rates) and translate them into actionable requirements for our engineering and operations teams.

  • Construction agreements: Manage the contractual side of customer-build programs - design package submittals, procurement compliance against utility approved lists, commissioning and title transfer sequencing, easement and land-rights deliverables, and closeout obligations with enough EPC fluency to engage credibly with project and construction teams.

  • Cross-Functional Coordination: Act as the connective tissue between EDG, Real Estate, Power Engineering, Legal, Finance, and our data center tenants on everything touching the utility agreements - from milestone payments and collateral postings to easement deliveries and operating protocols.

  • Executive Reporting: Provide leadership with clear, current visibility into obligation status, upcoming deadlines, counterparty performance, and contract risks across the portfolio.

What You'll Bring to the Team

  • Deep Utility Experience: 8+ years in the electric utility sector, at a utility, or negotiating and managing utility agreements on behalf of large customers or developers - with direct experience in large-load interconnection, energy service / electric service agreements, and utility construction agreements.

  • Utility Requirements Fluency: Strong working command of utility tariffs, end-user connection requirements, interconnection processes, metering standards, and reliability obligations (NERC standards, RTO/ISO requirements such as MISO, ERCOT, or CAISO large-load rules). You know how utilities operate, what they will and won't agree to, and why.

  • EPC Exposure: Hands-on familiarity with the engineering, procurement, and construction lifecycle - design reviews, procurement standards, commissioning, and project closeout - sufficient to manage customer-build and transfer obligations credibly alongside project teams.

  • Negotiation Track Record: Demonstrated success negotiating complex infrastructure agreements with utility counterparties, balancing commercial outcomes, schedule protection, and long-term relationships.

  • Contract Management Rigor: Exceptional organization and attention to detail. You are the person who reads the footnotes, catches the cross-reference, and builds the system so nothing depends on memory.

  • Cross-Functional Communication: Ability to translate contract language into clear actions for engineers, real estate teams, finance, and executives - and to communicate credibly with utility commercial, legal, and operations staff.

  • Location: Based in, or willing to relocate to, Dallas, TX or San Francisco, CA.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience supporting hyperscale data center, large industrial, or other large-load development projects.

  • Familiarity with behind-the-meter / bring-your-own-capacity structures, customer-build lead lines, or asset transfer agreements with utilities.

  • Experience implementing contract lifecycle management or obligation-tracking tools.

  • Utility regulatory exposure (state commission proceedings, tariff filings)

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $160,000 - $200,000+ Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

title: Senior BIM Designer MEP, Data Center Engineering
location: Austin, Texas, United States; Denver, Colorado, United States; Remote US; Seattle, Washington, United States
salary: $120,000 - $150,000 Salary + Discretionary Bonus
description:
Overview
Fleet Data Centers designs, builds and operates mega-scale data center campuses. Fleet provides its customers flexibility and predictability to meet their upside demand forecasts, addressing a key need in the market as traditional leased models are struggling to keep pace with the demand for new Cloud and AI infrastructure. Fleet is led by a team of industry veterans that have already made a lasting imprint on the evolution of global digital infrastructure and are committed and uniquely capable of upleveling data center development scale and operations in the face of rising demand. Fleet is well positioned to bring in-house design, engineering and operational capabilities to collaborate with customers on tailored solutions for campuses of 500MW+. This unique model enables Fleet to provide the world’s largest and most sophisticated customers a seamless extension of their own data center fleets with constant access to design innovation. Fleet is headquartered in Denver, Colorado, with satellite offices in Seattle, WA and Arlington, VA.
 
Position Overview:
The Senior BIM Designer MEP Engineer will be responsible for reviewing project Revit and Navisworks models assessing model development, modeling standards and practices and adherence to the BIM standards and compile your comments on the same. They will be responsible for supporting partner teams such as design, construction, and operations.
 
The BIM Designer MEP will be responsible for establishing and maintaining BIM standards, processes, and workflows. The candidate shall also be responsible for the BIM lifecycle of multiple design projects across the globe.
The candidate shall also be responsible for developing piping, instrumentation, and electrical plantroom layouts along with single line diagrams and schematics.
 
Key Responsibilities:

BIM Implementation Strategy, establishing and maintaining BIM standards, processes, and workflows as well as educating and training internal teams in BIM software and procedures
BIM oversight of all aspects of the data center life cycle starting with design, construction, and maintenance of data center BIM models
Lead discussions in engineering and construction best practices, supporting the wider team by sharing knowledge with a view to establishing new standards
Develop BIM Implementation strategy and deliver complex international projects
Establish and ensure BIM files meet Fleet Data Center standards and are always following the BIM Guidelines during the project by reviewing consultant BIM documentation, BIM files, coordinate output formats, and validate data quality, collect design documents and files for projects
CDE Management, establish and administer the CDE and support efficient management of multi-stakeholder projects
Project Management, coordinating BIM execution and project delivery with project leadership
BIM Execution, create and maintain the project’s industry framework documents including BEP, MIDP, MPDT, appendices etc.
Technical support, establish data-integrated workflows for building projects and provide support, guidance and training to project teams
Digital technology and content management, oversee the production of smart object content, templates and libraries in the context of the project, deploy the use of Fleet Data Centers content management system Autodesk Content Catalog or other onto projects and manage the best practice use of digital technology for collaboration, coordination and delivery
Quality, establish and administer the digital quality assurance control procedures
Working with multiple design and engineering professionals on concepts and build projects

Required Qualifications:

Extensive experience in managing MEP delivery across multiple projects or business units
5+ years of design and construction experience
5+ years working with Revit
5+ years working with Navisworks
Strong technical knowledge of mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems
Strong problem-solving, analytical and strategic planning skills
Excellent organization skills in archival and maintenance operations of project documents
Experience with Tier 1 contractor projects or complex multi-disciplinary programs
Familiarity with digital construction tools, BIM and lean methodologies
Extensive knowledge of software packages such as ACC and Procore
Experience in the establishment and management of BIM and VDC models including orientation, geo-positioning, co-ordination and the set-up of model reviews

Preferred Qualifications:

Degree or equivalent in mechanical, electrical, building services or related discipline
Experience in mission critical design
Experience in piping design and chilled water piping and instrumentation layout, plantroom layout design and electrical architecture
Professional accreditation or membership of a relevant body such as CIBSE, IET, Engineers Ireland
Postgraduate qualification in building services, project management or sustainability
Training in digital design, BIM management or innovative MEP technologies

Key Competencies:

Integrity and Ethical Standards: Build trust, ensure fairness, and foster long-term, transparent relationships with suppliers
Effective Communication: The ability to clearly convey expectations and requirements to suppliers and negotiation parties, while understanding their needs and concerns. Comfortable delivering written and verbal presentations to internal leadership teams
Emotional Intelligence (EQ): Ability to understand the emotions, cultural nuances, and motivations of others, while effectively managing one's own emotions during high-pressure negotiations
Strategic Thinking: Ability to think big picture while also managing granular details
Adaptability: Proven track record of managing change and ambiguity in a fast-paced environment
Leadership: Ability to manage cross-functional teams and external vendors
Experience with complex, multi-site projects: Manage multiple projects under tight deadlines and deliver exceptional results
Excellent communication and presentation skills: Capable of interfacing with senior leadership and diverse stakeholders
Creative problem-solver: Ability to troubleshoot and optimize system performance effectively

Working Conditions:

This role requires occasional travel to data center sites across multiple regions (up to 25% travel)
Ability to work in both office environments and active construction sites, adhering to all safety protocols

 
Expected Salary Range: $120,000 - $150,000 Salary + Discretionary Bonus
 
Seattle, WA (Mercer Island), Denver, CO, or Alexandria, VAA.
Fleet Data Centers Employment
Fleet Data Centers employees enjoy competitive compensation and comprehensive benefits, including 100% employer-covered medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401K program, standard paid holidays, and unlimited PTO. 
 
NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may perform other related duties to meet the organization's ongoing needs.
 
Fleet Data Centers is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants are considered for employment regardless of age, race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, or veteran status. If you need assistance applying for any of our open positions, please contact us at info@fleetdatacenters.com.

title: Graduate Firmware Engineer
description:
About Graphcore
Graphcore is a global leader in artificial intelligence computing systems. We design advanced semiconductors, software, and data center systems that provide the specialized processing power needed to advance AI while improving the efficiency required for broad adoption.
As part of SoftBank Group, Graphcore belongs to a family of companies developing transformative technologies. Our U.S. engineering teams contribute to the hardware and software platforms that support the next generation of AI systems.
The Opportunity
We are looking for a recent graduate or early-career engineer to join the BMC Engineering team as a Graduate Firmware Engineer. You will develop low-level and embedded firmware that supports the operation, control, monitoring, and validation of advanced compute systems.
You will work with experienced firmware, hardware, systems, and software engineers throughout the development lifecycle. The role combines hands-on implementation with automated testing, lab-based debugging, hardware bring-up, and analysis of interactions between firmware and the underlying platform.

Start: September, 2027Location: Austin, Texas, USA

What You Will Do

Design, implement, test, and maintain system and embedded firmware in C, C++, or Python.
Take ownership of defined firmware features and deliver them from requirements and design through implementation, validation, and documentation.
Develop and debug firmware in a Linux-based engineering environment using appropriate diagnostic tools and techniques.
Create automated tests and scripts that improve firmware validation, test coverage, and engineering efficiency.
Contribute to continuous integration and delivery workflows for firmware development and testing.
Plan and conduct engineering experiments, analyze test data, and communicate findings clearly.
Support lab setup, system configuration, hardware bring-up, and firmware validation on development platforms.
Investigate firmware behavior and hardware-software interactions, identify root causes, and implement verified fixes.
Work across BMC, firmware, hardware, silicon, systems, and software teams to reproduce and resolve technical issues.
Write clear design notes, test procedures, change descriptions, and technical findings.
Follow established engineering and coding practices and contribute constructively to code and design reviews.

What You Will Bring

A bachelor's or master's degree in computer engineering, electrical engineering, computer science, or a closely related field, completed recently or expected before the role begins.
A strong foundation in C or C++ and working knowledge of Python or another scripting language.
Understanding of computer architecture, embedded systems, firmware, and low-level software concepts.
Familiarity with Linux environments, command-line development tools, and version-control systems.
Experience applying structured debugging methods to software, firmware, or hardware-software problems.
Ability to interpret technical requirements, break work into manageable tasks, and deliver reliable results with appropriate guidance.
Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering disciplines.
Curiosity, sound engineering judgment, and willingness to learn new technologies, tools, and development methods.

Preferred Qualifications

Academic, internship, or personal project experience developing embedded software or firmware.
Experience with microcontrollers, embedded processors, system-level firmware, or hardware bring-up.
Experience using lab equipment to test or debug hardware-based systems.
Experience with automated testing, Python scripting, or continuous integration workflows.
Exposure to baseboard management controllers, platform management, data center hardware, or high-speed compute systems.
Experience debugging interfaces or interactions between hardware and software.

These qualifications are helpful, not required. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification.
United States Benefits Overview
Graphcore offers competitive compensation and programs designed to support employees' health, financial well-being, flexibility, and development. Benefits for eligible U.S. employees may include:

Medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus mental health, wellness, and employee assistance resources.
A 401(k) retirement plan with company matching, together with company-provided life and disability coverage.
Paid time off, company holidays, flexible working hours, parental leave, and learning and career-development resources.

Benefits vary by work location, employment status, and plan eligibility and are subject to the terms of the applicable plans and company policies. This overview is not a contract or guarantee of benefits.
Equal Opportunity and Accommodations
Graphcore is an equal opportunity employer. We consider qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, pregnancy, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, ancestry, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.
Graphcore is committed to an inclusive and accessible hiring process. If you need a reasonable accommodation to participate in the application or interview process, please let the recruiting team know.
Candidate Privacy
Personal information submitted during the recruiting process will be handled in accordance with Graphcore's applicable candidate privacy notices.

description:

description:

Graphcore is a global leader in artificial intelligence computing systems. We design advanced semiconductors and data center hardware that provide the specialized processing power needed to advance AI while improving the efficiency required for broad adoption.
As part of SoftBank Group, Graphcore belongs to a family of companies developing transformative technologies. Our AI Engineering Campus in Austin plays an important role in building the hardware platforms that support the next generation of AI systems.
The Opportunity
We are looking for a recent graduate or early-career engineer to join the Hardware Platform Development team as a Graduate Systems Engineer. You will contribute to the design, integration, validation, and performance analysis of advanced AI compute platforms.
You will work with experienced hardware, firmware, software, mechanical, thermal, and systems engineers throughout the development lifecycle. The role combines subsystem engineering, hands-on laboratory work, test automation, data analysis, troubleshooting, and clear technical documentation.
Start: September, 2027Location: Austin, Texas, USA
What You Will Do

Contribute to the design, integration, and testing of CPU and high-speed input and output subsystems for advanced compute platforms.
Take ownership of defined engineering tasks from requirements and test planning through execution, analysis, and technical review.
Develop system-level validation plans, procedures, scripts, and tools that improve test coverage, repeatability, data collection, and analysis.
Evaluate platform performance, power, signal behavior, reliability, and interoperability using laboratory measurements and system data.
Investigate emerging input and output technologies, including PCIe 6.0 and 800G Ethernet, and assess their use in advanced computing systems.
Support platform power, cooling, and energy-efficiency investigations, including liquid-cooling systems for high-performance processors.
Use power meters, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and comparable laboratory equipment to execute tests and gather reliable evidence.
Analyze unexpected behavior, reproduce issues, perform structured root-cause investigations, and help verify corrective actions.
Collaborate across hardware, firmware, software, mechanical, thermal, manufacturing, and systems teams to resolve integration issues.
Maintain accurate requirements, test procedures, scripts, data summaries, engineering notes, and change records.
Present progress, results, risks, and technical recommendations clearly and follow applicable engineering, configuration-control, laboratory, and safety procedures.

What You Will Bring

A bachelor's or master's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, systems engineering, or a closely related field, completed recently or expected before the role begins.
A strong foundation in computer architecture, digital systems, embedded systems, hardware-software interaction, or system-level engineering.
Hands-on experience with laboratory testing and technical measurements through coursework, research, internships, student teams, or personal projects.
Experience with at least one programming or scripting language, such as Python, C, C++, or MATLAB.
Ability to plan technical work, analyze test data, document results accurately, and draw evidence-based conclusions.
A structured approach to problem-solving, troubleshooting, and root-cause investigation.
Clear written and verbal communication skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across engineering disciplines.
Curiosity, sound engineering judgment, and willingness to learn unfamiliar tools, systems, and laboratory methods.

Preferred Qualifications

Internship, research, academic, or project experience with CPU subsystems, PCIe, Ethernet, high-speed interfaces, or platform validation.
Experience using power meters, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, protocol analyzers, or similar laboratory equipment.
Experience creating test automation, data-analysis tools, or engineering scripts.
Exposure to platform performance characterization, power delivery, thermal management, liquid cooling, or energy efficiency.
Familiarity with systems integration, design verification, configuration control, or engineering change processes.
Experience presenting engineering work or test results in a technical review setting.

These qualifications are helpful, not required. We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification.

Provide leadership for estimates and proposals including cost analysis, estimate coordination, as well as development and review of trade takeoffs and internal pricing. 
Oversee all capital bids before submission. 
Delegate new customer opportunities within estimating team. 
Evaluate subcontract cost estimates and proposals, as well as preparing/reviewing self-perform estimates, and assembling final estimate for owner. 
Drive and maintain all National Opportunities Reporting. 
Perform productivity analysis of cost estimates, comparisons of scope, quantities, and cost data between projects. 
Negotiate with and engage in subcontract solicitation during the bidding process and maintain master subcontractor/vendor lists by trade.

Exceed expectations with excellent customer service, operational excellence, and strategic insight.

Demonstrated experience with heavy civil construction projects, specifically water/wastewater treatment plants and process piping.
Ability to build and maintain a positive working relationship with staff, vendors, and clients. 
Exceptional time management and customer relation skills.

description:
Job Title: Equipment OperatorCompany: Loenbro, LLCBusiness Unit/Department:  Loenbro South                                        Location: Afton, TXReports to:  Foreman / SuperintendentEmployment Type: Full-TimeFLSA Classification: Non-Exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.
Job SummaryLoenbro is looking for an experienced heavy equipment operator to join our team. We are looking for experienced people who can operate track hoe, skid steer, telehandler for a variety of construction projects. This position is responsible for operating heavy equipment, preparing job sites, performing basic maintenance on machinery, and ensuring compliance with all safety regulations and guidelines.
Essential Job Responsibilities

Perform daily inspections of equipment to ensure proper functionality and safety.
Perform light maintenance on equipment as required to ensure optimal performance.
Adhere to all safety regulations to ensure a safe and compliant work environment.
Submit daily reports detailing equipment status, work progress, and any issues encountered.
Operate a diverse range of heavy equipment to support project needs and ensure efficient completion of tasks.
Perform all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications
Required:

PEC certificate holders are preferred.
Highschool Diploma or GED required. 3+ years of operating heavy equipment experience required.
Basic mechanical knowledge and skills.

Preferred:

Candidates who have experience with operating an Excavator.
Must be able to clearly explain steps and provide clear directions.
Must be able to complete and complete the paperwork required for purchase orders, time sheets, etc. and answer questions about the construction processes for field staff and other subcontractors.
Must be willing to embrace the company’s core values.

Physical Demands and Work Environment
The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work Environment:

Potential exposure to extreme cold and hot temperatures.
Manufacturing, pipeline, and refining environment.
Fit and move in confined spaces including tanks and vessels.
Limited working surfaces.
Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors.
Exposure to areas with limited visibility.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.
Benefits
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team:

Medical, dental, and vision insurance.
401(k) retirement plan with company match.
Paid time off (PTO).
Life and disability insurance.
Professional development and training opportunities.
Employee assistance program (EAP).

Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked.
Guided by Core Values (LEAD), grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro betters our families, customers, and local communities. If you are ready to be part of a company that LEADS by:

Living with Integrity
Exceeding Expectations
Acting with Urgency
Delivering Excellence

…we want to hear from you.
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer

title: Foreman
description:
Job Title: Foreman 
Company: Loenbro, LLC Business Unit/Department: Loenbro South  Location: Andrews, TX / On-site Reports to: Site Superintendent Employment Type: Full-Time FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt 
About Loenbro 
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation. 
Position Summary
The Foreman is responsible for overseeing and coordinating daily pipeline construction, installation, maintenance, and repair activities. This role provides direct supervision to field crews, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and in compliance with company standards, client requirements, and regulatory guidelines. The Pipeline Foreman serves as the primary field leader and acts as the key liaison between craft personnel, subcontractors, and project management.
Essential Responsibilities

Supervise and direct pipeline construction crews in the installation, maintenance, and repair of pipeline systems.
Plan and coordinate daily work activities, manpower, equipment, and material requirements.
Review project drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and construction schedules.
Conduct daily safety meetings and enforce all company, client, and regulatory safety requirements.
Ensure compliance with OSHA, DOT, environmental, and company policies.
Coordinate excavation, trenching, pipe installation, welding, coating, hydrostatic testing, tie-ins, and restoration activities.
Verify elevations, grades, alignments, and installation requirements are met according to project specifications.
Monitor crew productivity, project progress, and quality standards.
Identify and resolve field issues that could impact project schedules or budgets.
Coordinate with inspectors, utility companies, landowners, subcontractors, and project stakeholders.
Maintain accurate daily reports, production records, timesheets, equipment utilization reports, and safety documentation.
Ensure proper use, maintenance, and accountability of company equipment and tools.
Train and mentor crew members, fostering a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
Assist project management with project planning, forecasting, and resource allocation.
Participate in incident investigations and implement corrective actions when necessary.

Required Qualifications

High school diploma or GED.
5+ years of pipeline construction experience.
2+ years of supervisory or foreman experience leading pipeline crews.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction methods, excavation, trench safety, and utility coordination.
Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and survey information.
Knowledge of OSHA regulations and industry safety standards.
Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
Ability to pass pre-employment and client-required screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with oil & gas, natural gas, water, wastewater, or industrial pipeline projects.
OSHA 30 Certification.
NCCER Foreman Certification.
First Aid/CPR Certification.
Competent Person Trenching and Excavation Certification.
Experience managing subcontractors and multiple work crews.
Knowledge of hydrostatic testing, welding inspection processes, and pipeline integrity requirements.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

Strong leadership and team management skills.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Strong understanding of pipeline construction equipment and methods.
Effective verbal and written communication skills.
Commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
Ability to work effectively with project managers, superintendents, inspectors, clients, and field personnel.

Physical Requirements

Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
Frequent standing, walking, bending, kneeling, climbing, and lifting up to 50 pounds.
Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and travel as project demands require.
Ability to safely access active construction sites and uneven terrain.

Work Environment

Heavy civil and pipeline construction projects.
Exposure to construction equipment, noise, dust, vibration, and changing weather conditions.
Travel between project locations may be required.

Benefits 
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team: 

Medical, dental, and vision insurance

Job Title: Foreman 

Company: Loenbro, LLC 
Business Unit/Department: Loenbro South  
Location: Andrews, TX / On-site 
Reports to: Site Superintendent 
Employment Type: Full-Time 
FLSA Classification: Non-Exempt 

About Loenbro 

Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care. 

At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation. 

Position Summary

The Foreman is responsible for overseeing and coordinating daily pipeline construction, installation, maintenance, and repair activities. This role provides direct supervision to field crews, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, on schedule, and in compliance with company standards, client requirements, and regulatory guidelines. The Pipeline Foreman serves as the primary field leader and acts as the key liaison between craft personnel, subcontractors, and project management.

Essential Responsibilities

  • Supervise and direct pipeline construction crews in the installation, maintenance, and repair of pipeline systems.
  • Plan and coordinate daily work activities, manpower, equipment, and material requirements.
  • Review project drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and construction schedules.
  • Conduct daily safety meetings and enforce all company, client, and regulatory safety requirements.
  • Ensure compliance with OSHA, DOT, environmental, and company policies.
  • Coordinate excavation, trenching, pipe installation, welding, coating, hydrostatic testing, tie-ins, and restoration activities.
  • Verify elevations, grades, alignments, and installation requirements are met according to project specifications.
  • Monitor crew productivity, project progress, and quality standards.
  • Identify and resolve field issues that could impact project schedules or budgets.
  • Coordinate with inspectors, utility companies, landowners, subcontractors, and project stakeholders.
  • Maintain accurate daily reports, production records, timesheets, equipment utilization reports, and safety documentation.
  • Ensure proper use, maintenance, and accountability of company equipment and tools.
  • Train and mentor crew members, fostering a culture of safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
  • Assist project management with project planning, forecasting, and resource allocation.
  • Participate in incident investigations and implement corrective actions when necessary.

Required Qualifications

  • High school diploma or GED.
  • 5+ years of pipeline construction experience.
  • 2+ years of supervisory or foreman experience leading pipeline crews.
  • Strong understanding of pipeline construction methods, excavation, trench safety, and utility coordination.
  • Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, alignment sheets, and survey information.
  • Knowledge of OSHA regulations and industry safety standards.
  • Strong leadership, communication, and organizational skills.
  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.
  • Ability to pass pre-employment and client-required screenings.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with oil & gas, natural gas, water, wastewater, or industrial pipeline projects.
  • OSHA 30 Certification.
  • NCCER Foreman Certification.
  • First Aid/CPR Certification.
  • Competent Person Trenching and Excavation Certification.
  • Experience managing subcontractors and multiple work crews.
  • Knowledge of hydrostatic testing, welding inspection processes, and pipeline integrity requirements.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong leadership and team management skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced construction environment.
  • Excellent problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
  • Strong understanding of pipeline construction equipment and methods.
  • Effective verbal and written communication skills.
  • Commitment to safety, quality, and operational excellence.
  • Ability to work effectively with project managers, superintendents, inspectors, clients, and field personnel.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to work outdoors in varying weather conditions.
  • Frequent standing, walking, bending, kneeling, climbing, and lifting up to 50 pounds.
  • Ability to work extended hours, weekends, and travel as project demands require.
  • Ability to safely access active construction sites and uneven terrain.

Work Environment

  • Heavy civil and pipeline construction projects.
  • Exposure to construction equipment, noise, dust, vibration, and changing weather conditions.
  • Travel between project locations may be required.

Benefits

  • Medical, dental, and vision insurance 
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match 
  • Paid time off (PTO)

Job SummaryResponsible for planning, scheduling, employee oversite, and management of Underground Maintenance and Inspection projects. Assists Project Manager in coordinating activities of employees engaged in construction process, utilizing knowledge of equipment, techniques, procedures, and specifications. This position is responsible for assisting craft supervision to coordinating activities of workers engaged in construction process, utilizing knowledge of equipment, techniques, procedures, and specifications.
 
Essential Job Responsibilities 

Understand how to read project drawings.
Knowledge of national and local code requirements relevant to this discipline.
Supervises the daily work of employees.
Support estimating effort through bid reviews and constructability reviews, including review of activity productions, crew makeup, equipment selection and cost analysis.
Understand how to generate and manage a 3 week and 6 week look ahead schedule to ensure manpower, materials, equipment, subcontractors, and all resources are scheduled appropriately.
Assures all employees within the team know and follow the company safety and work rules and policies.
Participates in review of job costs and overall performance with a particular focus on production
Supports planning of on-the-job training for team members to ensure safety and quality of the work being done. Timely review of job sites for safety and quality of the work.
Work closely with clients of the operations to create new opportunities for Loenbro.
Perform all other duties as assigned by Supervisor

 
Minimum Qualifications
Required: 

Minimum of 5 years of Superintendent experience in the construction of industrial projects.
Experience managing projects and leading crews of up to 12 or more personals
Understanding of Industry standard scheduling software and reports, Microsoft Office Suite
Valid Driver’s license with a clean driving record and Completion of OSHA 30 or equivalent safety training.
Trench Safety Training
Have a background in underground installation of piping, trench and excavating experience, and underground boring experience.

External work environments

Fit and move in confined spaces including tanks and vessels
Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors

Climbing up and down stairs and ladders to both get in and out of trenches and up to elevated platforms (scaffolding at significant heights)
Lifting necessary equipment and materials 1-50 pounds
If driving is required, valid driver license and proof of insurability is required. All drivers are subject to a DMV background records search

title: Telecom Revit Designer - Data Centers
location: Austin, TX; Dallas, TX; Denver, CO; Fort Worth, TX; Lincoln, NE; Minneapolis, MN; Omaha, NE; Remote
description:
Company Description

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.
Job Description
As a Telecom Revit Designer on Olsson’s Data Center team, you’ll support the design of low‑voltage, telecommunications, security, and audio/visual systems within complex data center environments. You’ll work in a collaborative, fast‑paced setting alongside experienced designers and engineers, helping deliver high‑quality technical solutions for mission‑critical facilities.
Key responsibilities:

Use CAD/BIM tools to support cable routing, equipment layouts, and communications system design.
Assist with telecom, security, and A/V system layouts, including MDF/IDF/Demarc rooms and horizontal cabling design.
Contribute to project design tasks under the guidance of senior team members.
Support coordination efforts across disciplines to maintain accuracy and design consistency.
Participate in client discussions, reinforcing Olsson’s commitment to quality and partnership.
Complete occasional site visits to support field verification and project progress.

Qualifications

You are passionate about:

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

You bring to the team:

Strong communication and teamwork skills
Solid interpersonal and problem‑solving abilities
Associate degree in Drafting/Design (preferred)
3+ years of CAD/BIM experience; Revit proficiency is a plus
Experience with Cellular DAS, PSDAS, ROIP, or ERRCS (nice to have)
Interest in developing stronger telecom design skills, including complex drawing layout and industry standards
Interest in pursuing RCDD certification in the future

#LI-DNP

Actual compensation will vary based on factors such as experience, qualifications, geographic location, skills, education, and internal equity.

The typical annual salary range for this role is as listed below. Compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience, and qualifications. Employees in this role may be eligible for our performance‑based bonus and merit increases.
 National Pay Range$21—$43 USDAdditional Information
Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.
As an Olsson employee, you will:

Receive a competitive 401(k) match
Be empowered to build your career with tailored development paths
Have the possibility for flexible work arrangements

title: Principal Mechanical Engineer (Starship)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.PRINCIPAL MECHANICAL ENGINEER (STARSHIP)
Our elite Starbase team is working on our planet's toughest and most audacious project: making humanity multi-planetary. The mechanical engineer is responsible for designing and building flight hardware such as propellant tanks, integration interfaces, primary structures, and structural subassemblies. You will be empowered to make real-time decisions, solve complex problems on the fly, and own end-to-end processes. The role will require the readiness to develop subject matter expertise in design for manufacturability, specifically those related to sheet metal and subassembly design and fabrication. If you are ready to be a hardware owner, eager to get out from behind a desk, and be hands-on working alongside a world-class production team, this may be the right role for you.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Develop design concepts from a clean sheet and size vehicle structures based on flight loads
Collaborate with peers from different vehicle systems to develop designs that balance mass, cost, and capability
Create detailed designs to implement structural concepts and generate CAD models in NX for components, assemblies, and vehicle integration
Build finite element models to assess your designs in detail and analyze your structures to prove they meet the needs of the vehicle
Apply first-order hand calculations and empirical formulas to assess and iterate on your designs rapidly
Validate your designs by building development articles to test individual joints and design elements for strength
Perform structural testing on subassemblies and full sections of the airframe
Partner with build engineers and technicians to improve your designs
Support the assembly of your hardware in the factory, witness your designs being brought to life daily, and watch them take flight and make history

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree in an engineering discipline
7+ years of experience with mechanical design and analysis

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Experience designing, analyzing, building, and testing high performance, mechanical systems
Experience working within interdisciplinary teams to develop solutions to challenging and complex problems
Experience with FEA or multiphysics simulation package (e.g. NASTRAN, ABAQUS, ANSYS)
Experience designing and executing qualification testing
Strong understanding of mechanical first principles and structural analysis methodologies
Proficiency in selecting materials and manufacturing methods for mechanical components
Analytical/scientific programming experience (i.e. Python, Matlab, Excel)
Self-motivated with strong organizational, written, and oral communication skills

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Ability to work extended hours and weekends as necessary
Stand: Up to 3 hours per day
Sit: Up to 6 hours per day
Push/Pull: Up to 50lbs. (unassisted) Up to 15 minutes per day
Overhead reach: Up to 3 hours per day
Walk: Up to 3 hours per day
Lift/Carry: Up to 25lbs. (unassisted) Up to 15 minutes per day
Climb (ladder/stairs): Up to 1 hour per day
Kneel/Crouch: N/A
Upper body twist: N/A
Ability to work in temperatures over 80 degrees: up to 30 minutes per day
Candidate must be capable of safely working at heights (up to 500ft), in confined spaces, using an air purifying respirator, and performing the physical requirements of the job listed in the job description
Candidate may be required to complete a pre-employment questionnaire and/or physical to confirm these capabilities, which may include a medical history review
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Mechanical Engineer (Data Center MEP Systems)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.SR. MECHANICAL ENGINEER (DATA CENTER MEP SYSTEMS)
SpaceX is looking for an MEP Engineer with deep mechanical and plumbing expertise to design, specify, and commission the cooling and fluid systems that keep our data center infrastructure running. This role sits at the intersection of critical facilities engineering and the physical plant — you’ll be equally comfortable in a design review and walking a mechanical room during startup.
RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Design and specify mechanical cooling systems for data center facilities: chilled water plants, CRAH/CRAC units, air handling units, and cooling towers
Own plumbing system design: domestic water, sanitary, storm drainage, makeup water, and process piping for cooling systems
Evaluate and specify facility liquid cooling infrastructure (direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchangers, immersion cooling)
Perform heat load calculations, airflow modeling, and capacity planning to ensure design requirements are met
Develop piping design, pump sizing, and hydraulic calculations for chilled water and condenser water loops
Review and coordinate mechanical/plumbing drawings with architectural, electrical, structural, and fire protection disciplines
Support commissioning of mechanical systems: functional performance testing, integrated systems testing (IST), and level 5 commissioning for critical cooling infrastructure
Work directly with equipment vendors (chillers, CRAH units, pumps, cooling towers) on technical specifications and factory witness testing
Troubleshoot operational issues in existing facilities — water treatment, pump cavitation, control valve failures, capacity shortfalls
Support due diligence and technical evaluation for new site selection, including utility water availability and existing mechanical infrastructure condition

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:  

Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering or related discipline
10+ years of experience in mechanical/plumbing design for mission-critical facilities, data centers, or comparable industrial environments

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

Working knowledge of HVAC and hydronic system design: chilled water plants, cooling towers, air handling systems
Experience with plumbing system design and code compliance (domestic water, sanitary, storm drainage)
Ability to read and produce mechanical/plumbing construction documents, P&IDs, and equipment schedules
Direct data center design or operations experience, ideally at hyperscale or colocation facility scale
Experience with liquid cooling technologies: direct-to-chip, rear-door heat exchangers, or immersion cooling systems
Familiarity with Uptime Institute Tier standards and ASHRAE TC9.9 data center thermal guidelines
Commissioning experience, including functional performance testing (FPT) and integrated systems testing (IST)
Experience with water treatment systems and makeup water strategy for evaporative cooling systems
Knowledge of relevant codes: ASHRAE 90.1, IPC/UPC plumbing codes, NFPA where applicable
Experience working alongside electrical and controls engineers to ensure integrated BMS/EPMS operation
Comfort working in a fast-moving environment where facility capacity has to keep pace with compute deployment schedules

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on site operational needs; flexibility required
Willingness to travel to job sites during construction, commissioning, and critical operational events
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. location: Dallas, Texas, United States; Des Moines, Iowa, United States; Houston, Texas, United States; Omaha, Nebraska, United States
description:
DLR Group is an integrated design firm with a promise to elevate the human experience through design. This fuels the work we do around the world and inspires our mission to improve the lives of our clients, our communities, and our planet. If this sparks your interest, you’re in the right place.Our Reality Capture team has an opening for a Reality Capture Technician / Architectural BIM Technician. This role could be based in the following studios:

Dallas
Des Moines
Houston
Omaha

About Reality Capture at DLR Group
The Reality Capture team utilizes a combination of lidar 3D scans, photogrammetry, photographs, and construction documents to create 3D models that elevate accuracy and safety throughout the lifecycle of our projects. Reality capture delivers ultra-precise documentation that captures details invisible to traditional methods. From historic preservation to commercial development, reality capture accelerates design phases and reduces costs.
Position Summary
As a Reality Capture Technician / Architectural BIM Technician, you will use advanced technology to quickly develop digital models of existing buildings and spaces. This is a role where attention to detail is a must, as the deliverable is leveraged by DLR Group design teams or clients. Utilizing Revit, Capture, and visualization software, you will translate LiDAR or photogrammetry data into 3D BIM models or other deliverables.
DLR Group is 100% employee owned and as such you’ll enjoy the opportunity to have ownership in the Firm. We rely on all our employee-owners to apply their financial acumen to grow the Firm profitably. 
What You Will Do

Communicate effectively with the Reality Capture team
Prepare high-quality 3D models, drawings, or similar deliverables
Perform Revit modeling from 3D point clouds
Work in a fast-paced team environment to complete tasks accurately and efficiently
Coordinate with architects and engineers on various projects
Understand and follow DLR Group and client-standard BIM procedures for model setup, as well as standard drawing procedures for sheet layout
Learn advanced Revit techniques and advanced technology topics
Meet critical deadlines through efficient time management
Communicate effectively with design teams
Work with the Reality Capture team to leverage advanced technology

Required Qualifications

2-3 years of Revit-related professional experience
Understanding of building components
Ability to manage and develop Revit families
Working knowledge of construction documentation, with the ability to develop models that are usable for design, documentation, and scheduling
Ability to plan daily activities to meet production requirements
Flexibility to work with numerous project teams to support project completion
Associate degree or currently pursuing an associate degree in Engineering Technology, Architectural Engineering, Computer-Aided Drafting, or a related field
Must be eligible to work in the United States without need for work visa or residency sponsorship

Visa sponsorship is not offered for this position, including temporary visas such as E, F-1 (including OPT and CPT), TN, J, H-1B, or those who need employment-based visa sponsorship now or in the future.

description_html:
About Fluidstack

We exist to make humanity more free. For most of human history, you farmed or you starved. Technology gave people more time for the things they wanted to do, instead of things they had to do. Powerful AI will be the biggest lever for human choice we've ever built - but only if models are aligned with what humanity actually wants. There are groups building AI who don't share these goals. Whoever deploys frontier compute infrastructure fastest will decide whether AI expands human freedom or shrinks it.

We're singularly focused on delivering 10 to 100s of GWs of compute faster than anyone else, rethinking every layer of the stack. We acquire power, design and build data centers, and operate them - with teams spanning hardware and software. Speed and scale are our key differentiators. Come be a part of building civilization-scale infrastructure for AI.


We hire people who care deeply about this problem space. If that is you, please apply!

How We Operate

  • Be a barrel. Full autonomy. Own things end to end, take on scope without being asked, no permission required to operate outside your core role.

  • Insane urgency. We drive everything forward as fast as possible.

  • Reason from first principles. Challenge every assumption. Zero analogy thinking, no egos, the best idea wins.

  • Love of the game. The frontier of AI is the most interesting problem of our time. We put in long hours at high intensity to push the frontier forward.

  • Build something that actually matters. If you're going to spend your time, spend it on something that matters to the world.

The Capacity Delivery Team

Examples of key problems the team is working on

  • Engineer gigawatts from drawing to energized, in months not years. Capacity Delivery owns technical execution across every build: the drawings, the field questions, and the engineering calls that keep multiple concurrent gigawatt sites moving.

  • Engineer data centers that go up in months, not years. At that pace rework is not an option: problems get caught on paper or they cost a data hall.

  • Design it once, build it a hundred times. Every site's lessons roll into the reference design on the way to 10s to 100s of GWs, so each build starts ahead of the last.

Role Scope

  • Own controls engineering for assigned sites: BMS and EPMS design review, integration oversight, and commissioning support.

  • Review controls submittals against the standard: architecture, points, sequences, graphics.

  • Oversee integrator programming quality before it reaches the field.

  • Support Level 3 through 5 commissioning with engineering answers in hours.

What We're Looking For

  • The below is a starting point. We always make space for exceptional people, so if you don't fit this role exactly, tell us where you would.

  • You've engineered building or industrial controls on mission critical projects.

  • You read and write sequences of operations.

  • You've reviewed integrator work and sent it back with specifics.

  • You debug controls issues from the points list up.

  • Bonus: Niagara or Ignition. EPMS platforms. Networking for controls. Commissioning experience.

We are committed to pay equity and transparency.

Fluidstack is an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability and protected veterans’ status, or any other characteristic protected by law. Fluidstack will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records pursuant to applicable law.

You will receive a confirmation email once your application has successfully been accepted. If there is an error with your submission and you did not receive a confirmation email, please email careers@fluidstack.io with your resume/CV, the role you've applied for, and the date you submitted your application-- someone from our recruiting team will be in touch.

title: Concrete Carpenter
description:
At Keeley Companies, we believe in empowering our people and fulfilling career aspirations. Keeley is a career destination with countless opportunities for advancement, and a world-class family culture that is centered around creating the best possible environment for our people to thrive. 

Keeley Construction is seeking an experienced Concrete Carpenter to join our construction team, with a strong emphasis on striping expertise.
Job Responsibilities
 
Concrete Carpentry Support:

Read and interpret blueprints, drawings, and specifications to determine dimensions and materials needed for concrete formwork.
Build, erect, install, and repair concrete forms and structures using wood, metal, or other materials.
Measure, cut, and shape wood, plastic, or other materials to create precise formwork for concrete pouring.
Construct and set forms for foundations, walls, columns, stairs, and other concrete structures.
Ensure proper alignment, leveling, and bracing of forms to meet specifications and ensure stability.
Install expansion joints and embedded items in concrete structures as specified.
Strip and dismantle formwork after concrete has sufficiently cured.
Maintain and care for equipment, tools, and materials used in concrete carpentry and striping work.
Check completed formwork for quality, stability, and compliance with specifications.
Apply curing compounds or perform additional concrete finishing tasks as needed.

Qualifications

High school diploma or equivalent.
2+ years of experience in concrete formwork and carpentry.
Proven ability to read and interpret construction blueprints and specifications.
Experience with various forming systems (traditional wood forms, modular systems, etc.).
Proficiency with carpentry tools and equipment specific to concrete work.
Strong understanding of concrete properties and curing requirements.
Knowledge of proper forming techniques for various concrete elements.
Strong attention to detail, accuracy, and precision.

All candidates must agree to complete a skills assessment and pre‑employment drug screen.EOE/AA M/F/Disabled/Vet

description:

Lead Superintendent (Structural Concrete)
 
Our North Texas Civil Group is seeking a seasoned Lead Superintendent with proven expertise in structural concrete construction. This leader will oversee large-scale, self-performed concrete operations and complex civil projects, managing everything from site logistics and crew leadership to quality control and schedule execution. The ideal candidate has successfully led structural concrete scopes including foundations, footings, drilled piers, retaining walls, cast-in-place structures, rebar installation, formwork, and major concrete placement activities while maintaining a strong commitment to safety, operational excellence, and client satisfaction.
 
Primary Responsibilities

Responsible for managing overall project safety management and compliance with the applicable company safety expectations, rules, and regulations.
Responsible for overall success and management of all assigned projects.
Confer with Preconstruction Services during the preparation of estimates regarding methods, systems, schedule, and general conditions.
Lead and oversee field meetings including safety, coordination, and schedule meetings.
Enforce compliance with project procedures, safety program requirements, work rules and client requirements.
Document all violations, notify Project Management personnel, and recommend/implement corrective actions as required.
Provide performance feedback for project team members.
Manage the coordination of onsite subcontractors and their work.
Provide technical assistance, interpretation of drawings, and recommendation of construction methods and equipment installation.
Support Project Management Personnel with overseeing and directing construction progress tracking and forecasting.
Read, interpret, and understand controls and instrumentation drawings, specification, and commercial documents.
Complete all other duties as assigned.

Minimum Qualifications

About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries, and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.
 
Job SummaryLoenbro is looking for a dedicated and hardworking Construction Laborers / Helpers to join our team. The ideal candidate will assist in various construction tasks, ensuring projects are completed safely and efficiently. This is a physically demanding role that requires mindfulness and the ability to work well in a team.
Essential Job Responsibilities

Assist with the setup and cleanup of construction sites.
Load and unload materials and equipment.
Operate hand and power tools under supervision.
Dig trenches, backfill excavations, and compact soil.
Assist with the installation of construction materials, such as pipes, concrete, and steel.
Follow safety protocols and maintain a clean work area.

Minimum Qualifications
Required:

GED or High School Diploma.
Ability to work from ladders and scaffolds.
Lift & carry objects and materials of various weights. 

Preferred:

Skilled in math which includes adding and subtracting fractions.
Able to pass preliminary and periodic drug testing.

Physical Demands and Work Environment
The physical demands and work environment described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodation may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
Work Environment:

Potential exposure to extreme cold and hot temperatures.
Manufacturing, pipeline, and refining environment.
Fit and move in confined spaces including tanks and vessels.
Limited working surfaces.
Exposure to noise above 85 decibels and intense odors.
Exposure to areas with limited visibility.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

Job Summary:
This position is responsible for welding on industrial and construction projects, ensuring safety, quality, and timely completion of work. The Welder will work closely with the Foremen/Superintendent to ensure project goals are met. The role involves unloading, stacking, and organizing steel materials, erecting structural steel, and performing welding tasks on construction sites. Additionally, may assist with minor mechanical repairs or installations. Requires the ability to operate heavy equipment such as manlifts, forklifts, etc.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

 Safety
 Follow all safety policies and procedures on the job site.
 Attend daily safety meetings and toolbox talks with the crew.
 Identify and address potential safety hazards immediately.
 Ensure use of required PPE.
 Key Responsibilities:
 Ensure all work is performed to the highest quality standards and in accordance with project specifications and industry best practices.
 Maintain accurate records of work performed, including daily logs and material usage.
 Coordinate with other trades on the job site.
 Work with Foremen to troubleshoot and resolve any on-site issues that may arise.
 Maintain a clean and organized work area.
 Ensure all welds meet required standards and specifications.
 Identify and correct any defects or deficiencies.

Qualifications:

Minimum 2 years of experience as an Iron Worker/Welder.
Strong knowledge of ironworking and welding techniques, including layout and erection.
Experience with a variety of welding processes (e.g., 3G, 4G, SMAW).
Excellent safety record and a strong commitment to safety.
Strong communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a team.
Ability to problem-solve and make quick decisions.
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation.
OSHA 10 or 30 certification preferred.
First Aid/CPR certification preferred.
Ability to travel outside of AZ

Physical Demands:

Ability to lift and up to 75 pounds.
Ability to work in various weather conditions.
Ability to stand, bend stretch and climb for extended periods.
Ability to work at heights.

This role requires compliance with all applicable safety regulations, personal protective equipment (PPE) requirements, and Loenbro's Environmental Health and Safety (EH&S) policies.

401(k) retirement plan with company match

Life and disability insurance 

Professional development and training opportunities

title: Data Center Construction- Project Manager

It’s an exciting time to join MGAC!
MGAC is a global boutique consultancy dedicated to managing and representing our clients’ best interests. Our success is rooted in hiring exceptional people who are driven to do challenging work with the unique blend of experience, integrity, creativity, and commitment that separates us from our competitors.
We have three simple goals: to do the most interesting and challenging work, to have fun working together, and to build a successful business in the process.
This position requires local support, with approximately 4-5 days per week onsite in Corpus Christi, TX subject to client needs.

Unlock Your Potential
We’re looking for candidates eager to take ownership of challenging projects and grow their careers. Here’s what will set you up for success at MGAC:

5+ years of experience in construction project management with a thorough understanding of the building design and construction process.

2+ years of experience managing critical environment construction projects (e.g., data centers, labs, hospitals).

Ambitious, construction and project management-focused, and seeking a modern and energetic business that will empower you to grow your career.

30 years strong in North America and growing fast—with a positive, energizing culture.

Consistently recognized as a Top Workplace with a true employee-first mindset.

Entrepreneurial spirit encouraged—bring fresh ideas and exceed client expectations.

Global reach, yet agile and client-focused like a boutique firm.

Your voice matters—flat structure, open doors, and recognition for your contributions.

Recognized as a Top Workplace for over a decade.

Vacation starts on day one—accrue 3 weeks per year, plus a paid birthday off.

8 sick days and 10 paid holidays annually for full-time employees.

Competitive benefits that support both personal and professional growth.

$120,000 - $150,000 per year (commensurate with experience)

description:
Overview


Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Mechanical Engineer, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. 

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter professionals working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

A demonstrated desire and capability to learn, grow, and develop new skills 
Empower a culture of safety, security, and compliance in all aspect of data center activities  
Understand the design and functionality of your datacenter  
Work alongside a team of industry professionals across the Information Technology (IT) and Critical Environments (CE) spectrum to support 24x7x365 on-site datacenter operations and mechanical infrastructures.  
Act as the technical authority for on-site operations of large-scale mechanical systems and designs. 
Collaborate with the Operations and Design team to develop data center (DC) mechanical designs, starting from project conception to issue for construction (IFC) for new DC projects build outs and major infrastructure upgrades. 
Establish and coordinate maintenance & safety procedures, maintaining redundant high-capacity cooling systems; to operating and supporting datacenter backup electrical systems (diesel generators, rotary UPS, etc.) 
Steward vital infrastructure supporting deployments of Microsoft's online services.  
Assist with supplier selection and overseeing mechanical supplier execution 
Learn, live, and coach the One Microsoft culture and values.? Lead through change by bringing clarity, generating energy, and delivering success 


Qualifications


Required Qualifications:

Master's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 1+ year(s) related technical engineering experience OR Bachelor's Degree in Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 2+ years related technical engineering experience OR equivalent experience.

Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

8+ years related technical engineering experience

OR equivalent experience.
