title: Controls Project Manager
description:
Texas AirSystems has been shaping the HVAC landscape in Texas for over four decades. With 500+ team members and seven offices statewide, we partner with over 60 leading manufacturers to deliver custom, high-performance solutions that stand the test of time.
Here, your work matters. You’ll be part of a team that values collaboration, rewards curiosity, and gives you the tools to keep growing. Whether you’re just getting started or looking for your next big challenge, this is a place where you can thrive and make a real impact.The Opportunity
We are seeking an experienced HVAC DDC BAS Controls Project Manager will work as part of a team which will be responsible for the installation, programming, start-up, troubleshooting, commissioning and servicing of DDC building automation systems. This position requires the ability to communicate clearly with customers, mechanical contractors, mechanical engineers and fellow employees.
Responsibilities

Manage installation subcontractor during construction phase of project to keep them on track and on schedule.
Manage the checkout, start-up and commissioning on BAS projects.
Schedule Programmer and Technicians after install is finished to program and commission project.
Must have excellent computer skills and be proficient in MS Word, MS Excel, MS Project and IP networks.
Review and correct submittal documents for BAS projects.
Create monthly AIA forms for progressive billings.
Work with customers to establish successful project schedule.
Attend jobsite meetings to discuss BAS progress and any issues holding up our progress.
Document all construction issues that handle project completion.
Analyze problems and resolve issues to ensure the complete system functions properly.
Review and correction of submittal documentation for new BAS projects.
Must be familiar with various hand and power tools.
Coordinate customer-training and complete closeout documents
Provide technical support and direction to end-users and employees when applicable.

The Required Profile

5 years of experience as a Project Manager on HVAC Building Automation Systems, LON, BACnet, and Niagara Tridium.
Some flexibility to work overtime/weekends.
Proficient in reading plans, submittal drawings and wiring diagrams.
Both written and verbal communication skills a must.
General understanding of IP networks.
Occasional travel may be required.
5 Years of Project Management with Tridium, Lonworks and BACnet Control Systems
High School Diploma, Military Service, and/or Trade School
Valid driver’s license with clean driving history.
Niagara Tridium AX and N4, familiar with Siemens Talon, and/or Distech Controls.

Other Skills & Abilities
Language SkillsAbility to read and comprehend simple instructions, short correspondence, and memos. Ability to write correspondence. Ability to effectively present information in one-on-one and small group situations to customers, clients, and other employees of the organization.
Mathematical SkillsAbility to add, subtract, multiply, and divide in all units of measure, using whole numbers, common fractions, and decimals. Ability to compute rate, ratio, and percent and to draw and interpret graphs.Reasoning AbilityAbility to apply common sense understanding to carry out instructions furnished in written, oral, or diagram form. Ability to deal with problems involving several concrete variables in standardized situations. Mental stamina for problem solving and prioritizing multiple tasks.
Environmental Requirements
Will be required to work in a field environment, multiple customer sites on a daily basis.
Physical Demands
While performing the duties of this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands to operate computer keyboard reach with hands and arms. The employee frequently is required to stand, walk, and sit. The employee is continually required to climb or balance and stoop, kneel, crouch, or crawl. The employee must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, frequently lift and/or move up to 75 pounds. Specific vision abilities required by this job include close vision, distance vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and ability to adjust focus.

title: HVAC Controls Specialist Supervisor
description:
Texas AirSystems has been shaping the HVAC landscape in Texas for over four decades. With 500+ team members and seven offices statewide, we partner with over 60 leading manufacturers to deliver custom, high-performance solutions that stand the test of time.
Here, your work matters. You’ll be part of a team that values collaboration, rewards curiosity, and gives you the tools to keep growing. Whether you’re just getting started or looking for your next big challenge, this is a place where you can thrive and make a real impact.The Opportunity
The Controls Specialist Supervisor serves as a senior technical leader and people manager within the Controls organization, responsible for overseeing the execution of complex Building Automation System (BAS) projects while leading and developing a team of Controls Specialists and Technicians.  This role combines advanced technical expertise with supervisory responsibility to ensure high-quality project delivery, standardization of best practices, and continuous development of team capability.  The Controls Specialist Supervisor acts as a key escalation point for technical issues and plats a critical role in aligning field execution with operational and business objectives. 
Responsibilities
Technical Leadership & Project Oversight:

Oversee and support the execution of large-scale, multi-system BAS projects from initiation through commissioning and closeout.
Architect and review control strategies, sequences of operation, and system designs for complex applications.
Provide advanced diagnostics, troubleshooting, and system optimization support across projects.
Serve as the primary escalation point for complex technical challenges.

Team Leadership & Development

Supervise, coach, and develop a team of Controls Specialists and Technicians.
Conduct performance management activities, including goal setting, feedback, and development planning.
Support hiring, onboarding, and training of new team members.
Foster a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Commissioning & Quality Assurance

Ensure commissioning activities are executed effectively and systems meet design specifications and customer expectations.
Drive quality standards across all projects, ensuring consistency in programming, installation, and system performance.
Identify opportunities for system improvements, energy efficiency, and operational optimization.

Standardization & Continuous Improvement

Establish and enforce best practices, technical standards, and programming consistency across the Controls team.
Lead initiatives to improve processes, tools, and methodologies to enhance operational efficiency and scalability.

Preconstruction & Cross-Functional Collaboration

Partner with Sales and Engineering teams to support estimating, design reviews, and project planning.
Provide technical guidance on system architecture, integration strategies, and project feasibility.
Collaborate with Operations to align field execution with project schedules and financial objectives.

The Required Profile

Advanced expertise in DDC programming, controls architecture, and BAS design.
Strong experience with multi-protocol integration, including BASnet, Modbus, and LonWorks.
Advanced knowledge of IP networking and troubleshooting within BAS environments.
Experience with energy analytics, system optimization, and performance tuning.
Deep understanding of HVAC mechanical systems and their interaction with control systems.
6 – 10+ years of experience in Building Automation Systems (BAS/BMS).
Prior experience in a lead, supervisory, or project leadership role preferred.
Demonstrated ability to lead complex BAS projects and mentor technical teams.
Recognized as a technical subject matter expert in controls systems.
Relevant certifications or experience with BAS platforms such as Niagara, Distech, or similar preferred.

Work Environment
This position operates in a combination of office and field environments, with regular visits to construction sites, customer facilities, and mechanical rooms.  The role requires collaboration with cross-functional teams, including Sales, Engineering, and Field Operations.  Work environments may include exposure to varying temperatures, noise levels, and industrial conditions.  Adherence to safety protocols and use of personal protective equipment (PPE) is required during site visits.  Occasional travel may be required to support project execution and team oversight.
Physical Demands
The physical demands described here are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this job:

Regularly required to stand, walk, and navigate active job sites for extended periods.
Frequent use of hands and fingers to operate tools, equipment, and computer systems.
Ability to climb ladders, access rooftops, and work within mechanical rooms or confined spaces.
Must be able to lift and carry materials or equipment up to 25 – 50 pounds as needed.
Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, and reach to inspect, troubleshoot, or support installation of control systems.
Visual acuity required to read technical documents, wiring diagrams, and digital displays.
May require extended periods of driving to and from job sites and customer locations.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employee may perform other related duties as negotiated to meet the ongoing needs of the organization.
Employment practices will not be influenced or affected by an applicant’s or employee’s race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, veteran status or any other legally protected status.  Reasonable accommodations will be made for qualified individuals with disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship.
Salary ranges listed are dependent upon a candidate’s qualifications, experience, internal equity, and the budgeted amount for the specific role and location.

The physical demands described here are representative of those required to successfully perform the essential functions of this job:

  • Regularly required to stand, walk, and navigate active job sites for extended periods.
  • Frequent use of hands and fingers to operate tools, equipment, and computer systems.
  • Ability to climb ladders, access rooftops, and work within mechanical rooms or confined spaces.
  • Must be able to lift and carry materials or equipment up to 25 – 50 pounds as needed.
  • Ability to bend, stoop, kneel, and reach to inspect, troubleshoot, or support installation of control systems.
  • Visual acuity required to read technical documents, wiring diagrams, and digital displays.
  • May require extended periods of driving to and from job sites and customer locations.

title: Fueling Facilities Technician (Starship)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.FUELING FACILITIES TECHNICIAN (STARSHIP)
The Fueling Facilities Technician is a highly skilled and respected professional responsible for the maintenance, troubleshooting, and operational efficiency of fueling systems supporting Starship fleet operations. This role supports the Starship fleet maintenance team across a variety of fleet assets, including vehicles, heavy equipment, ground support equipment, generators, and related fuel storage and transfer systems. This role requires advanced technical expertise, leadership, and coordination across multiple teams to ensure mission-critical operations are executed flawlessly. The technician is a proactive leader who drives safety, mentors team members, and implements innovative solutions to enhance team performance and system reliability. SpaceX doesn’t shut down production for maintenance, and instead, we find ways to predict failures and perform the maintenance without interrupting production. This role will require direct work with the engineers and technicians who design and build unique machines and perform risk analysis together to map out the maintenance strategy and find the best condition monitoring systems to monitor the performance.
RESPONSIBILITIES

Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair fueling systems, pumps, dispensers, filtration, and transfer equipment across a variety of fleet assets, ensuring team proficiency in these areas
Implementing process improvements and physical upgrades to improve reliability of fueling operations
Execute fueling, defueling, and emergency procedures for fleet vehicles, ground support equipment, and related systems
Create basic and complex work orders from scratch for fueling assemblies and support equipment
Provide preventative and corrective maintenance on fuel storage, transfer, filtration, and dispensing systems
Develop complex rework work order dispositions, including custom hardware installs without design references and functional/leak checks post-rework
Drive fuel trucks, forklifts, and other company equipment
Design and create specialized tooling to complete projects or tasks
Trains and mentors the operations team to ensure fleet operators are capable of self-diagnosing, troubleshooting, and performing common fueling and repair tasks

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
2+ years of experience with fueling operations, fuel system service, or fleet maintenance

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

Able to adapt to constantly changing work assignments and fast-paced work environment
Excellent concentration and attention to detail with outstanding work efficiency and accuracy
Work in compliance with the applicable SpaceX and industry standards and regulations
Understanding of hazardous materials handling, fuel quality control, and spill prevention best practices
Read and interpret engineering work instructions/drawings and verify that fueling, transfer, and loading/unloading processes are carried out successfully and in accordance with the fueling plan
Proven track record in high-pressure, mission-critical environments
5+ years of experience as a maintenance technician or field service engineer
Experience with CAD and/or mechanical design
Experience operating a forklift, fuel truck, and other related fleet equipment
Ability to read and interpret electrical, hydraulic, and pneumatic schematics and drawings
Ability to write detailed repair reports (advanced MS Office skills)
Ability to use power tools and hand tools as well as heavy equipment
Ability to maintain a safe and clean working environment while adhering to company policies, quality policies, and industry standards
Detail-oriented, organized, and able to demonstrate a high sense of urgency
Analytic thinker who gets to the root of problems and comes up with permanent solutions to remedy issues
Experience in aerospace maintenance, fleet fueling, cryogenic or hazardous commodity transfer, or vehicle assembly operations
Bachelor's degree in a technical discipline

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Must be able to stand for extended periods (8 hours min)
Must be able to travel for short and extended trips as needed
Willing to travel up to 25%
Must be available for all shifts, overtime, and weekends as needed
Capable of lifting up to 50 lbs. unassisted and working at heights
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. You are passionate about:

Working collaboratively with others.

Strong communication skills.

Company Description

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.

Olsson offers clients a full spectrum of water and wastewater services, including a complete line of planning, design, permitting, and construction phase services. Maintaining water quality is Olsson’s number one concern, and we are able to respond to a broad set of client demands in a timely and cost-effective manner. 
The Olsson Water/Wastewater team is looking for an experienced water and/or sewer modeling engineer to perform hydraulic modeling and master planning to meet the client’s needs from conception to completion.  As a modeling engineer, you will perform process design calculations, create population and demand projections, assist with report writing, and attend meetings with the client.
As an Engineer for the Water/Wastewater team, other responsibilities will include providing project design utilizing CAD/modeling software, performing technical analysis, preparing construction documents, providing construction services, performing research, and writing technical reports. You will work closely with other team members and engineers on wastewater collection and treatment projects, along with water supply, storage, treatment, and distribution. Typical tasks you will work on include sanitary sewer piping, wastewater pump stations, wastewater treatment facilities, water piping, water supply wells, water storage tanks, and water treatment facilities. 
Primary responsibilities:

Provides high-level project design and review of project documents and design quality for complex projects.
Serves as a technical specialist, applying advanced engineering concepts and developing approaches to solve for complexities.
Performs QA/QC and ensures delivery of completed designs meets quality standards and project objectives.
Conducts research in areas of considerable scope and complexity.
Advises and directs staff on design approaches to fulfill project requirements.
Works collaboratively to promote efficiencies and produce high quality work.
Contributes to the development of standards and/or guidelines for engineering activities within the team.
Supervises and reviews technical assignments of less experienced staff.  Assists with mentoring and development of junior staff.
Helps to build and maintain strong client relationships, ensuring our projects meet and exceed client expectations.

Qualifications

You are passionate about:

Working collaboratively with others
Having ownership in the work you do
Using your talents to positively affect communities

You bring to the team:

Strong communication skills.
Ability to contribute and work well on a team.
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, planning, or a related field.
Understanding of water and wastewater master planning process.
Solid understanding of open channel and closed pipe hydraulics.

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.

We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.

Job Description

Olsson offers clients a full spectrum of water and wastewater services, including a complete line of planning, design, permitting, and construction phase services. Maintaining water quality is Olsson’s number one concern, and we are able to respond to a broad set of client demands in a timely and cost-effective manner. 

The Olsson Water/Wastewater team is looking for an experienced water and/or sewer modeling engineer to perform hydraulic modeling and master planning to meet the client’s needs from conception to completion.  As a modeling engineer, you will perform process design calculations, create population and demand projections, assist with report writing, and attend meetings with the client.

As an Engineer for the Water/Wastewater team, other responsibilities will include providing project design utilizing CAD/modeling software, performing technical analysis, preparing construction documents, providing construction services, performing research, and writing technical reports. You will work closely with other team members and engineers on wastewater collection and treatment projects, along with water supply, storage, treatment, and distribution. Typical tasks you will work on include sanitary sewer piping, wastewater pump stations, wastewater treatment facilities, water piping, water supply wells, water storage tanks, and water treatment facilities.

title: Sr. Construction Safety Engineer (Terafab)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.SR. ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH & SAFETY ENGINEER, CONSTRUCTION SAFETY (TERAFAB)
We are building Terafab, a vertically integrated semiconductor factory at an unprecedented scale. The facility houses logic, memory, packaging, test, and lithography mask production under one roof, optimized for rapid iteration and maximum compute density per square foot. Additionally, the campus will include power generation and compute testing facilities that will enable fully optimized development, operation, and testing of the fabrication facility and its products.
This position requires a dedicated environmental, health, and safety professional who will be able to use their skill, knowledge, and experience to further our Environmental Health and Safety programs within our fast-paced work environment that includes operations that have never been attempted before. You will bring deep experience in construction safety, preferably with experience in the semiconductor or power generation sectors. You will have the opportunity to work across multiple projects as the site evolves, and success depends on clear communication, strong cross-functional influence, and the ability to operate in a fast-paced, high-change environment.
RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Develop, implement, execute, and improve construction safety and contractor management programs at the Terafab location
Lead daily safety engagements with employees and contractors to drive safe operations across the site
Create, review and approve Purchase Orders and manage the operational budget for construction safety programs
Develop practical solutions that improve construction site safety, reduce incident rates, drive contractor engagement, and advance the overall EHS program
Investigate mishaps and develop sustainable improvement plans to reduce risk
Ensure EHS policies, practices, and procedures are understood and consistently followed by project teams, clients, and contractors
Collaborate with internal project teams and contractors to foster a strong safety culture that focuses on preventing serious incidents
Review and interpret new and proposed safety laws and regulations (with emphasis on construction-related requirements) and provide clear guidance to management
Provide training, coaching, and technical guidance to construction stakeholders on job hazard analyses (JHAs), safe work procedures, contractor onboarding, permits to work, and other key risk management tools to ensure consistent implementation of a robust construction safety program
Hold routine site/operation-wide Contractor Safety Steering Reviews to drive accountability for execution of EHS performance across contractor groups
Perform construction safety compliance audits, pre-task planning reviews, and contractor risk assessments to measure performance and facilitate risk reduction 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

Bachelor’s degree
5+ years of experience in the design, development, and operational oversight of environmental, health, and safety programs with an emphasis on construction safety operations 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

Bachelor of Science in Engineering, Occupational Health & Safety, Construction Management, or related field (emphasis in Construction Safety preferred)
10+ years of experience, preferably in construction safety
Demonstrated strong organizational and communication skills with a clear aptitude and desire to influence people
Hands-on experience leading multi-site or multi-contractor construction safety programs in high-risk or complex environments
Able to review as-built drawings, assess safety-in-design opportunities, and lead technical risk engineering solutions in the design-build environment  
Strong knowledge and experience interpreting, applying, and documenting federal, state, and local construction safety regulations
Experience with fall protection, scaffolding, crane/heavy equipment safety, excavation, confined space, and contractor safety management (including contractor pre-qualification)
Intermediate proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, PowerPoint, Word, Outlook)
Professional certifications such as CSP, CHST, or equivalent preferred 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Must be able to work extended hours, weekends, and travel to construction sites as needed
Must be able to work in outdoor construction environments and wear required personal protective equipment 
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.  

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.

description:

We are building Terafab, a vertically integrated semiconductor factory at an unprecedented scale. The facility houses logic, memory, packaging, test, and lithography mask production under one roof, optimized for rapid iteration and maximum compute density per square foot. Additionally, the campus will include power generation and compute testing facilities that will enable fully optimized development, operation, and testing of the fabrication facility and its products.
This position requires a dedicated safety leader who will be able to use their skill, knowledge, and experience to further our Environmental Health and Safety programs within our fast-paced work environment that includes operations that have never been attempted before. You will bring deep experience in EHS risk assessment, industrial hygiene, environmental compliance, and equipment, process, and construction safety. You will have the opportunity to build and lead a talented team of EHS managers, specialists, and engineers. Success depends on clear communication, strong cross-functional influence, and the ability to operate in a fast-paced, high-change environment. This role may require up to 50% domestic travel.
RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Lead comprehensive EHS programs and operational plans across multiple teams, aligned to business goals and Tesla EHS standards
Set day-to-day priorities and long-range plans for the EHS organization, including EHS managers, specialists, and engineers
Lead EHS risk assessments and drive engineering controls and safeguards that mitigate or eliminate hazards
Coordinate with site leadership to ensure appropriate process safety involvement in department development/modification plans and procedure development
Represent the EHS department at site wide management meetings/briefings
Provide instructional guidance of job assignments, correct procedures and applicable techniques to perform specific skills; ensure accuracy and completion
Ensure mission and values are communicated to the team and are integrated within team goals, objectives, and work tasks
Implement all aspects of an occupational safety program, including processes, programs and documentation outlined by OSHA standards
Evaluate equipment overpressure/overtemperature scenarios and reaction hazards
Coordinate with and serve as the main point of contact for local resource agencies 

BASIC REQUIREMENTS: 

Bachelor’s degree
10+ years of experience in the design, development, and general operational oversight of EHS disciplines
5+ years of progressive EHS management experience

PREFERRED REQUIREMENTS:  

Bachelor's degree in engineering with an emphasis in process safety, chemical engineering, environmental engineering or systems safety engineering
Experience working in semiconductor industry
Experience with design and commissioning of process systems associated with or similar to those used in semiconductor manufacturing
Advanced understanding of industry codes, standards, and practices such as ASME, NFPA, ANSI, IBC/IFC, RAGAGEP, etc.
Strong command of federal and state EHS laws, regulations, and standards applicable to complex manufacturing; Texas experience preferred
Knowledge of quality tools such as lean manufacturing principles, statistical process control, root cause analysis and corrective action, process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA), control plans, and various problem-solving approaches 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

This is not a remote position and will require relocation if not already local to the Anderson / College Station, TX area
Position requires the ability to work extended hours and weekends when needed
Ability to travel up to 50%
Position is subject to pre-employment drug and random drug and alcohol testing

title: Electrical Superintendent - Data Center
description:
Join the Team!
Is technology your passion? Do you want to work with smart, forward-thinking individuals? Do you want to grow in a career you love?
At Align, our professionals are the key to our success. We don’t just hire talent, we invest in exceptional people who are forward-thinking, results-driven, and passionate about what they do. We’re a group of tech-savvy professionals who are motivated by making an impact. Our culture is one of unbounded opportunity that celebrates the passions, skills and ideas of our team—work hard, play hard, be smart!
We believe great communities lead to great companies. That’s why we offer a dynamic workplace where you feel inspired, engaged and innovative. We offer professionals opportunities to train in the leading technologies, make an impact within the industry and acquire valuable new skills whether on client sites or in one of our regional offices.Position Overview
Align is seeking an experienced Electrical Superintendent to oversee onsite electrical installation for data center construction and infrastructure projects. This individual will lead field teams, coordinate subcontractors, and ensure work is completed safely, on schedule, and in accordance with project specifications.
The ideal candidate brings strong electrical construction experience, practical knowledge of power distribution systems, and a proven ability to manage field execution in data centers or other mission-critical environments. This role focuses on electrical power infrastructure, including busway, switchgear, panels, feeders, conduit, grounding, and equipment connections. Structured cabling or telecommunications experience alone does not meet the requirements.

This is a full-time, salaried position, full benefits, paid time off, paid training, and performance-based bonuses.
This position is based in the Dallas-Fort Worth Metroplex area and will work onsite for local data center projects.
Approximately 50% travel outside of the Texas area should be expected at times.

Responsibilities

Lead daily electrical installation activities, coordinating crews, subcontractors, and vendors
Plan manpower, materials, equipment, and work sequencing to support project schedules
Oversee installation of power distribution equipment, busway, RPPs, PDUs, conduit, feeders, grounding, and electrical containment
Review drawings, one-line diagrams, specifications, and submittals to guide field execution
Coordinate with project managers, general contractors, clients, and other trades to resolve installation conflicts
Monitor workmanship and progress, addressing deficiencies and schedule risks early
Maintain daily reports, progress updates, and field documentation; support RFIs, change orders, and as-built updates
Enforce site safety requirements and approved procedures for shutdowns, tie-ins, and work in operational facilities
Coordinate inspections and support testing, commissioning, energization readiness, and project turnover
Manage punch-list completion and ensure installations meet project quality standards

Qualifications

3-5 years of electrical construction experience, including three years in a Superintendent, General Foreman, or comparable field leadership role
Experience leading electrical work in data centers, mission-critical facilities, or complex industrial environments
Strong knowledge of electrical power distribution, equipment installation, conduit, feeders, grounding, and bonding
Ability to interpret electrical drawings, one-line diagrams, specifications, and equipment submittals
Experience supervising crews, coordinating subcontractors, and managing field schedules and resources
Strong communication, organization, problem-solving, and client relationship skills
Familiarity with Procore, Bluebeam, Microsoft Office, or similar project tools

Preferred Qualifications

Journeyman or master electrician license
OSHA 30 certification
Experience with hyperscale or colocation data centers and white space electrical fit-outs
Experience working in live facilities and supporting commissioning, shutdowns, and energization

To support a fair, consistent, and high-quality hiring experience, some interviews may be recorded. These recordings help our team focus fully on the conversation at hand, rather than note-taking, and allow us to better evaluate and improve our recruitment process. Recordings are used solely for internal purposes such as training, quality assurance, and process improvement. Candidates will be informed in advance and asked to provide consent before any recording takes place.

Benefits and Perks:

At Align, we believe that supporting our employees both personally and professionally is key to our success. We offer a competitive benefits package designed to promote health, wellness, financial security, and work-life balance, including:

Comprehensive Medical, Dental, and Vision coverage
Health Savings Account (HSA) and Flexible Spending Account (FSA) options

401(k) plan with a dollar-for-dollar company match at 3% up to an annual maximum of $5k.

Complimentary ClassPass membership to support your health and wellness goals
Generous Paid Time Off (PTO)
Company-paid holidays
Cellphone Reimbursement Program
Floating Holiday to celebrate a day that is meaningful to you
Pre-tax commuter benefits, where applicable
Employee wellness programs, events, and team-building activities
Employee referral program

Align is a premier global provider of technology infrastructure solutions.
Align specializes in designing and deploying technology infrastructure solutions from the data center to the desktop as well as providing managed IT services for clients.
Our professional services team, which includes Data Center Solutions, provide strategic consulting, design, project management, engineering, implementation and support. Our best-in-class Managed Services team provides IT services and cybersecurity advisory for clients within the Alternative Investment industry. Align is a Microsoft Tier 1 Cloud Solutions Provider (CSP) and Gold Partner.
Our client centric approach and passion for driving IT innovation has enabled us to provide tailored solutions and business transformations for over three decades. Leading firms have relied on Align to provide forward-thinking technology strategies that support their current and future business needs.
Our teams have flawless track records of delivering technical solutions and have established long-standing relationships with an impressive client list of both Global 1000 and SMB clients. We work across a diverse list of industries including financial services, life sciences (pharmaceutical and health care), retail, technology, media and telecommunications.
For more information, visit: www.align.com

- 4+ years of commissioning experience

- Experience in industrial or commercial engineering in mission critical facilities including but not limited to: data centers, power generation or oil and gas facilities

description:
Who We Are:
Headquartered in Austin, TX with operations in Kermit and Monahans, TX, Atlas Energy Solutions is the leading provider of high-quality frac sand and innovative logistics solutions to Exploration & Production operators and oil field service providers in the Permian Basin. We are proud of what we do – we have state of the art manufacturing facilities, premium offerings, outstanding customer service, and exceptional work culture and a commitment to giving back to the community.
We’re very excited about what we see in front of us, and we think you will be too – so come join our team and contribute   to our growth!
How You Will Make an Impact:
The I & E Technician is critical to ensuring the Conveyor stays running.  Atlas prides itself on being a technology driven company and a critical piece of that is maintaining our sensors and hardware at the plants. 
Responsibilities:

Calibrate, troubleshoot and repair plant instrumentation, transmitters, analyzers, control valves, switches and relays
Diagnose and correct problems associated with PLC’s and electrical systems & controls.
Plan details of jobs that are assigned.
Ability to use blueprints, sketches and complex drawings.
Tools used by I&E technicians include oscilloscopes, signal generators, voltmeters, multimeters, and high and low voltage detectors.
Inspect, troubleshoot, and maintain process control systems such as Control Logix PLC’s, analog and discrete IO devices, and Ethernet IP communications.
Ability to troubleshoot intelligent motor starters with E300 communication modules
Ability to troubleshoot Allan Bradley lines of PowerFlex VFDs and Allan Bradley Soft Starts

Qualifications:

Ability to work in a manufacturing environment both indoors and outdoors.
Previous experience working with electronic communication devices such as oscilloscopes, signal generators, voltmeters, multimeters, and high and low voltage detectors.
Experience reading product manuals and troubleshooting equipment.
Ability to calibrate a wide array of sensors and detectors.

What You’ll Love About Us:

title: Staff Electrical Engineer
description:
Who We Are:Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. (NYSE: AESI) is a leading solutions provider to the energy industry. Atlas’ portfolio of offerings includes oilfield logistics, distributed power systems, and the largest proppant supply network in the Permian Basin. With a focus on leveraging technology, automation, and remote operations to enhance efficiencies, Atlas is centered around a core mission of improving human beings’ access to hydrocarbons that power our lives and, by doing so, maximizing value creation for our shareholders.
The Staff Electrical Engineer serves as a senior technical authority responsible for system architecture, engineering governance, and complex power system decision-making across the power generation and microgrid portfolio. This role defines scalable, utility-grade electrical solutions, establishes and enforces corporate engineering standards, and resolves high-risk technical challenges that affect multiple projects and long-term system performance. The Staff Electrical Engineer is the final technical authority for generator control and interconnection strategy, represents Atlas to utilities and authorities having jurisdiction, and develops technical capability across the electrical engineering organization.
 Responsibilities
Technical Authority & System Architecture

Serve as the subject matter expert for power systems, generator integration, and electrical controls.
Define and approve electrical system architectures for modular and scalable power plants.
Provide final technical authority for generator control and interconnection strategies.
Lead advanced power system studies and protection philosophies.

Engineering Governance & Standards

Author, approve, and maintain corporate electrical standards, specifications, and design guidelines.
Lead and approve complex construction drawing packages and engineering deliverables.
Support long-range technical planning and CAPEX strategy.

Risk Resolution & External Interface

Lead high-risk commissioning, troubleshooting, and failure investigations, driving issues to root cause and corrective action.
Interface with utilities, authorities having jurisdiction, third-party engineers, and owners’ engineers.
Participate in executive-level safety and technical risk reviews.

Technical Leadership

Mentor Senior Electrical Engineers and guide technical development across teams.
Comply with all Atlas Energy Solutions safety policies, procedures, and site requirements, including NFPA 70E and energy isolation lockout/tagout (LOTO), when working in shop and field environments.
Handle confidential and proprietary information with professionalism and integrity.
Other duties as assigned.

 Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering required
Directly related experience may substitute for education
10–15+ years of experience in power systems engineering, generation, or utility-scale electrical design
Demonstrated leadership in electrical system architecture, generator control and integration, and construction documentation standards
Demonstrated experience authoring and enforcing engineering standards, specifications, or design guidelines
Experience leading power system studies and defining protection philosophies
Proven ability to resolve complex technical challenges and lead failure investigations to root cause
Experience mentoring and developing engineers
Expert technical writing and documentation capability
Strong communication skills, with the ability to represent Atlas to utilities, authorities having jurisdiction, third-party engineers, and executive leadership
Ability to travel to the Atlas corporate office, project field sites, fabrication shops, and customer locations
Valid Driver’s License

Preferred:

Professional Engineering License in TX, NM, WY, or CO, or actively working toward licensure
Expert-level experience with ETAP or SKM Power Tools
Extensive experience developing and enforcing electrical standards and specifications
Experience serving as Engineer of Record or supporting stamped designs
Experience interfacing with utilities and regulatory authorities
Experience with distributed generation, microgrid, islanded, black start, or behind-the-meter power systems
Experience with battery energy storage systems (BESS) or inverter-based resources

 Reporting Relationship:

Reports To: Director of Electrical Engineering
Supervisory Responsibilities:

This position does not have direct supervisory responsibility but may provide mentorship, guidance, training, or work direction to others

 Work Location & Travel Requirements

Location: Austin TX (Remote)
Work Environment: Remote office, with travel to the Atlas corporate office, project field sites, fabrication shops, and customer locations
Travel %: 25%

Schedule/Work Arrangement: Fully remote; Monday through Friday, standard business hours, with flexibility to support project, commissioning, and incident response needs
 Physical Demands:

Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer
Must be able to lift and carry materials, tools, and equipment weighing up to 40 pounds on an occasional basis
Position requires site visits in office, shop, outdoor, and industrial field environments, including areas with uneven surfaces and potential exposure to slips, trips, falls, and other common site hazards
Must be able to walk job sites, climb stairs and ladders as needed, stand for extended periods, and perform field inspections and measurements
Must be able to bend, stoop, reach, and work in or around active construction, fabrication, or operating environments while complying with all applicable safety requirements
Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment, including arc-rated clothing, when working in or around energized equipment
Must be able to travel by air and vehicle to corporate, project, shop, and customer locations

 What You Will Love About Us

Best People and Team. Great Place to Work , Hire Vets, Top Place to Work For – Austin American Statesman
Your Well-Being is a Priority. 100% covered Medical, Dental, and Vision
Invest in Your Future. 401K with company match, immediate vesting
Relax and Recharge. Paid time off (non-rotational roles), 15+ company paid holidays

title: Staff MEP Engineer
description:
Who We Are:Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. (NYSE: AESI) is a leading solutions provider to the energy industry. Atlas’ portfolio of offerings includes oilfield logistics, distributed power systems, and the largest proppant supply network in the Permian Basin. With a focus on leveraging technology, automation, and remote operations to enhance efficiencies, Atlas is centered around a core mission of improving human beings’ access to hydrocarbons that power our lives and, by doing so, maximizing value creation for our shareholders.
The Role:
The Staff MEP Engineer serves as the senior mechanical, electrical, plumbing technical authority for the power generation and microgrid portfolio and provides technical leadership to all mechanical engineers on the team. This role owns mechanical system architecture, engineering governance, and complex technical decision-making for engine-based power plants, spanning fuel gas systems, heat rejection, lubrication, starting air, exhaust and emissions interfaces, and building mechanical systems. The Staff MEP Engineer defines scalable, repeatable mechanical solutions across a multi-project portfolio, establishes and enforces engineering standards, and resolves high-risk technical challenges affecting plant performance, reliability, and schedule.
 Responsibilities

Lead and direct the mechanical,engineering,plumbing engineering team: assign and review work, set technical priorities, establish checking discipline, and develop engineers across concurrent projects.
Serve as Subject Matter Expert for mechanical balance of plant on reciprocating engine power generation, including fuel gas systems, cooling water circuits, lube oil, compressed and starting air, exhaust, and emissions equipment interfaces.
Define and approve mechanical system architectures, equipment arrangements, and plot plans for modular, scalable power plants.
Lead and approve P&IDs, piping and equipment specifications, line and equipment lists, and issue-for-construction mechanical packages.
Author, approve, and maintain corporate mechanical standards, specifications, and design guidelines, driving standardization across the portfolio.
Direct mechanical system studies, including fuel gas hydraulics and pressure regulation, cooling hydraulics and heat rejection, exhaust backpressure, pipe stress, relief and vent design, ventilation and combustion air, and utility consumption.
Own building mechanical scope for engine halls and electrical buildings, including ventilation, HVAC, and fire protection interfaces.
Establish the mechanical basis of design for each project, including site ambient and altitude effects on equipment rating and performance.
Provide final technical authority on vendor mechanical packages (engine auxiliaries, balance-of-plant skids, radiators, emissions systems), including specification, bid evaluation, submittal review, and interface resolution.
Coordinate mechanical interfaces with the engine OEM, EPC contractor, owner's engineer, gas supplier, and authorities having jurisdiction.
Support construction and commissioning: respond to RFIs, disposition field changes, witness critical mechanical testing, and support first fuel gas introduction and engine startup.
Lead high-risk troubleshooting and mechanical failure investigations from root cause through corrective action and standards feedback.
Participate in executive-level safety and technical risk reviews, and support long-range technical planning and capital strategy.
Other duties as assigned.

 Qualifications

Required:

Bachelor of Science in Mechanical Engineering from an accredited program
Licensed Professional Engineer
12 or more years of progressive mechanical engineering experience, including substantial experience with mechanical balance of plant for engine- or turbine-based power generation or comparable heavy industrial facilities
Demonstrated design experience with fuel gas systems (pressure regulation, conditioning, valve trains) and closed-loop cooling and heat rejection systems
Expert working knowledge of ASME codes (including B31.1/B31.3 piping), NFPA standards applicable to engine installations and fuel gas, and applicable mechanical and building codes
Proven ability to take mechanical designs from basis of design through installable, code-compliant construction packages and support them in the field
Experience leading, checking, and developing other engineers
Strong vendor, contractor, and cross-discipline coordination skills, with effective verbal and written communication
Ability and willingness to travel to project sites, including overnight stays
Valid Driver's License

Preferred:

Large reciprocating gas engine platform experience (Caterpillar or similar), including engine auxiliary systems and OEM installation requirements
Experience on islanded, black-start, or behind-the-meter power generation facilities
Gas flow and hydraulic modeling experience supporting pipeline interconnect, metering, and plant distribution design
SCR and emissions control system integration experience
Mechanical failure analysis or root-cause investigation background
Multi-jurisdiction PE registration; Master of Science in Mechanical Engineering

 Work Location & Travel Requirements

Location: Austin, TX with regular travel to West Texas project sites
Work Environment: Office and Field; active construction and industrial plant environments, including work around energized equipment and operating machinery
Travel %: 25-50%, increasing during critical design, construction, and commissioning windows

Physical Demands:

Regular use of hands to handle, finger, and reach tools, test equipment, and materials
Required to stand, walk, bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, and climb as needed, including work at elevation and in confined spaces
Must regularly lift and/or move up to 50 pounds, and heavier items with appropriate assistance or mechanical equipment
Required vision abilities include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus
Must be able to work in and around energized electrical equipment while wearing required personal protective equipment
Must be able to tolerate conditions associated with field and construction environments, including heat, cold, dust, noise, and limited climate control

 What You Will Love About Us

Best People and Team. Great Place to Work , Hire Vets, Top Place to Work For – Austin American Statesman
Your Well-Being is a Priority. 100% covered Medical, Dental, and Vision
Invest in Your Future. 401K with company match, immediate vesting
Relax and Recharge. Paid time off (non-rotational roles), 15+ company paid holidays

We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, genetic information, citizenship status, veteran or military status, or any other characteristic protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.This commitment applies to all aspects of employment, including recruiting, hiring, training, promotion, compensation, benefits, and termination.

description_html:
Crusoe is on a mission to accelerate the abundance of energy and intelligence. As the only vertically integrated AI infrastructure company built from the ground up, we own and operate each layer of the stack — from electrons to tokens — to power the world's most ambitious AI workloads. When you join Crusoe, you join a team that is building the future, faster.

We're in the midst of the greatest industrial revolution of our time. The demand for AI compute is boundless, and power is a bottleneck. We're solving that — with an energy-first approach that makes AI infrastructure better for the world and faster for the people innovating with AI.

We're looking for problem-solving, opportunity-finding teammates with a sense of urgency, who believe in the scale of our ambition and thrive on a path not fully paved — people who want to grow their careers alongside a team of experts across energy, manufacturing, data center construction, and cloud services.

If you want to do the most meaningful work of your career, help our customers and partners advance their AI strategies, and be part of a high-performing team that believes in each other, come build with us at Crusoe.

Position Summary

The Sr. Manager, Facility Operations – Colocation, North America is responsible for ensuring that every colocation provider supporting Crusoe Cloud across North America operates in full alignment with Crusoe Operations Standards. This role owns the operational governance relationship with colocation partners — from standards enforcement and compliance audits to incident management and vendor performance — safeguarding the reliability, safety, and security of the infrastructure that powers Crusoe Cloud. The ideal candidate combines deep mission-critical facilities expertise with strong vendor management skills and is comfortable operating as Crusoe's on-the-ground authority across a distributed, multi-provider colocation footprint.

 

Key Responsibilities

Operations Standards Governance & Compliance

  • Own enforcement of Crusoe Operations Standards across all third-party colocation provider sites supporting Crusoe Cloud in North America.

  • Conduct recurring audits, physical inspections, and documentation reviews of colocation facilities against Crusoe's safety, reliability, security, and environmental standards.

  • Partner with the Global Data Center Operations Standards team to localize and interpret standards in light of NFPA (70/70E/72), NEC, OSHA, and applicable state/provincial and utility interconnection requirements.

  • Own the tracking and timely closure of compliance gaps, audit findings, and corrective action plans (CAPs) in partnership with providers.

Colocation Partner Management

  • Serve as the primary operational point of contact for coordination with each provider's facility operators, engineers, account managers, customer-service teams, and leadership across third-party colocation facilities across North America.

  • Serve as Crusoe’s primary escalation point for maintenance, incidents, outages, service issues, chronic deficiencies, and provider performance.

  • Own provider communications, escalation tracking, action items, and timely resolution of operational issues.

  • Monitor service requests and ensure provider performance meets applicable Master Service Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), and Service Level Agreements (SLAs).

  • Conduct regular site visits, facility walkthroughs, maintenance reviews, operational assessments, and meetings with provider leadership.

  • Review provider staffing models, escalation procedures, preventive-maintenance programs, and emergency-response readiness.

  • Lead governance cadences (monthly/quarterly business reviews) with providers, reviewing SLA performance, uptime, maintenance execution, and standards adherence.

  • Provide operational input into Master Service Agreements, Statements of Work, and SLAs, ensuring Crusoe Operations Standards are contractually reflected.

  • Identify and escalate chronic performance, safety, or compliance issues, including formal partner risk assessments where warranted.

  • Participate in and lead applicable Monthly Business Reviews (MBRs) and Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs) with providers.

Facility & Technical Oversight

  • Review provider electrical, mechanical, fire/life-safety, and physical security systems and operating procedures for alignment with Crusoe standards, with particular attention to high-density GPU compute environments.

  • Oversee commissioning and acceptance testing of new colocation suites, cages, and data halls prior to Crusoe Cloud go-live.

  • Review and approve Methods of Procedure (MOPs) and maintenance schedules for work impacting Crusoe-critical infrastructure.

  • Support capacity planning, power/space utilization tracking, and growth forecasting in partnership with providers and internal Capacity Planning teams.

Incident & Risk Management

  • Own Crusoe’s review of provider root-cause analyses and ensure all corrective and preventive actions are tracked through closure.

  • Maintain a regional risk register for colocation facilities across North America and escalate material risks to senior leadership.

  • Own Crusoe’s operational response and coordinate with colocation providers during incidents, outages, emergencies, and business-continuity events.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Reporting

  • Partner with Data Center Design & Construction, Security, Network/IT, Procurement, and Legal on colocation strategy, standards rollout, and contract renewals.

  • Provide operational due diligence and standards input during evaluation of new colocation partners and markets in North America.

  • Develop and maintain KPI scorecards for colocation provider performance and present regional performance and risk summaries to senior leadership.

  • Champion continuous improvement, sharing lessons learned and best practices with the global Facility Operations and Operations Standards organization.

  • Act as the operational link between third-party providers and Crusoe’s ROC, Cloud, Compute, Hardware, Reliability, Procurement, Legal, and leadership teams.

  • Champion a safety-first culture across the third-party portfolio, including escalating work affecting Crusoe infrastructure when an unacceptable safety or operational risk exists.

 

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Facilities/Mechanical/Electrical Engineering, or related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • 8+ years of experience in mission-critical data center facility operations, including at least 3+ years managing multi-site or colocation-based operations at scale.

  • Strong working knowledge of critical infrastructure systems: UPS, generators, switchgear, CRAC/CRAH and chilled-water cooling, fire/life-safety, and BMS/EPMS platforms.

  • Proven experience managing third-party vendor and colocation relationships, including SLAs, MSAs, and governance cadences.

  • Working knowledge of industry frameworks and standards such as Uptime Institute Tier classifications, ASHRAE thermal guidelines, and ISO 9001/14001/27001/45001.

  • Excellent stakeholder management, audit, and written/verbal communication skills; comfortable presenting risk and performance data to senior leadership.

  • Working knowledge of NFPA (70/70E/72), NEC, OSHA regulations, and North American utility interconnection practices.

  • Familiarity with major North American colocation markets and providers (e.g., Digital Realty, Equinix, QTS, CyrusOne, Aligned).

  • Ability to travel up to 30–50% within the United States and Canada.

 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience supporting GPU-dense, AI/ML, or other high-density compute environments (including liquid cooling deployments).

  • Professional certifications such as Uptime Institute Accredited Tier Specialist (ATS)/Accredited Operations Specialist (AOS), CDCP/CDCS/CDCE, PMP, or Six Sigma.

  • Experience with data center commissioning (Cx) processes and acceptance testing.

  • Prior experience at a hyperscaler, cloud provider, or colocation operator supporting rapid capacity growth.

 

Benefits:

  • Competitive compensation and equity packages

  • Restricted Stock Units

  • Paid time off, paid holidays & leave of absence programs

  • Comprehensive health, dental & vision insurance

  • Employer contributions to HSA account

  • Paid parental leave

  • Paid life insurance, short-term and long-term disability

  • Professional development & tuition reimbursement

  • Mental health & wellness support

  • Commuter benefits (parking & transit)

  • Cell phone stipend

  • 401(k) Retirement plan with company match up to 4% of salary

  • Volunteer time off

  • Global travel insurance & emergency assistance

  • Daily meals allowance

  • Additional perks & programs specific to location

     

Compensation Range

Compensation will be paid in the range of up to $175,000-$205,000 + Bonus. Restricted Stock Units are included in all offers. Compensation to be determined by the applicants knowledge, education, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data.

Crusoe is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are made without regard to race, color, religion, disability, genetic information, pregnancy, citizenship, marital status, sex/gender, sexual preference/ orientation, gender identity, age, veteran status, national origin, or any other status protected by law or regulation.

Job Title: EH&S Coordinator II
Company: Loenbro, LLCBusiness Unit/Department: Loenbro Mission Critical - South    Location: Andrews, TXReports to:  EH&S ManagerEmployment Type: Full time

About Loenbro

description_html:
At Rowan Digital Infrastructure, we are transforming data center delivery for speed and scale. Our mission is to deliver best-in-class data center solutions to hyperscale customers who share our commitment to sustainability, and to do so with an unwavering focus on efficiency, quality, and flexibility. Our data center solutions are tailored to our customers’ needs and delivered by our exceptional end-to-end team. Rowan is assembling a strategic portfolio of data center sites in Tier 1 markets across the United States at various stages of development, and we’re looking for incredible and passionate people to help us advance our company and our commitment to building a more sustainable future.

Rowan is backed by Quinbrook, a leading investor in the energy transition, and Blackstone, the world’s largest alternative asset manager.

 

Ready to join us in transforming the future of data centers and sustainability? Apply now to explore exciting career opportunities at Rowan Digital Infrastructure and be a part of our mission to revolutionize data center delivery.

 

Role Summary

The Reliability Engineer - Commissioning will report to the Commissioning Manager and serve as Rowan’s owner-side commissioning representative for the Temple data center portfolio. The Reliability Engineer - Commissioning at Rowan Digital Infrastructure is responsible for ensuring that new data center facilities and expansions are delivered fully commissioned, operationally ready, and aligned with Rowan’s long-term reliability, resiliency, and operational excellence standards.

This role serves as the bridge between design, construction, commissioning, and operations, representing the operations organization throughout the project lifecycle. The Reliability Engineer-Commissioning ensures that all critical infrastructure systems are tested, validated, documented, and transitioned seamlessly into steady-state operations.

Travel: Ability to travel up to 50% depending on project needs

Location: Location: Temple, TX (3-day hybrid in-office/on-site role)

Compensation: $130K-$150K (Offers Bonus)

Essential Responsibilities

Operations-Focused Commissioning Leadership

  • Lead the operational commissioning strategy for Rowan data center projects from design through handover

  • Ensure commissioning activities support Rowan’s operational standards, maintenance philosophies, and risk tolerance

  • Act as the owner’s representative for commissioning with a strong operations-first mindset

Design & Pre-Construction Engagement

  • Review design documents, basis of design (BOD), and sequences of operation to ensure alignment with Rowan’s operational requirements

  • Influence design decisions to improve operability, maintainability, and lifecycle performance

  • Support development and validation of Owner’s Project Requirements (OPR)

Construction & Commissioning Execution

  • Oversee third-party commissioning agents and contractors to ensure compliance with Rowan standards

  • Lead and witness key commissioning activities, including:

    • Factory Witness Testing (FWT)

    • Site Acceptance Testing (SAT)

    • Functional Performance Testing (FPT)

    • Integrated Systems Testing (IST)

    • Load bank and reliability testing

  • Ensure proper testing and integration of critical systems:

    • Electrical power systems (utility, generators, UPS, switchgear, STS, PDUs)

    • Mechanical and cooling systems (chillers, cooling plants, CRAHs/CRACs)

    • BMS, EPMS, and controls

    • Fire detection and suppression systems

Operational Readiness & Turnover

  • Lead operational readiness planning, including staffing, training, spares, tools, and procedures

  • Ensure completion and quality of all commissioning and turnover documentation

  • Validate O&M manuals, SOPs, EOPs, and MOPs prior to facility handover

  • Support training and readiness of site operations teams

Risk Management & Reliability

  • Identify commissioning and operational risks early and drive mitigation strategies

  • Ensure redundancy, failover, and resiliency objectives are met and validated

  • Support Rowan’s reliability, uptime, and availability targets

Continuous Improvement

  • Capture lessons learned from commissioning and early operations phases

  • Contribute to the evolution of Rowan’s commissioning standards and operational playbooks

  • Support post-occupancy reviews and early-life performance optimization

Education, Skills, and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering (Mechanical, Electrical, or related discipline) or equivalent experience

  • 5-10+ years of experience in mission-critical facilities, data center operations, commissioning, or construction

  • Strong understanding of data center MEP systems and integrated systems testing

  • Direct experience supporting or leading commissioning activities from an owner/operator perspective for electrical, mechanical, controls, or integrated mission-critical systems

  • Ability to interpret construction documents, electrical single-line diagrams, and control sequences

  • Experience transitioning facilities from construction to live operations

  • Ability to work regularly in Temple, TX and travel up to 50% based on project needs

Preferred Experience

  • Experience working with hyperscale or large-scale data center developments

  • Commissioning or operations certifications (ACP, CxA, or similar)

  • Practical experience with generators, UPS systems, switchgear, STS/ATS equipment, PDUs, chilled-water plants, BMS, EPMS, PLCs, load banks, and controls integration

  • Experience using CxAlloy, Procore, SharePoint, Bluebeam, Smartsheet, or similar project and commissioning platforms

  • Familiarity with Uptime Institute Tier standards or equivalent reliability frameworks

  • Experience managing third-party commissioning agents and complex vendor teams

  • Strong leadership, communication, and stakeholder management skills

Fueled by Excellence & Collaboration

At Rowan, we are a distributed team united by a common mission to transform data center delivery. Across our two offices, we offer a hybrid work environment supported by teamwork, technology, and in-office gathering time to help you be successful. We are headquartered in downtown Denver, Colorado and have an office in Seattle, Washington. Our team of talented and passionate individuals is spread out across the U.S.

Here to support you

At Rowan, we want to make sure you can do great work. We offer competitive benefits focused on helping you be and achieve your best.

  • Hybrid working environment

  • Team building and educational opportunities

  • Generous benefits package including robust health benefits and a 401(k)-company contribution

  • Unlimited PTO

  • RTD ECO pass or parking reimbursement

  • Competitive compensation, bonus, and an incentive plan

Equal Opportunity Employer

Rowan Digital is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome and celebrate diversity in all aspects of our workforce. We do not discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, or any other legally protected status. We strive to create an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive.

title: Automation and Controls Engineer, Gateways (Starlink)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.AUTOMATION AND CONTROLS ENGINEER, GATEWAYS (STARLINK)  
At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites, consumer receivers that allow users to connect within minutes of unboxing, and the software that brings it all together. We’ve only begun to scratch the surface of Starlink’s potential global impact and are looking for best-in-class engineers to help maximize Starlink’s utility for communities and businesses around the globe. 
One key component of SpaceX’s success so far is our commitment to keeping all engineering and production in-house, which enables a tight feedback loop, nimble decision making, and speedy deliverables. Automation and Controls Engineers at our Bastrop site are hyper-focused on designing and developing full factory solutions for novel technologies that are critical to our mission of connecting the unconnected. As a member of this team, you will lead creative, multi-disciplinary projects spanning machine design, robotics, motion systems, and factory health monitoring that all come together to form the innovative, high-rate factories that allow us to deliver internet to those that need it most.  
RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Design, develop, and manage automation projects - this includes initial factory ideation, machine commissioning, and proof of rate capability, and eventual hand-off to operational teams  
Architect, write, and debug PLC code with an emphasis on generating code that is organized, structured, documented, maintainable, and reusable for high-volume manufacturing applications  
Keep our factory safe and reliable by implementing ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA compliant systems for robots, gantries, conveyors, and other manufacturing equipment 
Generate aesthetically simple HMI screens to make complex machines easy to understand, operate, and troubleshoot 
Design electrical systems compliant to NEC, NFPA, & UL508A regulations 
Stay organized by creating schedules and budgets, and then motivate the team to achieve them  

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:  

Bachelor's degree in an engineering, physics, or computer science discipline  

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:  

Excited by a quick and iterative design and manufacturing role 
Proven ability to solve complex problems with simple solutions in both design and implementation stages 
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to make plans and directional recommendations collaboratively and cross-functionally 
Ability to engineer creative, new approaches to problems while adhering to ANSI/RIA15.06/OSHA safety requirements to keep a factory safe 
Experience with at least one of the specific disciplines listed below. The ideal candidate is interested in learning at least the fundamentals of the other areas they are not yet strong in

Mechanical:  

Machine design with focus on speed, reliability, maintainability, and safety  
Motion system sizing and implementation (gantries, robotics, conveyance, motors, actuators, pneumatics/hydraulics, sensor selection and integration, etc.)  
Fundamental structures hand calculations and ability to design for strength and stiffness  
CAD and product lifecycle management programs to generate detailed designs and drawing packages utilizing geometric dimensioning and tolerancing, preferred Siemens NX and Teamcenter  
Familiarity with manufacturing processes and how to design for manufacturability 
Exposure to some variety of production machinery, industrial sensors, and equipment (motion systems, dispense systems, temperature controllers, laser distance sensors, injection molders, die casters, etc.)  

Electrical:  

Electrical sizing of motors, cables, circuit protection, VFDs, motor starters, various other motion systems  
Design of fail-safe electrical circuits using both safety logic controllers and safety-rated relays  
Hands-on experience troubleshooting industrial electrical systems using tools like multimeters, oscilloscopes, EMI probes 
Proficiency in understanding and creating electrical schematics and single line diagrams (EPLAN preferred) 
Field bus networks, serial communication, and Ethernet communication 
Hands-on experience designing and commissioning high quality electrical panels and electro-mechanical systems with appropriate safety considerations in mind 
Knowledge of NEC, NFPA, UL508A codes with ability to ensure compliance with control system safety standards  

Industrial Software:  

PLC programming, preferably Beckhoff TwinCAT structured text programming  
Programming and implementing machine safety software through the use of safety PLC’s  
HMI, SCADA, IoT (MQTT, OPC-UA), ignition systems with focus on user friendly navigation and machine health monitoring and control  
Field Bus Networking protocols, preferably EtherCAT, Profinet, Profisafe, Ethernet/IP  
Robotics programming, preferably ABB 
Industrial software application to mechanical assemblies, electrical systems, sensors, pneumatics/hydraulics, including how to safely checkout these interdisciplinary systems prior to production implementation  

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:  

Ability to work long hours and weekends as necessary to support critical milestones  
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.  

SpaceX is an Equal Opportunity Employer; employment with SpaceX is governed on the basis of merit, competence and qualifications and will not be influenced in any manner by race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability or any other legally protected status.
Applicants wishing to view a copy of SpaceX’s Affirmative Action Plan for veterans and individuals with disabilities, or applicants requiring reasonable accommodation to the application/interview process should reach out to EEOCompliance@spacex.com.
