description:
AWS Infrastructure Services owns the design, planning, delivery, and operation of all AWS global infrastructure. In other words, we’re the people who keep the cloud running. We support all AWS data centers and all of the servers, storage, networking, power, and cooling equipment that ensure our customers have continual access to the innovation they rely on. We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

As an Controls Design Engineer, you will be part of a global engineering team, responsible for the implementation and technical evaluation of our global data center design standards with a focus on control, automation and electrical power monitoring systems.
As an Engineer in this role, you will work with the Principals and Senior Electrical and Controls Engineers to drive the standardization of designs across the global region in production data centers and resolve open technical issues in the controls space. You will participate in the research and development of new technologies and designs applicable to our products or services. You will be part of a highly creative and efficient design team comprised of Architects, Engineers, and Designers tasked with solving problems and challenging the status quo. As a subject matter expert, you will provide technical guidance, have a direct impact on the design of data center facilities, solve large-scale implementation issues, and be responsible for developing and communicating security design requirements to internal and external project partners.

Key job responsibilities
This position is for an Controls Design Engineer. Key responsibilities and requirements for this role include:

- Produce clear and concise documentation such as detailed design specifications, drawings, white papers, wiring schematics and diagrams, and reports.
- Understand and safeguard implementation of the Global Controls (Electrical and Mechanical) Basis of Design (BoD) by driving standardization in the data center controls designs.
- Development of strategic solutions, which meet or exceed our quality requirements and fall within our budgetary requirements. Capture requirements and turn aspirational company or customer goals into well-defined, achievable and testable specifications and solutions.
- Define project scope and provide technical support for information requests prior to, and during innovation and research and development projects.
- Work with regional vendors and manufacturers to specify the appropriate electrical and mechanical equipment.
- Work on concurrent projects in multiple geographical regions.

About the team
About AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud
platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers
from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and
services to power their businesses.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster
a culture of inclusion that empower us to celebrate our differences. Ongoing events and learning
experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of
sacrifices at home, which is why flexible work hours and arrangements are part of our culture.
When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the
cloud.

Mentorship & Career Growth
We have a career path for you no matter what stage you’re in when you start here. We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer.
That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing
resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Basic Qualifications

- 4+ years of relevant work in a data center or other critical environment experience
- 3+ years of experience working with electrical diagrams, single line diagrams, and electrical distribution systems
- 3+ years of experience working with industrial controls systems
- Experience with power monitoring and SCADA systems
- Experience with industrial communication protocols such as Modbus

Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field, or 4+ years of relevant discipline work experience
- Experience working with electrical power monitoring systems (EPMS), including platforms such as Eaton Foreseer, Ignition, and Schneider PSO/PME
- Familiarity with utility disturbance monitoring, power quality analysis, and event capture (sag/swell detection, harmonic analysis, transient recording)
- Knowledge of data center facilities infrastructure and operations (PDU, UPS, generators, etc.)

title: Data Center Controls Tech, Andrews, Texas
category: data center / critical infrastructure construction and engineering
description:
The Data Center Global Controls team is looking for exceptional individuals to join our Controls organization as a Controls Technician for Service & Construction of the Building Management Systems (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) within Amazon data centers. If you are passionate about the Customer Experience, think and act globally and have the ability to contribute to major new innovations in the area of building controls and automation this is the challenge you are looking for! The candidate will possess technical background and experience in installation, troubleshooting, operations and/or maintenance of field sensors, controllers, wiring, networking and programming associated with the industrial controls systems. The candidate may also have relevant experience operating and maintaining mission critical electrical and mechanical systems. A Controls Technician shall be responsible for participating in the installation, testing, troubleshooting and startup of equipment and controls system associated with the BMS and EPMS system deployment in the data centers. A Controls Technician is expected to actively innovate on behalf of their customers in the area of Data Center building automation.

Key job responsibilities
• Primarily work in and support multiple data centers by deploying, servicing, and upgrading BMS and EPMS systems.
• Mentor and train Facilities team members on the operation and control of BMS and EPMS systems.
• Manage small to medium-sized projects and programs.
• Perform point-to-point checkouts between field devices and controllers.
• Perform first-line diagnostics, troubleshooting, and maintenance of programming code and hardware associated with BMS and EPMS in data centers.
• Execute provisioning processes for servers, controllers, industrial PCs, and network configurations, including communication testing between third-party devices and controllers or servers.
• Install, replace, configure, and calibrate sensors.
• Read and interpret electrical schematics and control panel drawings with a basic understanding of closed-loop controls, field sensor scaling, and functions typically performed by industrial controllers.
• Supervise low-voltage electrical contractors performing wiring and installation of field devices in compliance with AWS requirements.
• Provide commissioning and systems-level testing support.
• Create red-lined drawings and documentation of systems.
• Follow change management processes to generate work requests and methods of procedures.
• Participate in factory witness tests at vendor or panel builder facilities.
• Perform root cause analysis during testing and commissioning.
• Ensure personnel on site utilize proper safety methodology.
• Perform service activities including monitoring and reviewing ticketing systems, conducting root cause analysis, and prioritizing tasks.
• Actively manage service agreements including vendor labor scheduling, quality assurance, and financial invoice review.
• Participate in material handling tasks such as lifting, carrying, or moving up to 50 lbs of equipment, and utilize OSHA-standard safety equipment including limited weight-bearing work platforms, ladders, step stools, and personal protective equipment (PPE) such as safety harnesses.
• Perform other tasks as assigned by manager


Physical Requirements:
· Walk job-sites in uneven terrain and work at heights and from ladders.
· Regularly walk, use hands and fingers, handle or feel, reach with hands and arms, stoop, kneel, crouch
or crawl.
· On occasions, lift and/or move up to 49 pounds; and participate in group lifts for 50 pounds or more.

A day in the life
A typical day is attending morning construction/commissioning meetings, assessing and prioritization of project tasks and service tickets for the given day. Field work which requires configuring controllers, testing sensors, troubleshooting, safety site walks, and supporting general startup processes. Technician is responsible for logging their daily efforts in construction and service related AWS tools.

The mission of the Data Center Controls Engineering team is to manage the design, deployment, and service of a highly reliable electrical and mechanical control system for the life-cycle of an AWS data center.

About the team
As a member of the Global Controls Team, you will collaborate with highly motivated operators, engineers and technicians in the data center industry to maintain and optimize critical infrastructure systems. You will be responsible for troubleshooting and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) while developing new processes and standards that drive innovation in the controls space.
AWS data centers utilize sophisticated industrial control systems to automatically operate mechanical equipment, maintaining optimal temperature and pressure conditions throughout the facilities. These systems integrate and monitor multiple critical components, including generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic and static transfer switches, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs), and air economizers. Within this industrial control system infrastructure, the BMS serves as the primary control platform for all mechanical systems within the data center, while the EPMS functions as the primary monitoring platform for all electrical systems. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in mission-critical environments while contributing to the reliability and efficiency of AWS's global infrastructure.


Basic Qualifications

- High school or equivalent diploma
- Basic understanding of Industrial controls system, knowledge of meters, devices, sensors, relays and troubleshooting utilizing standard hand tools, digital metering, or calibration/diagnostic equipment in a data center, hospitals, large commercial complex, water, power, oil & gas or similar industries
- 1+ years of experience working with low voltage controls, wiring, networking signals, electrical and mechanical systems, computers and operating systems
- Ability to work non-standard hours and differing work rotations/shifts and overtime as required.

Preferred Qualifications

- High School or equivalent diploma
- International Society of Automation (ISA) Certified Controls System Technician (CCST) Level I or higher certification.
- Experiencing using common communication protocols (MQTT, BACnet, and/or MODBUS).
- 5+ years of experience in controls/automation, construction or related field in a technical environment
- Demonstrated understanding of engineering documentation, electrical and mechanical diagrams, and standard operating procedures.
- Experience in data centers or mission critical environment
- Fundamental knowledge of network design and layout as well as low voltage (copper/ fiber) cabling.
- Prior AWS/Amazon experience
- 4+ Yr. Military Service

Field work which requires configuring controllers, testing sensors, troubleshooting, safety site walks, and supporting general startup processes. Technician is responsible for logging their daily efforts in construction and service related AWS tools.
The mission of the Data Center Controls Engineering team is to manage the design, deployment, and service of a highly reliable electrical and mechanical control system for the life-cycle of an AWS data center.

About the team

You will be responsible for troubleshooting and maintaining the Building Management System (BMS) and Electrical Power Monitoring System (EPMS) while developing new processes and standards that drive innovation in the controls space.
AWS data centers utilize sophisticated industrial control systems to automatically operate mechanical equipment, maintaining optimal temperature and pressure conditions throughout the facilities. These systems integrate and monitor multiple critical components, including generators, uninterruptible power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic and static transfer switches, air-cooled and water-cooled chillers, pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, Computer Room Air Handlers (CRAHs), and air economizers. Within this industrial control system infrastructure, the BMS serves as the primary control platform for all mechanical systems within the data center, while the EPMS functions as the primary monitoring platform for all electrical systems. This position offers the opportunity to work with cutting-edge technology in mission-critical environments while contributing to the reliability and efficiency of AWS's global infrastructure.

description:
Who We Are:
Galaxy Digital Inc. (Nasdaq: GLXY) is a global leader in digital assets and data center infrastructure, growing the economy that runs on code. Galaxy delivers the onchain infrastructure that connects institutions to digital assets, including trading, advisory, asset management, staking, self-custody, and tokenization. Galaxy also develops and operates data center infrastructure to power AI and HPC workloads. Anchored by its Helios campus in Texas, Galaxy is building a multi-gigawatt pipeline of more than 5.7 GW of potential capacity, positioning it among the largest and fastest-growing data center developers in North America.
The Company is headquartered in New York City, with offices across North America, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia.
Additional information about Galaxy's businesses and products is available on www.galaxy.com.
What We Value:
We are a diverse team of free thinkers, and fast movers united to help investors and creators energize the global economy. We are looking for individuals who thrive in a culture of builders and overachievers and embrace high performance, transparent feedback, and a mission-first approach. Our culture shapes our way of working and gets us where we want to be.

Seek Excellence.
Be Selective To Be Effective.
Be Highly Aligned, Loosely Coupled.
Disagree Transparently.
Encourage Independent Decision-Making.
Build Dream Teams.
Who You Are:
The Project Management Office (PMO) Project Manager (Data Center Construction) is the PMO's embedded project management partner to the Pre-Construction and Construction functions. This is not a traditional construction PM role responsible for replacing the technical ownership of the Pre-Construction or Construction teams. Department leaders and subject matter experts retain ownership and accountability for their work. Instead, the PM provides the cross-functional coordination, structure, visibility, and accountability required to move complex initiatives forward across departmental boundaries. Pre-construction and construction activities inherently depend on multiple teams - including Site Development, Operations, Technology, EHS, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and external partners. The PM ensures those dependencies are identified early, responsibilities are clear, decisions occur at the appropriate time, and work across departments remains aligned to broader project and business priorities. The role gives department leadership a partner who can take complex initiatives and create the structure required to execute them effectively while allowing technical leaders to remain focused on their areas of expertise.
What You’ll Do:

Partner closely with Pre-Construction and Construction leadership to understand priorities, upcoming work, constraints, and cross-functional needs.
Translate complex initiatives into clearly defined workstreams, tasks, milestones, owners, dependencies, and decision points.
Establish and maintain visibility into current and upcoming work through the PMO project management systems and reporting processes.
Identify dependencies between Pre-Construction / Construction and Site Development, Operations, Technology, EHS, Procurement, Finance, Legal, and other functions.
Facilitate the cross-functional meetings required to move work forward, with clear objectives, ownership, decisions, action items, and follow-through.
Connect department heads and functional stakeholders when work has broader organizational impacts or requires decisions across teams.
Identify risks, stalled work, unclear ownership, resource constraints, or competing priorities and drive the appropriate conversations toward resolution.
Escalate material risks and decisions to department leadership, the Head of PMO, or business leadership when appropriate.
Partner with department leadership on prioritization and sequencing when multiple initiatives compete for resources or have interdependent timelines.
Support capacity and resourcing discussions by providing visibility into upcoming work, workload, dependencies, and potential constraints.
Ensure required Procurement, Finance, Legal, and other support-function processes are incorporated into project plans and initiated at the appropriate time.
Improve communication between Pre-Construction / Construction and other departments by ensuring relevant information reaches the appropriate stakeholders and other embedded PMO PMs.
Provide objective facilitation when priorities, ownership, timelines, or expectations conflict across departments.
Track execution against agreed business priorities and provide leadership with clear visibility into progress, risks, decisions, and blockers.
Partner with the Head of PMO and other embedded PMO PMs to consistently apply PMO standards, tools, processes, and reporting practices.

What We’re Looking For:

5+ years of experience in project management, program management, construction, infrastructure, engineering, development, or a related environment.
Experience coordinating complex initiatives involving multiple departments, technical teams, and business stakeholders.
Working knowledge of pre-construction and construction processes sufficient to understand dependencies, sequencing, terminology, and business impacts.
Strong ability to take ambiguous or complex initiatives and create structured execution plans.
Demonstrated ability to facilitate cross-functional teams and create accountability without direct authority.
Strong stakeholder-management skills and ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, functional leaders, and executives.
Strong problem-solving skills with an ability to identify organizational gaps, dependencies, and risks before they affect execution.
Experience with project/work management platforms such as Jira and related collaboration and documentation tools.
Strong written and verbal communication and executive reporting skills.
PMP or equivalent certification preferred.

What We Offer (US):

Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus

Flexible Time Off (i.e. unlimited paid vacation days)
Company paid Holidays (11)
Company paid sick leave
Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
3% 401(k) company contribution
Generous paid Parental Leave
Free virtual coaching and counseling sessions through Ginger
Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry
Free daily snacks in-office
Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.

We will endeavor to make a reasonable accommodation to the known limitations of a qualified applicant with a disability unless the accommodation would impose an undue hardship on the operation of our business. If you believe you require such assistance to complete the application process or to participate in an interview, please contact careers@galaxy.com.

Who You Are:

The Project Management Office (PMO) Project Manager (Data Center Construction) is the PMO's embedded project management partner to the Pre-Construction and Construction functions. This is not a traditional construction PM role responsible for replacing the technical ownership of the Pre-Construction or Construction teams. Department leaders and subject matter experts retain ownership and accountability for their work. Instead, the PM provides the cross-functional coordination, structure, visibility, and accountability required to move complex initiatives forward across departmental boundaries. Pre-construction and construction activities inherently depend on multiple teams - including Site Development, Operations, Technology, EHS, Finance, Procurement, Legal, and external partners. The PM ensures those dependencies are identified early, responsibilities are clear, decisions occur at the appropriate time, and work across departments remains aligned to broader project and business priorities. The role gives department leadership a partner who can take complex initiatives and create the structure required to execute them effectively while allowing technical leaders to remain focused on their areas of expertise.

What You’ll Do:

  • Partner closely with Pre-Construction and Construction leadership to understand priorities, upcoming work, constraints, and cross-functional needs.
  • Translate complex initiatives into clearly defined workstreams, tasks, milestones, owners, dependencies, and decision points.
  • Establish and maintain visibility into current and upcoming work through the PMO project management systems and reporting processes.
  • Identify dependencies between Pre-Construction / Construction and Site Development, Operations, Technology, EHS, Procurement, Finance, Legal, and other functions.
  • Facilitate the cross-functional meetings required to move work forward, with clear objectives, ownership, decisions, action items, and follow-through.
  • Connect department heads and functional stakeholders when work has broader organizational impacts or requires decisions across teams.
  • Identify risks, stalled work, unclear ownership, resource constraints, or competing priorities and drive the appropriate conversations toward resolution.
  • Escalate material risks and decisions to department leadership, the Head of PMO, or business leadership when appropriate.
  • Partner with department leadership on prioritization and sequencing when multiple initiatives compete for resources or have interdependent timelines.
  • Support capacity and resourcing discussions by providing visibility into upcoming work, workload, dependencies, and potential constraints.
  • Ensure required Procurement, Finance, Legal, and other support-function processes are incorporated into project plans and initiated at the appropriate time.
  • Improve communication between Pre-Construction / Construction and other departments by ensuring relevant information reaches the appropriate stakeholders and other embedded PMO PMs.
  • Provide objective facilitation when priorities, ownership, timelines, or expectations conflict across departments.
  • Track execution against agreed business priorities and provide leadership with clear visibility into progress, risks, decisions, and blockers.
  • Partner with the Head of PMO and other embedded PMO PMs to consistently apply PMO standards, tools, processes, and reporting practices.

What We’re Looking For:

  • 5+ years of experience in project management, program management, construction, infrastructure, engineering, development, or a related environment.
  • Experience coordinating complex initiatives involving multiple departments, technical teams, and business stakeholders.
  • Working knowledge of pre-construction and construction processes sufficient to understand dependencies, sequencing, terminology, and business impacts.
  • Strong ability to take ambiguous or complex initiatives and create structured execution plans.
  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate cross-functional teams and create accountability without direct authority.
  • Strong stakeholder-management skills and ability to communicate effectively with technical teams, functional leaders, and executives.
  • Strong problem-solving skills with an ability to identify organizational gaps, dependencies, and risks before they affect execution.
  • Experience with project/work management platforms such as Jira and related collaboration and documentation tools.
  • Strong written and verbal communication and executive reporting skills.
  • PMP or equivalent certification preferred.

What We Offer (US):

  • Competitive base salary and discretionary bonus
  • Flexible Time Off (i.e. unlimited paid vacation days)
  • Company paid Holidays (11)
  • Company paid sick leave
  • Company-paid health and protective benefits for employees, partners, and other dependents
  • 3% 401(k) company contribution
  • Generous paid Parental Leave
  • Free virtual coaching and counseling sessions through Ginger
  • Opportunities to learn about the Crypto industry
  • Free daily snacks in-office
  • Smart, entrepreneurial, and fun colleagues
  • Employee Resource Groups

*Benefits may vary depending on location.

title: Staff Engineering Operations Technical Program Manager
description:
About us
Graphcore is one of the world’s leading innovators in Artificial Intelligence compute. It is developing hardware, software and systems infrastructure that will unlock the next generation of AI breakthroughs and power the widespread adoption of AI solutions across every industry.
As part of the SoftBank Group, Graphcore is a member of an elite family of companies responsible for some of the world’s most transformative technologies. Together, they share a bold vision: to enable Artificial Super Intelligence and ensure its benefits are accessible to everyone.
Graphcore’s teams are drawn from diverse backgrounds and bring a broad range of skills and perspectives. A melting pot of AI research specialists, silicon designers, software engineers and systems architects, Graphcore enjoys a culture of continuous learning and constant innovation.
 
Job Summary
We are seeking a Staff Hardware Engineer to provide advanced operational, diagnostic, and engineering support for Graphcore’s Arm-based hardware platforms across lab and data center environments.
This role focuses on supporting hardware bring-up, validation, and troubleshooting of complex AI compute platforms, including server blades, racks, and rack-scale infrastructure. The successful candidate will collaborate closely with engineering, platform, and data center teams to ensure the reliability and performance of next-generation AI systems.
 
The Team
The Systems Engineering and Hardware Engineering teams are responsible for enabling the bring-up, validation, and operational reliability of Graphcore’s AI infrastructure platforms.
The team works closely with server engineering, firmware teams, platform architects, and data center operations to support the development, testing, and deployment of next-generation AI compute systems.
This collaborative environment enables rapid problem-solving and continuous improvement of Graphcore’s hardware platforms from early development through production deployment.
 
Responsibilities and Duties

Lead advanced break-fix troubleshooting for server blades, motherboards, power systems, and rack-scale infrastructure.
Support engineering bring-up activities, including component validation and firmware interaction testing.
Diagnose system-level failures involving thermal behavior, power anomalies, network configuration, and BIOS/BMC issues.
Collaborate with server engineering teams to perform root cause analysis and propose corrective actions or design improvements.
Support deployment and rollout of next-generation hardware platforms through structured validation and qualification cycles.
Interface with facilities and infrastructure teams to understand environmental factors impacting system reliability.
Develop and maintain standard operating procedures (SOPs), troubleshooting guides, and validation documentation.
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior technicians and engineers on troubleshooting methodologies and hardware diagnostics.
Participate in on-call rotations or off-hours support during critical engineering milestones or hardware bring-up phases.

Candidate Profile
Essential

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related discipline.
8 years of strong experience with server hardware architectures and board-level debugging.
Experience analyzing system logs, hardware telemetry, and power/thermal metrics to isolate hardware failures.
Hands-on experience with HPC systems, AI compute platforms, or rack-scale infrastructure.
Strong collaboration skills and ability to work effectively in fast-paced engineering environments.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.

Desirable

Experience supporting prototype or pre-production hardware bring-up.
Familiarity with data center facilities, including liquid cooling and power distribution systems.
Experience using Python, Bash, or automation tools for hardware validation or troubleshooting.
Exposure to structured failure analysis and reliability engineering methodologies.

 
USA BenefitsIn addition to a competitive salary, Graphcore offers flexible working and a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your health, wellbeing and financial future. Our benefits include medical, dental and vision coverage, Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs), Health Savings Accounts (HSAs), disability and life insurance, a 401(k) retirement plan, commuter benefits, wellness services and an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP). We welcome people of different backgrounds and experiences; we're committed to building an inclusive work environment that makes Graphcore a great home for everyone. We offer an equal opportunity process and understand that there are visible and invisible differences in all of us. We can provide a flexible approach to interview and encourage you to chat to us if you require any reasonable adjustments.

title: Concrete Finisher
description:
At Keeley Companies, we believe in empowering our people and fulfilling career aspirations. Keeley is a career destination with countless opportunities for advancement, and a world-class family culture that is centered around creating the best possible environment for our people to thrive.Our Paving team in Texas has an exciting opportunity as a Concrete Finisher.
Primary Responsibilities:

Assist in the installation and construction of concrete pavements, curbs, and sidewalks following project specifications and design plans.
Lift, carry, and transport construction materials, tools, and equipment weighing over 50 pounds to the work area, ensuring the availability of necessary resources for the project.
Assist in preparation and pouring of concrete mixtures into forms or onto surfaces, ensuring accurate placement and distribution.
Assist in performing repairs on concrete surfaces, including patching, resurfacing, and finishing, to ensure a smooth and uniform appearance.
Strike off with experience straight edge techniques, float and finish concrete.
Support the finishing process by smoothing, leveling, and shaping concrete surfaces using appropriate tools and techniques.
Operate and maneuver small equipment like skid steers, mini excavators, backhoes, rollers, etc., as needed for concrete finishing and related tasks.
Assist in inspecting finished concrete work to ensure it meets project specifications, quality standards, and customer expectations.
Collaborate with construction teams, including contractors, architects, and engineers, to coordinate work and achieve project goals.

 
Minimum Qualifications

High school diploma or Equivalent plus a minimum of two years previous experience as a concrete finisher
Ability to travel a 3-4 hour radius outside of home location
2-5 years of experience in the construction industry, with a focus on concrete finishing and related tasks.
Drivers License (preferred) to facilitate transportation to various jobsites.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills and a good attitude.
Strong analytical and critical thinking skills; trainable.
Strong attention to detail; take pride in work.
Ability to read and understand blueprints.

title: Civil Superintendent
description:
Job Title: Civil Superintendent - Mission CriticalCompany: Loenbro, LLCBusiness Unit/Department: Underground Maintenance & Installation (UMI)Location: Afton, TXReports To: UMI ManagerEmployment Type: Full TimeFLSA Classification: Exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach, and every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
At Loenbro, we don't just offer jobs, we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps build and maintain the critical infrastructure that supports communities across the nation.
Job Summary
The Civil Superintendent is responsible for the overall planning, coordination, execution, and supervision of civil construction projects, including site development, earthwork, grading, excavation, underground utilities, drainage systems, concrete structures, and related infrastructure. This position provides direct leadership to field personnel, subcontractors, and equipment operators while ensuring projects are completed safely, on schedule, within budget, and in accordance with project specifications and quality standards.
The Civil Superintendent works closely with Project Managers, clients, engineers, and foremen to coordinate resources, monitor production, and drive project success from mobilization through completion.
Essential Job Responsibilities

Read, interpret, and implement project drawings, specifications, contracts, and civil construction plans.
Direct and supervise daily field operations for civil construction projects.
Coordinate crews, subcontractors, equipment, materials, and vendors to ensure efficient project execution.
Develop, maintain, and manage three-week and six-week look-ahead schedules.
Monitor project production rates and implement corrective actions to maintain schedule and budget objectives.
Lead earthwork, grading, excavation, trenching, underground utility installation, storm drainage, paving preparation, and concrete activities.

Job Summary
We are seeking an experienced Scaffold Foreman to lead and oversee scaffold crews on industrial and commercial construction projects. The Scaffold Foreman is responsible for planning, coordinating, supervising, and inspecting scaffold erection, modification, and dismantling activities while ensuring compliance with all safety regulations, project specifications, and company standards. The ideal candidate will possess strong leadership skills, extensive scaffolding experience, and a commitment to maintaining a safe and productive work environment.
 
Essential Job Responsibilities

Supervise and direct scaffold crews in the safe erection, modification, inspection, and dismantling of scaffolding systems.
Plan daily work activities, assign tasks, and ensure projects are completed safely, efficiently, and on schedule.
Verify that all scaffold structures are built according to applicable regulations, engineering requirements, and company standards.
Conduct pre-job planning meetings and daily safety briefings with crew members.
Perform routine scaffold inspections to ensure structural integrity and compliance with OSHA and project-specific safety requirements.
Identify and correct unsafe conditions, work practices, or equipment deficiencies.
Coordinate scaffold activities with project managers, superintendents, contractors, and other trades to support project goals.
Maintain accurate records of inspections, workforce activity, material usage, and equipment inventory.
Ensure scaffold materials, tools, and equipment are properly maintained, stored, and accounted for.

Company: Loenbro, LLCBusiness Unit/Department: South                          Location: Dallas, TXReports to: Lead Survey TechnicianEmployment Type: Full-TimeFLSA Classification: Non-exempt
About Loenbro
Loenbro is a trusted, long-term construction lifecycle partner to thousands of customers across the U.S. Our market spans all industries and our service offerings include Critical Electrical, Mechanical & Structural, Soft Crafts, Inspection, Underground Maintenance and Installation, and Fabrication. Our expertise lies in simplifying the complex and establishing long-standing relationships with our partners. We have a national presence but a local approach—every customer benefits from our capabilities and our care.
 
At Loenbro, we don’t just offer jobs—we build careers grounded in integrity, teamwork, excellence, and purpose. Join a team where your expertise is valued, your growth is supported, and your work helps maintain and enhance the critical infrastructure that powers communities across the nation.
 
Job Summary
Loenbro is seeking a detail-oriented and motivated Survey Technician to support mission-critical construction projects, including hyperscale data centers, advanced manufacturing facilities, and other complex infrastructure developments. This role is responsible for performing field surveying, layout verification, quality control measurements, and construction staking activities utilizing Trimble survey equipment and software platforms. 
The Survey Technician will work closely with project managers, superintendents, engineers, BIM/VDC teams, and craft professionals to ensure accurate project layout, alignment, and documentation throughout all phases of construction. 
 
Essential Job Responsibilities 

Perform construction staking and layout for foundations, structural steel, equipment pads, underground utilities, roadways, electrical infrastructure, and building components. 

Operate and maintain Trimble total stations, GNSS/GPS receivers, robotic instruments, and data collectors. 

Utilize Trimble Business Center (TBC), Trimble Access, Trimble Siteworks, and other survey software to process and manage field data. 

Interpret engineering drawings, BIM models, civil plans, utility plans, and specifications to establish project control points. 

Verify as-built conditions and perform quality assurance/quality control surveys throughout construction activities. 

Establish and maintain horizontal and vertical control networks on active construction sites. 

Collaborate with project management and field operations teams to identify and resolve layout discrepancies. 

Generate survey reports, field notes, stakeout documentation, and as-built deliverables. 

Assist with reality capture activities utilizing laser scanning, GPS technologies, and drone-based mapping programs when applicable. 

Ensure surveying activities align with project schedules while maintaining the highest levels of accuracy and safety. 

Support construction teams in fast-paced mission-critical environments where schedule adherence and precision directly impact project success. 

 
Minimum Qualifications 

High school diploma or GED required. 

Associate degree in Surveying, Civil Engineering Technology, Construction Management, Geomatics, or related field preferred. 

Minimum 2 years of construction surveying experience required. 

Experience supporting large-scale commercial, industrial, mission-critical, semiconductor, advanced manufacturing, or data center construction projects preferred. 

Working knowledge of survey principles, coordinate systems, control networks, and construction layout procedures. 

Ability to read and interpret construction drawings, specifications, and engineering documents. 

Valid driver's license and ability to travel to project sites as required. 

 
Preferred Qualifications 

3+ years of experience with Trimble surveying technologies. 

Proficiency with:  

Trimble Business Center (TBC) 

Trimble Siteworks 

Trimble Access 

Trimble GNSS/GPS Systems 

Robotic Total Stations 

Experience integrating survey data with BIM/VDC workflows and Autodesk platforms. 

Familiarity with data center construction, electrical infrastructure, and mission-critical facilities. 

OSHA 10 or OSHA 30 certification preferred. 

FAA Part 107 Drone License a plus. 

 
Knowledge, Skills & Abilities 

Strong understanding of construction surveying methods and best practices. 

High attention to detail with exceptional measurement accuracy. 

Ability to work in dynamic, active construction environments. 

Strong mathematical, analytical, and problem-solving abilities. 

Effective communication and collaboration skills. 

Ability to manage multiple priorities and meet aggressive project schedules. 

Demonstrated commitment to safety, quality, and continuous improvement. 

 
 
Physical Requirements & Work Environment 

Ability to work outdoors in varied weather conditions. 

Frequent standing, walking, climbing, bending, and lifting up to 50 pounds. 

Ability to travel to construction sites nationwide as required. 

Must wear required personal protective equipment (PPE) and comply with all safety regulations. 

Ability to safely navigate active construction sites, including mission-critical and industrial environments. 

 
Benefits 
Loenbro offers a competitive salary, comprehensive benefits package, and rewards to those who join our team: 

Medical, dental, and vision insurance 

401(k) retirement plan with company match 

Paid time off (PTO)

Life and disability insurance 

Professional development and training opportunities 

Employee assistance program (EAP) 

 
Benefits eligibility may vary based on employment classification and hours worked. 
 
Our Core Values 
LEAD with Values: 

Live with Integrity – We do the right thing and do what we say, in every Interaction - and practice stewardship to car for the communities where we live & work.  

Exceed Expectations – We anticipate customer needs, deliver Innovative solutions, and dedicate ourselves to creating outcomes that make a real difference.  

Act with Urgency – We take action, adapt seamlessly, and keep projects moving without compromising quality - because our customers priorities are our priorities.  

Deliver Excellence – We combine our passion for quality, our Industry expertise, and our eye for Innovation to make excellence our standard.  

Guided by core values, grounded in grit and a commitment to excellence, Loenbro maintains and enhances the industrial infrastructure that betters our families, customers, and local communities. 
 
Loenbro is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

title: Project Mechanical Engineer - Healthcare Buildings
description:
Company Description

We are Olsson. We engineer and design solutions that improve the world around us. As a company, we promise to always be responsive, transparent, and focused on results – for our people, our clients, and our company.
We’re a people-centric firm, so it’s no surprise our greatest asset is our people. The impact this creates is an environment that encourages our people to grow and be creative with their talents. This approach builds a culture that is uniquely Olsson. It allows us to grow our people as we grow our business. This, in turn, creates a lasting impact on the world around us.Job Description
Olsson is seeking a Project Mechanical Engineer to join our Facilities Engineering and Design Team, focusing on healthcare facility projects. In this role, you will apply advanced engineering principles to design mechanical systems for healthcare facilities, ensuring they meet the highest standards of safety, efficiency, and functionality. You will have the opportunity to lead design efforts, coordinate with multidisciplinary teams, and contribute to high-impact projects that improve healthcare environments.
This role is ideal for an experienced engineer looking to take on greater responsibility, mentor junior staff, and play a key role in project execution.
Key responsibilities:

Lead the design and development of mechanical systems for healthcare facilities.
Perform detailed engineering calculations, cost estimates, and system analyses to ensure compliance with project and industry standards.
Prepare and oversee the production of project documents, including plans, specifications, and reports.
Provide technical guidance to junior engineers and designers, ensuring quality and consistency in deliverables.
Coordinate with internal teams, architects, and clients to align design efforts with project objectives.
Oversee design execution, progress tracking, and adherence to project scope, schedule, and budget.
Support client meetings, project coordination efforts, and design reviews.
Conduct field visits and site assessments to validate design accuracy and functionality.

Qualifications

You are passionate about:

Working collaboratively with others.
Having ownership in the work you do.
Using your talents to positively affect communities.

You bring to the team:

Strong communication skills.
Ability to contribute and work well with a team.
Excellent interpersonal and problem-solving skills.
Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical Engineering.
Professional Engineer (PE) license required.
6+ years of mechanical engineering experience, with at least 2 years in healthcare facility design preferred.
Enthusiasm for contributing to the healthcare industry through innovative and reliable mechanical engineering solutions.
Healthcare-related certifications such as ASHRAE Healthcare Facilities Design Professional (HFDP), ASSE 6060 Medical Gas Systems Designer, ASSE 12080 Certified Legionella Water Safety & Management Specialist, Certified Healthcare Constructor (CHC), and/or Healthcare Physical Environment Worker, are a plus.

Olsson specializes in engineering and design, client advisory services, planning, field services, and environmental. Improving the world has been our mindset from the very beginning, back when Olsson first opened for business in 1956. And it will be our mindset for years to come.

Receive a competitive 401(k) match
Be empowered to build your career with tailored development paths
Have the possibility for flexible work arrangements

You are passionate about:

  • Using your talents to positively affect communities.

You bring to the team:

  • Strong communication skills.
  • Ability to contribute and work well on a team.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Engineering or a related area preferred. In lieu of a bachelor’s degree, an associate degree with equivalent experience is required.
  • Minimum of ten years of related experience within an applicable field or discipline.

title: Construction Project Manager, Warranties (Starbase Development)
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.CONSTRUCTION PROJECT MANAGER, WARRANTIES (STARBASE DEVELOPMENT)
The Starbase Development Team is seeking a Construction Project Manager, Warranties to own construction quality assurance and the warranty program for residential and commercial infrastructure in Starbase, TX. This role will own build quality and performance initiatives and serve as the primary liaison between the design, construction, and maintenance teams throughout construction and the project life cycle.
RESPONSIBILITIES:

Manage quality assurance during construction, including reviewing 3rd party reports, performing independent inspections, issuing reports with corrective actions, and documenting as-built conditions
Perform investigations and root cause analyses on known warranty issues; create plan of action to address root causes and identify discrepancies between design intent and as-built conditions
Manage all project controls for warranty work, including scheduling, coordination with maintenance teams, and budgeting as needed
Hold builders and vendors accountable for construction quality and warranty performance
Proactively review designs with an eye for prevention of future warranty issues, driving systemic continual improvements based on lessons learned
Oversee warranty repairs from initiation through verified completion, maintaining clear program documentation and reporting
Lead small-to-medium process improvement and special projects, exercising independent judgment and significant autonomy
Build and maintain relationships with contractors, vendors, fabricators, architects, and internal stakeholders to align with residential project goals
Partner with facilities teams and end-users to transition spaces into fully operational, low-maintenance environments post-construction

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

Bachelor's degree in construction management, engineering, or architecture; OR 6+ years of professional construction, closeout, or warranty experience in lieu of a degree
4+ years of hands-on professional experience in residential architecture, engineering, construction management, or facilities development

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

2+ years of experience working in a quality assurance, quality control, or warranty-related field
Working knowledge of typical residential warranty structures (workmanship, systems, envelope, structural, manufacturer)
Expertise across residential development technical disciplines, including civil/site work, structural framing, mechanical/HVAC, electrical systems, plumbing, geotechnical analysis, and surveying
Skilled in reviewing, interpreting, and approving residential drawings, fabrication plans, blueprints, and technical specifications
Thrive in high-velocity environments, pivoting roles swiftly while sustaining urgency, precision, and results
Exceptional independent thinker and collaborative team player, with initiative, clear communication, and a bias for action

 ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

This position is based in Starbase, TX and requires being onsite – remote work not considered
Must be willing to travel to various SpaceX locations for mission critical projects
Must be available to work extended hours and weekends when needed based on project deadlines or residential operational requirements
Physical ability to lift and transport materials or tools (up to 25 lbs.) across construction sites
Occasional travel may be required to support other Spaceport Development project activations and turnovers
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

title: HVAC Programmer
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.HVAC PROGRAMMER
The HVAC Programmer at SpaceX works in a fast-paced environment, where the extraordinary becomes the everyday. The HVAC Programmer develops and integrates new and or existing applications into the technical infrastructure and existing business processes. The HVAC Programmer will create and provide a complete programming package to the System Manager/Team. The package includes but is not limited to a Sequence of Operation, Virtual Points, pre-tested programming and onsite Functional Test for assigned projects. This will involve training the technician team on how to interact with the control systems and overall helping improve all controls and automation for critical systems at the Starbase facility.
RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Set up process to write all programs and virtual points
Work in conjunction with engineers, environmental control system/HVAC lead and/or manager in order to produce controller and graphical software that will meet or exceed engineers, environmental control system/HVAC lead and/or manager’s expectations
Incorporate third party software into the design of building environmental control automation systems
Identify and obtain the necessary components to network the building automation system workstations; configure the software necessary to network the workstations
Set-up virtual and/or physical test system to test all programming prior to release to the field
Create functional test checkout sheets to be included in specialist checkout books
Provide technical support before, during and after system installation to the engineers, environmental control system/HVAC lead and/or manager regarding environmental control automation system
Provide recommendations to both engineering and technical teams as to how to make the environmental control automation systems more reliable
Provide in-house software support and assist in maintenance of existing system software
Provide onsite assistance at critical facilities with functional testing as required
Perform administrative duties such as expense reports, documentation of detail issues and time spent on tasks within work order system, writing weekly reports, acquiring vendor quotes, submitting purchase orders, etc.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
3+ years of experience with HVAC, pneumatic, mechanical, electrical systems and control systems

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

3+ years of experience programming HVAC control strategies
Associate degree or 1-2 years of vocational technical training
Specialized skill training/certification
Strong leadership and organizational skills
4+ years of experience with Johnson Controls or Andover Controls or Siemens Controls
Detail oriented, organized, and demonstrates a high sense of urgency
Able to work autonomously

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

Willingness to work all required shift hours, including overtime and weekends, as needed
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. title: Sr. Fire & Life Safety Program Specialist
description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.SR. FIRE & LIFE SAFETY PROGRAM SPECIALIST 
Reporting to Facilities/Maintenance, the Sr. Fire & Life Safety Program Specialist owns the full lifecycle of fire detection and suppression systems for our industrial and aerospace manufacturing campus — from the maintenance and reliability program for existing fire alarm infrastructure to the design, permitting, and installation of new fire suppression and sprinkler systems. This is primarily a program and project management role: you will be the site’s single point of accountability for fire protection strategy, contractor and vendor performance, code compliance, and AHJ engagement.   
Your deep technical background in fire alarm design and programming enables you to review vendor work critically, direct troubleshooting, and step in hands-on during emergencies and critical impairments. You will partner closely with EHS to identify and mitigate emerging fire hazards ranging from lithium-ion battery storage to aerospace vehicle integration. 
RESPONSIBILITIES: 

Manage the maintenance, reliability, and upgrade program for existing industrial fire alarm systems across the site, including inspection, testing, and maintenance (ITM) per NFPA 72 and NFPA 25
Provide project management for new installations of fire suppression and sprinkler systems, ranging from small-scope tenant improvements to multi-million-dollar capital projects, including scope development, budgeting, scheduling, bid packages, and contractor selection
Serve as the site's technical authority for fire alarm design and programming: review and approve fire alarm, suppression, and sprinkler designs, submittals, and shop drawings from vendors and engineering firms; perform in-house design and panel programming for small-scope modifications where faster or more cost-effective than contracting out
Direct troubleshooting and repair of fire alarm and suppression systems through service contractors, owning scope, quality, response time, and cost accountability; provide hands-on diagnosis and repair during emergencies, critical impairments, or when contractor response is inadequate
Identify existing and emerging fire hazards — including lithium-ion battery storage and charging, energetic materials, flammable liquids, and aerospace vehicle integration operations — and drive engineering and administrative controls to mitigate them
Partner with EHS to drive emergency response readiness, impairment management (fire watch), pre-incident planning, and post-incident investigation support
Ensure compliance with applicable building and fire codes (IBC, IFC, NFPA standards) and company standards; maintain system documentation, as-builts, and ITM records
Engage and maintain relationships with the Authority Having Jurisdiction (AHJ), fire marshal, and insurance carriers; manage permitting, plan review, acceptance testing, and inspections for fire protection projects
Develop and manage annual operating and capital budgets for fire protection systems; forecast end-of-life replacements and reliability upgrades
Support Alternate Means & Methods (AM&M) and performance-based design proposals to the AHJ where prescriptive code compliance is impractical
Develop training for facilities technicians, security, and emergency response teams on fire system operation and impairment procedures 

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS: 

High school diploma or equivalency certificate
NICET Level III or IV certification in Fire Alarm Systems
7+ years of experience in fire alarm and/or fire suppression system design, installation, programming, or maintenance
3+ years of experience in project or program management of fire protection or facilities construction projects 

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE: 

NICET Level IV in Fire Alarm Systems; additional NICET certification in Water-Based Systems Layout or Inspection & Testing of Water-Based Systems
Bachelor's degree in fire protection engineering, engineering technology, construction management, or a related field
Factory certification and programming experience on major fire alarm platforms (e.g., Notifier, Simplex, EST/Edwards, Siemens, Fire-Lite)
Working knowledge of NFPA 13, 25, 72, 855, and 30, and the International Building and Fire Codes
Experience with special hazards suppression (clean agent, water mist, deluge, foam) and hazardous material occupancies
Experience managing fire protection in industrial, manufacturing, aerospace, or high-hazard environments
Experience with lithium-ion battery energy storage system (ESS) fire protection and code requirements (NFPA 855, UL 9540A)
Direct experience with AHJ negotiation, permitting, plan review, and acceptance testing
Experience managing contractors and vendors, including bid evaluation, contract administration, and performance management
PMP certification or equivalent project management training
Proficiency with AutoCAD, Revit, Bluebeam, and CMMS platforms 

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS: 

Ability to respond to after-hours system troubles, impairments, and emergencies; participate in on-call rotation as needed
Position may require extended hours and weekends to support outages, acceptance testing, and critical project milestones
Ability to climb ladders, work at heights, work in industrial environments, and lift up to 25 lbs. unassisted
This is a fully on-site position at a single campus; occasional travel for training or vendor factory acceptance testing (less than 5%) 
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

To conform to U.S. Government export regulations, applicant must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful, permanent resident (aka green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State. Learn more about the ITAR here.

We work on the most challenging problems, with thousands of variables impacting the supply chain — and we’re looking for talented people who want to help.

You’ll join a diverse team of software, hardware, and network engineers, supply chain specialists, security experts, operations managers, and other vital roles. You’ll collaborate with people across AWS to help us deliver the highest standards for safety and security while providing seemingly infinite capacity at the lowest possible cost for our customers. And you’ll experience an inclusive culture that welcomes bold ideas and empowers you to own them to completion.

Amazon Web Services is seeking a Senior Electrical Engineer to become part of a global engineering team, responsible for the design and continuous innovation of our rapidly expanding data center foot print.

Engineers at Amazon work to design resilient, cost effective electrical distribution systems. As engineers at Amazon we are responsible for achieving a world class uptime for our customers. We justify and communicate the technical decisions we make to Sr. Management and work hard to drive continuous advancements and improvements with our designs. As an engineer at Amazon you have the ability to drive change and define/design the systems our customers rely on.

Amazon offers a fast paced, fun, and exciting work environment. We continue to grow at exponential rates and are looking for individuals that can support our speed to market, enjoy a challenge, and have a desire for professional growth and continuous learning experiences. Amazon’s work environment is unique in every aspect and offers an exceptional opportunity for the right candidate.

If you are a creative, smart and driven individual that enjoys working with complex problems we want YOU! At Amazon you will be responsible for working on multi-million dollar designs that support our array of businesses and wide variety of customers. Great ideas are encouraged and supported. Ingenuity is the main mechanism which supports our focus on quality, speed, and cost.

We are looking for engineers with hands on electrical design experience. If you can design an electrical system, have an understanding of the critical equipment needs for a data center, and understand the constructability of varying designs you may be a good fit. As we grow we are structuring our team to own more of our engineering in house. Engineers will be responsible for taking designs from concept to the permit and construction document set. You must be capable of defining critical equipment specifications and approving equipment submittals. Engineers will directly support construction and be a part of the process from site selection review through commissioning and ultimately turnover. You will be relied on as a subject matter expert in the electrical engineering field. At Amazon we highly support continued learning opportunities and focus on continued employee development.

At Amazon team work is absolutely necessary for us to accomplish our goals. You must be able to work within a team and depend on others to accomplish the required work. As an electrical engineer at Amazon you will be working with other internal groups as well as external groups including utilities, manufacturers, vendors, and contractors.

Amazon has a global presence. Travel should be up to 20% of your time and in-person collaboration efforts in your assigned office location.


Key job responsibilities
- Data center electrical designs and collaboration with other disciplines to create a construction document set.
- Creation of designs which meet or exceed our quality requirements and fall within our budgetary requirements.
- Work with local agencies having jurisdiction to ensure compliance with federal, state and municipal requirements and building codes.
- Review and approval of equipment submittals.
- Define project scope and provide technical support for information requests prior to, and during construction phases.
- Work with commissioning teams to properly test and validate installation, operation, and performance of electrical systems.
- Ability to work on concurrent projects in multiple geographical regions.
- Travel to sites for site review and work with onsite field engineers, as well as provide engineering evaluations, electrical systems audits, and startup as needed.
- Having fun and offering creative, out of the box solutions.

A day in the life
You'll start your day connecting with global team members to review ongoing projects. You might analyze energy efficiency data, collaborate on innovative cooling solutions, or mentor fellow engineers. You'll participate in design reviews, engage with vendors, and contribute to sustainability initiatives that shape our environmental footprint.

title: Industrial Maintenance Mechanic
location: Monahans, Texas, United States, Kermit, TX, United States
description:
Headquartered in Austin, TX with operations in Kermit and Monahans, TX, Atlas Sand is the leading provider of frac sand to the Permian Basin. We are proud of what we do – we have state of the art manufacturing facilities, high quality products, outstanding customer service, and exceptional work culture and a commitment to giving back to the community. Atlas was established in 2017 by a team of career oil & gas operators led by Bud Brigham. Since then, we’ve added top industrial sand mining talent and have navigated, grown and innovated our way through the recent ups and downs in the commodity markets. We’re very excited about what we see in front of us, and we think you will be too – so come join the team! 
The Industrial Maintenance Mechanic provides technical support for the safe and efficient operation of terminal and logistics equipment with limited supervision. Duties include but are not limited to maintenance and repair of equipment such as bucket elevators, conveyors, pumps, and control devices. Troubleshoots issues, repairs failures of production and facilities equipment and ensures maximum efficiency and effectiveness of operations. Understands process flow and evaluates ways to increase operating efficiency.
Responsibilities:

Gathers technical information to perform the job
Performs equipment walk around and inspects and adjusts equipment; properly disposes of wastes
Performs equipment repairs, changes out parts, checks the status of equipment availability with site supervisors, and follows procedures to pick up parts and supplies from the warehouse
Responsible for all tasks related to predictive and preventative maintenance programs. Tasks include but are not limited to: repair and maintenance of all machinery and equipment such as bucket elevators, conveyors, compressors, and pumps; repair or replacement of control devices such as switches, photo eyes, proximity sensors, pushbuttons, contactors, motor starters, as needed
Performs work order repairs
Performs light welding and cutting to patch holes in chutes and reduce spillage throughout the system
Coordinates and plans down time efficiently to maximize uptime of production
Understands all equipment in depth from electric motors, gearboxes, conveyors, hydraulics, load out chutes, gas and diesel engines, vehicle and machine repairs, with the ability to trouble shoot, analyze, and make quick responsive repairs without guidance
Able to set up operator welders, drill press, grinder, hand tools and other metal working equipment.

PHYSICAL DEMANDS: 

Ability to work in adverse conditions
Required to stand, walk, stoop, kneel, crouch or crawl
Must regularly lift and/or move 75-100 pounds frequently
Ability to work at elevated heights without fear
Open and willing to learn operations of a manlift and a forklift
Have strong VERBAL communication skills
Capable of working a rotating shift, 14 on 7 off rotating between days and nights

Qualifications:

High School Diploma or GED required
Sufficient education to make appropriate arithmetic equations and complete written documentation and records; or an equivalent combination of experience, education and training that provides the desired knowledge, skills and characteristics
Must be able to read and interpret drawings, follow routers, use simple math, and use basic hand held measuring tools
Minimum Three (3) years' experience with hydraulics, pneumatics, mechanics and basic electrical repair
Must have experience in maintaining and repairing processing equipment and heavy equipment
Strong electronics experience with controls and drives
Basic computer skills required to use maintenance software to track and log maintenance costs
Proficiency with Microsoft word and Excel are required
Courses and/or logged hours in the industrial maintenance field are recommended
Knowledge in equipment reliability and preventative maintenance preferred
Prior training and certification in the following areas highly desirable: welding certification, vibration analysis, electrical/mechanical, bearing training, conveyor systems, pumps, fans, screening equipment, and vibrating conveying systems

What You’ll Love About Us

Your Well-Being is a 100% covered Medical, Dental, and Vision
Invest in Your 401K with company match, immediate vesting

title: Field Archaeologist - Temporary Project Based
description:
Your future begins here! BGE, Inc. is a nationwide civil engineering consulting firm offering diverse career opportunities in a wide range of disciplines for public and private infrastructure projects. Our employees enjoy a comprehensive benefits package that includes outstanding health care, generous 401(k) match, professional career resources, and highly competitive work-life balance programs, including personal-time allowances, dependent care, and flexible Fridays.
In addition, BGE provides unlimited sick leave, floating holidays, and robust career growth guidance, including organization-wide leadership and mentorship programs to help you build connections and shape your career. BGE goes beyond competitive benefits to attract and retain the best in an environment that inspires excellence.
 
 Field Archaeologist - Temporary Project Based
 
Location: Frico, Tx (2595 Dallas Pkwy #101, Frisco, TX 75034)
 
-Temporary position (no benefits offered): you may work 40 hours + some weeks and 0 another week-
 
Job Responsibilities

Conduct phase one archaeological surveys including pedestrian surveys and shovel testing to identify presence or absence of cultural resources.
Assist with excavation and trenching activities as needed, primarily in Texas and surrounding regions
Collect and document field data using tablets, GPS devices, and maintain detailed photo logs.
Support preparation of reports, background research, and site documentation for archaeological projects.
Collaborate with project leads and team members to ensure accurate data collection and compliance with regulatory requirements.
Participate in fieldwork under the guidance of experienced crew chiefs, with opportunities for mentorship and skill development.
Communicate findings and technical information clearly to project managers and team members.
Adhere to safety protocols and carry out fieldwork in various weather conditions, often requiring travel within Texas and to other states.

 
Job Requirements

Career focus on cultural resources fieldwork, archaeological investigations or related industry.
Bachelor’s degree in anthropology or archaeology upperclassmen nearing graduation with relevant field school experience will also be considered.
Solid organizational skills and proficiency in technical data entry and report documentation.
Effective time-management, written communication, analytical, and interpersonal skills.
Professional presence with the ability to make sound decisions in field and office settings.
Ability to work effectively in team environments and establish strong working relationships across project teams.
Proficient with Microsoft Office Suite and comfortable using tablets and GPS technology for field data collection; GIS experience is a plus.
Ability to navigate through rugged terrain using a compass
Knowledge of archaeological field methods such as pedestrian survey, shovel testing, and trenching preferred.
Ability to appropriately identify and document archaeological sites
Willingness to travel within Texas and to other project sites in Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Kansas.
Ability to record field data accurately with minimal assistance from other employees and manage time effectively;
Ability to travel and perform daily strenuous fieldwork for extended periods (crews typically work 10-hour days during field efforts, except for travel days);
Ability to conduct fieldwork in various weather conditions (including cold, extreme heat, humidity, light rain or snow)
Ability to navigate rugged terrain and perform shovel tests at set intervals up to 10 miles per day while carrying field equipment weighing up to 40 lbs
Ability to conduct a minimum of 10-15 shovel tests per day, in rugged conditions
Ability to maintain a positive attitude
CPR, First Aid, and Wilderness First Aid certifications are preferred
A valid driver’s license and access to reliable transportation are required
Ability to safely drive and appropriately maintain a work vehicle is required
Passing a drug screening test and driver record check is mandatory upon acceptance of an offer.

 
****Benefits Do not apply to this role as it is a Temp role*****
 Some of our Benefits:

401k Match: 100% up to 4% of your contributions with immediate vesting + 3% Safe Harbor Contribution with immediate vesting
Merit-Based Bonus Compensation
Medical, Dental, Vision Insurance; BGE contributes to HSA on eligible plans
9 paid Holidays, including 3 Floating holidays
Personal Time Allowances 
2 to 4 weeks of Vacation, depending on experience-level. Unused vacation carries over to the next year.
"Unlimited" Sick Days.
Mentorship Program – Provides you with the opportunity to learn and receive guidance from seasoned professionals.
Employee Referral Program that pays you for bringing great people into the BGE family

BGE is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity. We prohibit discrimination and all employment is decided on the basis of qualifications, merit, and business need. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, Vietnam Era Veteran Status, Disabled Veteran Status, or any other classification protected by federal, state or local laws.
